502986|2026-06.headline: Vardhman Q1 FY27 margins rose on spinning yarn-size gains and raw-material trading gains; fabric utilisation remains weak as US orders slipped.
502986|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 numbers improved in both percentage and absolute terms, driven mainly by the spinning business through better yarn sizes and a partial trading gain on raw material bought before the cotton price rise. The fabric business lagged: absolute volumes were roughly flat YoY and 3-4% below Q4 FY26, because US orders were lost after a missed sampling season tied to US tariffs. Management expects the spinning margin to moderate as cheap inventory runs out, but sees a 13-14% margin as a reasonable direction. Capex is mostly complete, with biomass boilers starting and the Dhar (PM MITRA) site dependent on land and power by around December 2026 and June 2027.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Utilisation full, margins good and demand strong; gains came from yarn-size mix and partial raw-material trading gains. Yarn export rose to about 110 million kg/month from 95-100 million kg, mostly from China (about 7-8% of production).

segments.name: Fabric (cotton and synthetic)
segments.commentary: Weak utilisation after losing US season orders; management says prices pass-through on yarn is only 60-70%, leaving 20-30% unrecovered. New synthetic fabric line has 15 lakh meters/month capacity at 15-20% utilisation, with two brand approvals and production starting in August 2026.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 7,000 shirts/day; plan to double to 4.5 million (units as stated) with peak revenue of about INR300 crore at full utilisation, targeted around Q1 FY28 (about one year from now). Mix is about 30% export and 70% domestic brands.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to show the benefit of higher yarn prices realised in April-May 2026, given the 3-month export and 45-day domestic order cover.
Management expects spinning margins to moderate after Q2 as low-cost cotton inventory is consumed, but not to fall back to the 2-3 year trough.
Management sees sales visibility for at least 3-4 months, but margins depend on when old cotton runs out and new cotton is consumed.
Management views 13-14% as a reasonable margin direction, equal to about USD0.80-0.90 per kg of yarn conversion.
Biomass boiler at Baddi started last week; second boiler in Madhya Pradesh expected in about a month; power projects to complete in about 3 months.
Remaining capex of about INR800-900 crore to flow into FY28; most of the INR3,600 crore plan is complete or due within FY27.
Dhar site: land expected by December 2026; power not before June 2027; project implementation of 10-12 months once started.
capex_capacity: Open-end spinning project of about 55-60 tonnes/day started construction last week; expected in about 10 months.
Biomass boiler at Baddi started last week; second in Madhya Pradesh expected in about a month.
Synthetic fabric capacity at 15 lakh meters/month, utilisation 15-20%, target 70-80% within 6 months.

Dhar PM MITRA site: construction to start only once land and power are confirmed; not included in the announced INR3,600 crore capex.
demand_pricing: Cotton: management expects prices to firm as global supply falls 2-3% a year and demand rises, creating a 3-4% supply gap for 1-2 years; New York futures rose from about USD0.67-0.68 to about USD0.80/lb.
Indian cotton (CCI) rose from about INR55,000 to about INR64,000 per candy, now aligned with international prices; MSP up 6-7% implies cotton not below INR65,000-66,000 next season.
Yarn: China and Bangladesh take about 60% of Indian yarn exports; China accounts for about 30% of the export pool. Chinese reserve cotton sold at about USD1.15-1.16/lb.
Spinning capacity: 12-13 million spindles closed in India over three years; only about 0.7-0.8 million spindles of expansion announced this year.
Fabric pricing: customers want 20-45 day lead times; management says organised players gain share as brands prefer single-vendor sourcing.
Export share of garments about 30%; domestic brands about 70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spinning order book and does the price rise show up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders cover about 90-95 days and domestic about 45-50 days historically, with the same cover today. Management confirmed the April-May price gains should show in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will moderate as cheap inventory runs out, though not to the 2-3 year trough; trading margins may not persist at market cotton prices unless yarn rises further.

qa_highlights.question: Garment expansion economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Doubling capacity to 4.5 million (stated) could reach about INR300 crore revenue at 100%, with full operations about one year away due to worker training; the aim is stand-alone viability.

qa_highlights.question: Dhar capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhar capex is not included in the INR3,600 crore plan. Construction starts only once land is given (expected December 2026) and power is assured (not before June 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Cotton yarn spread and where margins settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spot spread was about USD0.90/kg. Management said historical range is USD0.85-1.00, with 13-14% margins reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Will China keep buying Indian yarn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Chinese yarn imports to continue because of high Chinese cotton prices (over USD1 per lb) and Xinjiang-cotton risk, though this is not confirmed beyond current months.

risks_watch: Cotton supply: El Nino-related rain variation, Brazil area down about 5%, and possible quality issues; management will watch crop estimates for 2-4 weeks.
Fabric utilisation and US order recovery, which management expects to improve over the next 2-3 months.
Unrecovered yarn cost: only 60-70% of yarn price rises passed on to fabric customers.
Cotton import window: duty-free import window only for the next 2-3 months; decisions taken daily.
Dhar land and power timelines (December 2026 and June 2027) and the garment plant ramp-up (about one year).

503100|2026-03.headline: Phoenix Mills FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% to Rs 4,423 crore and EBITDA 22% to Rs 2,637 crore, with no new retail capacity added.
503100|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong broad-based growth: consolidated revenue Rs 4,423 crore (+16%), EBITDA Rs 2,637 crore (+22%), and PAT Rs 1,557 crore (+20%), achieved without adding retail area. Retail consumption hit a record Rs 16,587 crore (+21%), with Q4 up 31%, though retail rentals grew only 10% to Rs 2,157 crore, which management attributes to the MG-plus-revenue-share lease structure and ramp-up of newer malls. Offices expanded to 4.8 million sq ft with occupancy at 70%, and management expects a meaningful step-up in office income from FY27. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.19x despite the ISMDPL (CPP stake) buyout and peak construction capex.

segments.commentary: Rental income Rs 2,157 crore (+10%) and EBITDA Rs 2,246 crore (+12%); consumption Rs 16,587 crore (+21%), Q4 consumption +31%. Phoenix Palladium rent Rs 461 crore (+14%).

segments.commentary: Operational Mumbai and Pune office income Rs 213 crore with EBITDA about Rs 141 crore; portfolio 4.8 million sq ft, occupancy 70%, gross leasing over 2.2 million sq ft in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 consumption growth excluding jewellery and electronics, and how will the rent-consumption gap move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-jewellery and electronics, Q4 consumption growth was about 17-18%. Management expects the gap to narrow as revenue share kicks in, and says rental growth should hold even if jewellery and electronics moderate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PMC Pune and Bangalore consumption gains reflect in rentals, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9% of area in both malls is leased but not yet trading, so rental upside lands in FY27; Pune is seen at 14-15% rental upside and Bangalore about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What rental upside is expected from the roughly 50% of portfolio area expiring in the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for rental uplift similar to FY26's roughly 20% blended new and renewal growth, supported by brand repositioning and F&B concepts like Gourmet Village; market conditions must remain supportive.

qa_highlights.question: When will office rental income start and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue from newer office assets expected from Q2 FY27, growing quarter on quarter, with quarterly office income seen doubling by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumption trend in April 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: April is very strong, with close to 30% growth including Akshay Tritiya; excluding jewellery and electronics, growth would be about 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the land strategy beyond 2030 and for new cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Scouting Hyderabad, Jaipur and Navi Mumbai; one or two new-city transactions targeted in FY27, plus conversion of existing assets such as Palladium and PMC Bangalore into super campuses.

503100|2026-06.headline: Phoenix Mills Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA 14% to Rs 642 crore, with retail consumption up 32%.
503100|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA grew 14% to Rs 642 crore at a 60% margin, with net profit up 23% to Rs 297 crore. Core annuity revenue rose 17% to Rs 1,033 crore and core EBITDA rose 19% to Rs 649 crore. Retail consumption grew 32% to Rs 4,730 crore, though jewelry and electronics drove much of that growth; ex-jewelry and electronics consumption grew 24% while rental grew 17%. Capex was Rs 1,085 crore, including Rs 716 crore paid to GAMADA for Chandigarh land, and net debt stood at Rs 3,658 crore (1.3x net debt/EBITDA).

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 8.7 million sq ft expiry is anchors and what is the mark-to-market upside?

rows.why: Core EBITDA up 19% vs core revenue up 17% and consolidated EBITDA margin at 60%, but the rent-to-consumption ratio is compressing and new openings add cost before rent ramps (malls take ~12 months to reach 85-90% occupancy).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2 (170,000 sq ft F&B floor) due early 2027, Palladium expansion (~4.5 lakh sq ft) in FY27/FY28, and Surat (~1 million sq ft) by end-2027 or early 2028; Pune and Bengaluru assets already at 89% trading occupancy, so pressure to add space is building, though most new capacity lands 2-4 quarters out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail consumption +32% to Rs 4,730 crore, leasing of ~1 million sq ft across 300-plus transactions in Q1, and about 390 new stores in last 12 months; malls leased at 97-98%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 89% in Pune and Bengaluru, Q1 capex of Rs 1,085 crore (Rs 716 crore to GAMADA for Chandigarh land) and Lower Parel Project Rise pre-leasing at Rs 350-400 per sq ft, with development plans for extra FSI to be shared after Rise Retail opens.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: July consumption trending above 20% and non-gold consumption +24% vs rental +17%, but management held mid-teens rental growth for FY27 and FY28 and gave no upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumption heavily reliant on jewelry and electronics (28% of consumption, ~7.5% of rental) and gold prices, and September is the weakest month; rent-to-consumption has fallen from ~14% to ~12.5%, near the bottom of the 12-14% range.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bengaluru residential launch and Kolkata residential (~1.2 million sq ft at ~Rs 30,000 per sq ft) by end-2026 or early 2027, plus Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2 F&B floor early 2027; management says timelines are indicative and approvals/RERA gated.

rows.label: Grand Victoria Kolkata and Grand Hyatt Whitefield
rows.why: Kolkata mall (~1 million sq ft) is planned and Whitefield offices (~0.4 million sq ft) with a 400-key Grand Hyatt have Phase-3 approvals secured with civil work to start shortly.

rows.label: Office occupancy convergence
rows.why: Rent-paying occupancy at 42% vs 72% leased, targeted to converge by March 2027, and leased occupancy at Asia Towers and One National Park targeted at 90% by end FY27 (from 72% overall).

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA at 1.3x despite capex
rows.why: Net debt Rs 3,658 crore at 1.3x net debt/EBITDA after Rs 1,085 crore Q1 capex, with operating FCF Rs 602 crore (+20%) funding part of the spend; further land and construction payouts could lift leverage.

tone.note: Management was confident on consumption momentum (July above 20%), leasing and mid-teens rental guidance, but cautious on opening timelines (Surat, Kolkata, Lower Parel) and gold-linked consumption; analysts pressed on the rent-to-consumption gap, the 8.7 million sq ft expiry and anchor mark-to-mark

503101|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated PAT of INR 206 crores, the company's highest ever, alongside INR 900 crores QIP and INR 576 crores FY26 presales (MNRL share).
503101|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as transformational, citing record PAT of INR 206 crores on total income of INR 639 crores and EBITDA of INR 261 crores. The INR 900 crore QIP was used for about INR 340 crores of debt repayment, roughly a third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores earmarked for new acquisitions, of which only about INR 54 crores (call also cited ~INR 50 crores) was deployed. The company acquired controlling interests in three Kanjurmarg entities (~INR 70 crores investment) with a six-project pipeline of over INR 840 crores GDV, and took a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Pvt Ltd. The amalgamation has received no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE and documents have been filed with NCLT, with hearing awaited.

segments.name: Marathon Futurex (Lower Parel, commercial)
segments.commentary: Presales rose 15% YoY to INR 466 crores on leasing and absorption; management says prices firmed about 15% YoY and rates rose 50-60% over five to six years. Inventory may take 12-15 months to exhaust.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, luxury residential, 40% revenue share)
segments.commentary: Presales of INR 391 crores in FY26. Tower B has OC up to the 45th floor, with the 45th-65th floors topped out and expected complete by December 2026. Tower C is built to 17 floors; Tower D is unlaunched; a commercial Tower 5 may launch in 12-18 months.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Presales of INR 104 crores. Phase 3 launched with about 4.9 lakh sq ft carpet area and INR 600 crores GDV. Phase 2 towers Antilia, Triton and Atria received full OC.

segments.name: Neo series (Bhandup)
segments.commentary: NeoValley, NeoPark, NeoSquare and Bhandup projects together recorded about INR 65 crores presales; NeoSquare received OC. Newly launched Neohome has INR 370 crores GDV.

segments.name: Mulund Millennium (commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 21 crores presales in FY26 from small offices and retail spaces.

segments.name: Kanjurmarg (acquired, PTC/B2B model)
segments.commentary: Six residential projects with GDV over INR 840 crores; one project at 5th slab of a 23-storey building; about INR 225 crores+ of GDV to launch within 12 months. Company holds 50% controlling interest and one-third economic interest in the transit camp model.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margins of 30-40% on the Kanjurmarg projects, in line with current company margins.
Remaining INR 250 crores-odd of the INR 300 crore new-project allocation is yet to be spent on acquisitions.
Monte South Tower B floors 45-65 expected to complete by December 2026, adding to revenue recognition.
Post-merger, around 418 acres of land is expected to come into the listed entity; management cited Panvel plotted development possibly launching in FY27 or FY28.
Bonus issue timing is uncertain; management said it may or may not happen after amalgamation.
Strategic focus for FY27: accelerate execution, expand presales, pursue redevelopment and acquisitions, scale PTC-led B2B vertical, maintain prudent capital allocation.
capex_capacity: Unsold value of the listed entity (MNRL share) around INR 6,500 crores, plus the INR 840 crores Kanjurmarg pipeline; the company said this covers about five years of inventory.
Unsold launched inventory is about INR 2,000 crores, with cost to complete about INR 1,600 crores.
Management's thumb rule: unsold/unlaunched projects need about 60% of cost still to be spent.
Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion basis; completion percentages are shown in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management says Grade A office demand in South and Central Mumbai is strong; supply is lower than before, and Futurex prices firmed about 15% YoY.
Futurex serves more than 300 institutional and leasing clients, including Nykaa, ZEE, L'Oreal, SBI and HDFC; leasing ticket sizes start from 1,500-2,000 sq ft.
Luxury segment inventory at premium addresses is said to be tight, supporting pricing at Monte South.
Infrastructure tailwinds cited: Navi Mumbai airport, Atal Setu, Panvel-Karjat rail, EduCity, Kharghar commercial complex, GMLR (Goregaon-Mulund Link Road) and Dombivli bullet train station.
BMC cleared 384 unauthorised structures in Mulund, Amar Nagar and Khindipada for the eastern GMLR section (about 12 km).

qa_highlights.question: Launch timelines, capital deployment and margins for the Kanjurmarg projects?
qa_highlights.answer: GDV is over INR 840 crores and could go higher depending on PTC or pre-sale model. About 10% is ongoing; more than INR 225 crores will launch within 12 months. Expected EBITDA margins are 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: No-adverse-observation letters received from BSE and NSE; all documents filed with NCLT. Company awaits the hearing; stakeholder meetings to be dispensed with given NOCs.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 900 crore QIP be allocated?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 340 crores repaid as debt, about one-third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores for new acquisitions. More than 30 projects evaluated; about three shortlisted; two acquired (Sunset Spaces and Kanjurmarg).

qa_highlights.question: Will commercial share of the portfolio increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to balance the portfolio by adding a new commercial project as each is sold; Monte South Tower 5 is a future commercial project.

qa_highlights.question: Remaining balance-sheet and unsold inventory question for Monte South and the 50% share?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on percentage of completion; sold area's revenue is recognised per completion, and unsold value is yet to be recognised. Tower A delivered, Tower B has OC to 45th floor, Tower C launched with 17 floors built, Tower D unlaunched.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a bonus issue after amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot commit; policy has been bonus after a few years, and currently 97% of capital is bonus capital.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for premium office assets in South and Central Mumbai?
qa_highlights.answer: Samyag Shah said demand is very strong, supported by both institutional sales and leasing; Futurex inventory could last 12-15 months and a new commercial portfolio is planned.

risks_watch: Kanjurmarg pipeline (GDV INR 840 crores+) is not yet launched beyond the ongoing project; launch timing relies on the next 12 months.
Amalgamation depends on NCLT approval; timing of hearing not specified.
About INR 250 crores of the INR 300 crore acquisition allocation remains unspent.

Collections in Q4 (INR 203 crores) were well below booking value (INR 156 crores) only in the sense of lower bookings; FY26 collections of INR 781 crores vs INR 576 crores presales should be tracked for sustainability.
Cost-to-complete of about INR 1,600 crores on launched inventory will need funding from the balance sheet.
Monte South Tower B completion and Tower D launch timing are key delivery milestones.

503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, JV, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Sold ~35,000 sq ft with booking value INR 125 crores and collections INR 140 crores. Tower A has OC; Tower B has RCC to 65th floor and part OC to 45th floor, with balance OC expected this FY; Tower C RCC at 28th floor.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Sold 14,000 sq ft with booking value INR 17 crores and collections INR 43 crores. Full OC received for Cedar and Daffodil towers, enabling handovers.

segments.name: Bhandup (NeoPark, NeoSquare)
segments.commentary: Sales of 8,000 sq ft with booking value INR 14 crores and collections INR 9 crores. NeoSquare has OC; NeoValley and NeoPark under construction per schedule.

segments.name: Commercial (Futurex and Millennium)
segments.commentary: Futurex combined sales ~4,000 sq ft, booking INR 19 crores, collections INR 23 crores; Futurex has OC. Millennium sold over 1,000 sq ft, booking INR 3 crores, collections INR 1 crore; under construction.

segments.name: PTC (Permanent Transit Camp) vertical
segments.commentary: Started after Kanjurmarg land acquisition in Q4 FY26, focused on Bhandup; no presales yet, but management expects some in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 outlook is positive and better than last year, but declined to give forward numbers; bookings from newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases expected to show in coming quarters (booking recognised on registration).
Collections this year expected to be on the heavier side, supported by ready-to-move inventory (about 3-month TAT on sales at Futurex and Monte South) and percentage-completion receipts.
Surplus capital of about INR 200 crores expected to be fully deployed into new projects this FY27.
Target EBITDA margin of 30-35% for project acquisitions.

Merger: shareholder and creditor meetings planned for first week of September 2026, followed by a second NCLT hearing; completion timing uncertain, dependent on NCLT dates (management said it was not sure whether it would complete by December).
capex_capacity: Upcoming pipeline GDV: Monte South Commercial ~INR 3,400 crores; Monte South Residential Tower D ~INR 1,600 crores; Marathon Neo Series (Bhandup) ~INR 2,800 crores.

Redevelopment additions: Versova (via subsidiary Sunset Spaces, ~1.5 acres, GDV >INR 450 crores, first society redevelopment) and Sewri (cluster redevelopment JDA, ~7,500 sq m, GDV ~INR 450 crores).
Merger to bring over 400 acres of land, several ongoing projects and ready inventory at Futurex into the listed entity.
Panvel-Karjat corridor deadline cited as December 2026; Monte South commercial to launch ~5 minutes from Futurex.
demand_pricing: Management cited strong demand at Monte South (footfalls up sharply), commercial space (limited Grade A supply near Futurex), and newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases.
Ready-to-move inventory at Monte South Towers A and B is sold at a premium, per management.
Redevelopment selection: prime locations and strict financial metrics; management said it avoids high-premium deals that may get stuck.
PTC demand from neighbouring redevelopment projects in Bhandup; area serves western suburbs (around Malad, P-South ward), Mulund, Ghatkopar and parts of Chembur.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch timelines for the INR 900 crore redevelopment GDV, and how much more can be added in 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two new projects (Sewri and Versova, INR 450 crores each) add INR 900 crores in the quarter; no launch timeline or further 12-24 month addition was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 business outlook and which projects will drive acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers but said the outlook is positive and better than last year, citing Monte South, commercial, and new Bhandup and Panvel phases, with bookings flowing in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ready-to-move sales at Futurex and Monte South convert to collections in about 3 months; Monte South Tower C is at the 28th slab, with about 40% collection on that basis. Collections expected to be heavier this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A Futurex investment-property floor was not sold in the quarter, so no rental/sale income was recognised from it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the amalgamation complete by December 2026 or slip into 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder and stakeholder meetings are planned for early September, followed by a second NCLT hearing; management said it is not sure of the timeline because NCLT benches are heavily loaded.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the redevelopment pipeline beyond INR 900 crores, and how are deals selected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Mumbai redevelopment opportunity is very large; selection focuses on prime locations and strict margin thresholds, and it avoids over-priced deals that can stall.

qa_highlights.question: How much capital will be deployed in FY27 and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Target EBITDA margin 30-35% on acquisitions; about INR 200 crores of surplus capital to be fully deployed this FY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PTC vertical's pipeline and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC business started after the Q4 FY26 Kanjurmarg land acquisition; strong demand from neighbouring redevelopments; presales may start in next few quarters.

503722|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose to a record Rs1,370 crore-scale year with EBITDA up 22.5% to Rs144 crore; FY27 guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore.
503722|2026-03.overview: Banswara Syntex reported Q4 FY26 total income of Rs369.3 crore, with EBITDA up 46% YoY to Rs46 crore and PAT of Rs9.6 crore (up 87% YoY). For FY26, EBITDA was about Rs144 crore (margin near 11%) and PAT Rs28.4 crore (up 32.8%) after a one-time Rs9 crore labour code exceptional charge. Fabric and Garment grew, while Yarn volumes and revenue fell on labour shortages in spinning. Management guided to FY27 revenue of Rs1,450-1,500 crore and EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% over the medium term, with near-term margin pressure from raw material pass-through lag.

financial_highlights.value: Rs28.4 crore (after Rs9 crore one-time labour code expense)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs456 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.value: 20% on face value, total Rs3.42 crore

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs113 crore (vs Rs123 crore; management corrected the gap to Rs10 crore), FY26 Rs449 crore vs Rs460 crore (about -2%). Volume 46 lakh kg in Q4 and 194 lakh kg in FY26; utilisation 78% in Q4 and 77% for FY26. Realisations up about Rs30-35/kg.

segments.name: Fabrics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs154 crore (vs Rs145 crore); FY26 record Rs569 crore, up 5%. Volume 62 lakh meters in Q4 and 230 lakh meters in FY26; utilisation 77% in Q4. Middle East exports affected.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs96 crore, up 40%; FY26 Rs324 crore, up 18%. Volume 11 lakh pieces in Q4 and 39 lakh pieces in FY26; FY26 utilisation 72% vs about 50% in FY25. Walmart added about Rs15 crore of Q4 revenue.

segments.name: Associate Tesca Textiles (40% stake)
segments.commentary: Management said Tesca had turnover of about Rs100 crore and PAT of about Rs10 crore, with Banswara's share about Rs4 crore. No plan to raise stake.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore, led by Fabric and Garment; FY26 was about Rs1,370 crore.
Management targets about 20% revenue growth in both Fabric and Garment in FY27; Garment division projects 18-20%.
EBITDA margin expected at 10.5-11% over the medium term; near-term margins may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
FY27 capex planned at Rs135-140 crore (an analyst cited Rs130-150 crore); Garment capex only Rs3-5 crore.
Long-term debt expected to rise in FY27 on planned capex and reduce from FY28 onwards; no reduction in total borrowings this year.
Management expects H2 FY27 growth to exceed H1; Garment momentum to improve from Q2 after a subdued Q1.
capex_capacity: Yarn and Fabric capacity was reshaped toward finer counts, Siro Compact yarn (about 200 tons per month) and worsted finishing machines; management says installed capacity fell YoY partly due to mix shift.
Garment capacity: about 70,000 pieces per month available vs 40,000-50,000 jackets used; could go to 80,000 with long runs.
Surat SEZ garment capacity (about 40,000-50,000 jackets and about 100,000 pants) awaits approval; timeline not given, file under process with Industries Commissionerate and Kandla SEZ.
Management said Garment expansion could start mid-year (Q2/Q3 FY27) and that Rs2,000 crore revenue is possible without significant capex, with no firm timeline.
Capex items: zero water discharge project, a 132 KVA power line application, and other infrastructure and sustainability spend.
demand_pricing: Polyester raw material costs up about 25% due to the Middle East conflict; yarn prices raised but not fully passed on.
Wool prices rose sharply, from Australia and China; management says customers take 6 months to 1 year to accept new prices.
Rupee depreciation of about 6-7% helped export realisations without price increases.
Walmart added as a Garment customer; JC Penney (Fabric) and Mango (Garment) already customers; Celio and Marks & Spencer cited as large relationships.
Middle East exposure about Rs100 crore; Rs8-9 crore of Q4 product could not ship on time; management expects Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region in FY27.
US demand improving; company says it is more competitive than China in spun-synthetic segment.
D2C brand One Mile averages about Rs15 lakh per month; fundraising planned once it reaches about Rs1 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Have new export clients been added, such as Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Walmart is a new addition; it contributed about Rs15 crore of Q4 Garment revenue. Management aims for 20% growth in Garment and Fabric next year and sees no need for many more large clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why did installed capacity fall YoY despite investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Finer counts and worsted machines lower kg output; capacity is planned around realistic labour availability. Management says labour shortages persist into May.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour shortage transient or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says automation is not viable given many SKUs; focus is on scaling winning products and shifting from made-to-order to predictive analytics planning.

qa_highlights.question: How will the borrowings be reduced?

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail revenue outlook and what would trigger faster store expansion?

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation expected to affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some pass-on was taken in Q1 with more possible if margins compress, and it reiterated the ~14% EBITDA margin guidance including the retail drag.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said other income is mostly recurring (delayed payment interest, rent); management said about 30% is a mark-to-market gain that varies quarter to quarter.

Raw material and chemical cost volatility, with pass-through to customers only partial.

504028|2026-03.headline: GEE Q4 FY26 turnover rose to INR112 crore and FY26 to about INR370 crore, with EBITDA margin near 9% and a 25-30% revenue CAGR target to FY29.
504028|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 turnover of about INR112 crore (up from INR79 crore in Q1 FY26), taking FY26 to roughly INR370 crore versus INR334 crore in FY25. Q4 EBITDA was about INR33 crore at a 9% margin, and PAT about INR13 crore (3.5% margin). Management framed FY26 as a stabilisation year after the May 2025 promoter restructuring, and set targets of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29-30, FY27 revenue above INR500 crore and EBITDA margin above 10%. Growth is tied to defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways and exports, with flux-cored wire production slated to start in July 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR79 crore in Q1 FY26 (sequential)
management says FY25 margins were stabilised and exceeded in the last couple of years

financial_highlights.value: under 10% of revenue; around INR350-plus crore of INR370 crore is domestic
financial_highlights.change: down from a higher share in earlier years

segments.name: Specialised/defence products
segments.commentary: Management says GEE holds 70-80% share in defence welding consumables (Griduct 100, GEEFLUX 521); specialised applications business was about INR25 crore per an analyst's figure, which management did not confirm. FY26 defence business was INR10-12 crore, planned to more than double in FY27.

segments.name: Flux-cored wires
segments.commentary: Import-driven business of INR25-30 crore a year; in-house production expected from July 2026 under new BIS rules, with management targeting more than INR50 crore revenue a year and adding lines over time. INR20-30 crore capex identified for flux-cored lines and ancillary machines.

segments.name: Distribution vs direct B2B
segments.commentary: Management gave conflicting splits: 70-80% via distributors and 15-20% to end customers in one answer, and about 25-30% direct B2B and 65-70% via distributors in another. Management said B2B share is rising from 20-25% toward 30-40%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share is under 10% of revenue, down from earlier years. Approvals were obtained from ADNOC (UAE) and a Saudi breakthrough, with NAKS approval from Russia in trial. Management targets export growth more than three times within two years, using TUV approval for stainless TIG wire for Europe.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target: 25-30% CAGR till FY29, reaching INR1,000 crore around FY29-30; FY27 revenue above INR500 crore.
EBITDA: FY27 EBITDA margin above 10%; Keshav Garg's annualised INR45 crore EBITDA for FY27 was confirmed by management, with Q1 seasonally weaker.
Longer term, management targets 13%+ sustained EBITDA margin, and a further INR1,000 crore via acquisitions over 5-6 years (INR2,000 crore total).
Management expects finance cost to fall in FY27 from solar installation and better working capital, and expects working capital and cash flow to improve.
Thane land development agreement (13,000+ sq m at Wagle Industrial Estate) expected to generate more than INR400 crore cash over five years.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 57%, targeted to rise to 80-90% through ancillary lines (drawing machines to feed extrusion machines); some machines already ordered.
Flux-cored wire production to start July 2026; machine dispatch in May 2026; capacity to be added in lines over time.
Submerged arc flux line with 30-35 metric tonne per day capacity recently started.
Capex of INR20-30 crore identified for ancillary machines and flux-cored wire lines, including shifting machines from the Thane plot to another facility.
Solar power installation in factories planned for this year or next to lower power cost and finance cost; management says growth to INR1,000 crore needs little capex.
demand_pricing: Management cites defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways (20,000+ bogie order expected), exports and shipbuilding as growth drivers; NPCIL approval received about two weeks before the call.
Inconel electrodes priced INR2,500-3,500 per kg, with a pending order above 20 tonnes; cobalt alloys INR3,500-5,500 per kg, with business above INR10 crore last year, targeted to double.
Pricing: management says GEE is 6-7% below ESAB and Ador in retail/distributor channels, but at par in project (tender) business.
Commodity inflation is passed to customers with about a one-month lag, per management.
Management says the Indian welding market is INR15,000-20,000 crore; GEE targets 10-15% share, and the organised share is 50-60% after GST.

qa_highlights.question: Which sectors will drive the 25-30% growth and what is the current sector-wise revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named power, railways, exports and defence as main drivers and declined to give a sector split, saying L&T and BHEL buy across all sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 EBITDA run-rate annualisable to about INR45 crore for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Payal Agarwal said yes, INR45 crore EBITDA is the target for FY27, with Q1 seasonally weaker due to monsoon and labour shortage.

qa_highlights.question: How many specialised-application volumes make up the roughly 36,000 tonnes volume and what is the realisation difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the figure and said it would revert with the exact numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D expense for the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number; it said R&D costs are moderate, with heavy lab equipment (e.g. an XRF machine from Germany) capitalised rather than expensed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 3x revenue growth square with 48-58% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come from ancillary lines to lift utilisation to 80-90%, new products such as flux-cored wires, and higher-value specialised products.

qa_highlights.question: What are the proceeds of the Thane land used for and will there be a distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a dividend is under consideration and proceeds would fund acquisitions of welding equipment and safety/maintenance product companies; one or two deals are targeted within a year.

Management gave inconsistent B2B vs distributor splits and did not provide R&D expense, specialised-product volume, or sector breakdown when asked.

Pricing gap vs ESAB and Ador in retail (6-7% lower), with competitive pressure in tender business.

504028|2026-06.headline: GEE Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR 103 crores, with EBITDA margin up 204 bps to 7.8%.
504028|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover grew 30% YoY to INR 103 crores from INR 79 crores, and EBITDA rose about 77% to INR 8 crores with margin at 7.8% versus 5.7%. PBT rose to INR 5.5 crores from INR 1 crore, and adjusted PAT rose to INR 3.2 crores from INR 1 crore. Management set a North Star of INR 1,000 crores revenue by FY29-30, with 10-13% EBITDA margin ambitions, supported by a NPCIL approval, new SAW wire, SAW flux and flux cored wire lines, and a Thane land monetisation. Management guided that Q1 and Q2 are seasonally weaker due to monsoons.

financial_highlights.change: +77% YoY from INR 4.5 crores (management cited INR 4 crores to INR 4.5 crores base)

segments.commentary: Niche products are around 27% to 30% of revenue; a BHEL Trichy order for P91 steel was received the day before the call.

segments.commentary: Commercial production started in Q1 FY27 per management; capacity not included in the 71,000 MT figure.

segments.commentary: Line of around 300 MT set up, planned to reach 1,000 MT by FY29; first line production expected by end-September or early October; 1,000 MT is said to yield more than INR 150 crores turnover.

EBITDA margin roadmap: 8% to 9% near term, then 10-11% and 12-13% sustainably; management said it is trying to reach 10% this year.

FY27 capex estimated at INR 5-10 crores; INR 30-40 crores total capex over three to four years.
No incremental working capital limits planned for the next year; working capital limit about INR 100 crores with headroom.
Nuclear expected to be at least 10% of business in coming years; shipbuilding (commercial) 3-5% of revenue.

Competition in exports cited as China and some Indian manufacturers; stainless steel cited as the product where India is competitive versus China due to raw material (wire rod) pricing.

NPCIL: GEE is one of three certified vendors with Ador and D&H Secheron; L&T, ISGEC, BHEL and NPCIL have inspected the plant; management expects about 7-8 potential vendors and has orders from 3-4 major players.
Management said consistent per-product margin differences exist but did not quantify niche vs commodity margin; it will provide an average chart next time.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the other NPCIL-empanelled partners and what bids are pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named D&H Secheron and Ador as the other certified players; L&T, ISGEC, BHEL and NPCIL have inspected the plant, with MEIL Hyderabad expected to inquire.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% growth and 10-11% EBITDA margin achievable this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the INR 1,000 crore target but 'not 100%' on margins, trying to reach 10% this year.

qa_highlights.question: Can electrode and wire capacity be interchanged, and what is the export opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacities are independent; electrodes have spare capacity, MIG wire is full. Export orders received from Vietnam, Saudi, Russia, and Middle East markets.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR 30-40 crore capex map to the 20,000 MT capacity and the INR 1,000 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified 12,000 MT wire addition needs far less than INR 30-40 crores; the INR 30-40 crore figure includes Thane shift, SAW and flux cored lines. Peak revenue from 71,000 MT is about INR 850 crores; SAW and flux cored lines bridge to INR 1,000 crores, with 1,000 MT flux cored yielding more than INR 150 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 revenue dip seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoons in Q1 and Q2 delay construction work; Q4 is always higher and work spills into the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and working capital need?
qa_highlights.answer: No term loan on books; only a working capital limit of about INR 100 crores with headroom; no further debt planned, funded by internal accruals and Thane land cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the promoter share pledged?
qa_highlights.answer: Pledge relates to promoter personal loans of INR 40 crores used for promoter settlement; management expects release over three to four years.

504132|2026-03.headline: Permanent Magnets Q4 standalone revenue rose 47% YoY to INR 66 crores; FY26 revenue INR 225 crores (+13%), with Relays ramp pushed to H2 FY27.
504132|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 66 crores, up 47% YoY, while FY26 revenue was INR 225 crores, up 13%. FY26 EBITDA margin was 17% versus 14% a year earlier, helped by product mix and second-half scale-up; Q4 margin was 15%, up YoY but down sequentially. The new Alloys furnace was installed in January and commercialised in Q4, while the Relays project slipped to commercial ramp from H2 FY27 and no rare-earth revenue was booked in FY26 due to Chinese export restrictions. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-30% with EBITDA margin of roughly 15-18%.

segments.commentary: New furnace installed January FY26, commercialised in Q4; utilisation about 80-90% from installation to year-end. Management expects FY27 volume roughly 3-4x FY26 levels. Q4 sales were mostly virgin-metal alloy, which carries slightly lower margin than scrap-based product.

segments.name: Relays (electricity meter relays)
segments.commentary: Commercial ramp delayed to H2 FY27 from earlier timelines; testing and customer approvals still in progress. Management estimates INR 25-50 crores of FY27 revenue at near-full utilisation of the initial 5 million unit capacity, with a possible step-up to 10 million units. Per-meter value cited at INR 250-300; TAM for 25 crore meter replacement put at INR 6,500-7,000 crores.

segments.commentary: Phase 1 (assembly) implemented. Phase 2 (block cutting, machining, surface treatment) due Q3-Q4 FY27, with commercial sales mainly from Q4 FY27. 504132|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 49% YoY to INR72.5 crore and EBITDA rose 159% to INR17.8 crore, led by EV demand.
504132|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR72.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 49% YoY, driven by higher EV-application supplies, mainly to export customers. EBITDA was INR17.8 crore (25% margin) versus 14% a year earlier and 19% in Q1, attributed to product mix and operating leverage. Alloys revenue grew in H1 but a new furnace ran below capacity due to teething issues, so FY27 alloys guidance was cut to INR40-50 crore. Relays commercial ramp-up slipped to FY28, and Quantum Magnetics product approvals have not started, so FY27 revenue from that segment is now expected to be nil.

504380|2026-06.headline: Flomic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to 9.34%, but PAT fell to INR2.06 crore from INR2.98 crore.
504380|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore, with management attributing most of the growth to higher freight rates rather than volume (shipments up roughly 6-7%). EBITDA rose about 68% to INR11.21 crore and margin improved to 9.34% from 6.59%. PBT turned positive at INR2.73 crore from a loss of INR3.3 crore a year earlier, while PAT was INR2.06 crore versus INR2.98 crore last year. Management said a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit was included, and it cited branch closures, manpower cost reduction and an AI-based back-office system from 1 July as margin levers.

segments.commentary: Revenue around INR33.39 crore in Q1; management said ocean exports are the main incremental profit pool while freight rates are rising.

segments.name: Air Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR22 crore in Q1; management said some cargo has shifted from ocean to air, adding to this segment.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore in Q1; around 15% of revenue now, with a stated gross margin of 15-16% (15-20% range), targeted at 17-18% and then about 20% of contribution.

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Clearance
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.42 crore in Q1; management did not give further detail.

504614|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 44% to INR2,025 crores and PAT 58% to INR1,109 crores, with Q4 PAT up 53% YoY to INR155 crores.
504614|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 thermal (4,155 MU ex-captive, +84% YoY) and hydro (661 MU, +31%) generation, with the energy segment contributing about two-thirds of EBITDA. Consolidated revenue rose 23% to INR5,928 crores, and net debt fell to INR215 crores from INR1,566 crores. Q4 was dented by a 30 MW captive unit shutdown, a 300 MW turbine maintenance outage in January, seasonal hydro slowdown and the coal mine hitting its 1.8 MTPA approved limit. Management outlined a doubling of energy capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 after the Supreme Court dismissed appeals on the SKS Power acquisition, plus a Raipur pellet expansion to 2 MTPA.

segments.name: Thermal power (ex captive)
segments.commentary: Generation reached a record 4,155 MU in FY26 versus 2,238 MU in FY25 (+84%), helped by SKS Power integration. Around 400 crore sellable units are guided for FY27 versus about 375 crore units sold in FY26; FY26 realisation was above INR5/unit.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: Generation hit a record 661 MU in FY26 versus 508 MU in FY25 (+31%), helped by the 25 MW Rehar project. Management said the hydro segment EBITDA was about INR386 crores, and that two hydro projects have long-term PPAs.

segments.name: Steel, sponge iron and pellets
segments.commentary: Iron ore pellet output hit a record 826,293 MT and sponge iron 345,066 MT in FY26; HB wire record 40,425 MT. Steel realisation improved YoY and QoQ in Q4 but FY26 averaged below FY25.

segments.name: Coal mining (Gare Palma IV/7)
segments.commentary: FY26 output hit the 1.8 MTPA permissible limit after CECB consent for expansion from 1.68 MTPA; Q4 volumes were lower as the annual cap was exhausted. Domestic coal sales were about 150k MT, as most output is captively consumed.

guidance_outlook: SKS Power capacity to double to 1,200 MW by FY30; management now says commissioning is around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being sought after the earlier one expired.
Acquisition of a majority stake in Adishankar Khuitam Power (66 MW, Arunachal Pradesh) approved; DPR being finalised, with the project expected to start by end-2026 and take 3-4 years.
Three small Chhattisgarh hydro projects (74 MW in total) may take 3-4 years to commission.
50 MW captive solar expected by end of Q1 FY27 (about September per later remarks); 30 MW TG set replacement to be back by end-June 2026.
Shahpur West high-grade coal mine targeted for commissioning before end-FY27; full-year operations expected in FY28.
Raipur pellet plant expansion from 0.9 to 2.0 MTPA, capex about INR500 crores, completion within 2.5 years; EC in place and DPR under preparation.

Annual hydro capex of about INR500-700 crores; the 600 MW IPP expansion to bring 'full blast' capex from next year, which will be substantially higher. Management did not give an investment figure for SKS expansion yet.
Management is evaluating separation of the renewable energy business (not the full power business); no conclusion yet.
Capex of about INR150 crores over the next two years at the Binjkot plant to improve PLF.
capex_capacity: Gare Palma IV/7 coal mine expansion to 1.8 MTPA with CECB consent; approvals for Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga and Senduri coal mines progressing.
Binjkot (SKS) plant: over INR140 crores capex invested to date, with about INR150 crores more planned over the next two years to lift PLF.
Raipur pellet plant: 9 lakh tons to 20 lakh tons; about INR500 crores capex; 2.5-year build.
Mineral wool project installed to use industrial waste; management expects it to add to bottom line as it ramps up.
FY27 earnings drivers named: full-year Rehar hydro, efficiency gains at the IPP, 50 MW solar and the 30 MW TG set; FY28 driver is full-year Shahpur coal mine.
demand_pricing: Power exchange prices averaged INR3.75/unit in Q4 FY26, versus INR4.30 a year earlier and INR3.33 in Q3. Peak demand hit a record 270.8 GW.
Indian coal index rose 8% from March 2025 and 9% from December 2025 levels, due to import disruption from the West Asia conflict.

Steel prices recovered by about 10-15% in Q4 FY26 after reaching multi-year lows. Management expects long-product prices to rise once the conflict settles, but would not give Q1 FY27 realisation guidance.
Management said NMDC and OMC have cut iron ore prices, so end-product prices may fall.
India crude steel output grew over 11% in FY26; steel consumption about 164 million tonnes. Safeguard duties have reduced Chinese imports.

About 300 MW of the 600 MW IPP capacity is under PPA (medium/long term), with about 200 MW under PPA this year, rising to 300 MW next year. Management said PPA prices give more visibility than the volatile spot market.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company restarting steel/pellet capex after holding back for a long time?

Full-scale TMT 550D direct-charging ramp expected by Q4 FY27 after monsoon and pollution-related construction halts.
Melt shop expansion considered once utilisation exceeds 70-75%; refinancing with existing lenders being discussed to lower borrowing cost.

504973|2026-03.headline: Chola MS FY26 combined ratio rose to 115.2% (112.2% ex-1/n) on motor claims and crop loss; PBT Rs454 crore, ROE 10.4%.
504973|2026-03.overview: Chola MS reported Q4 GDPI of Rs2,048 crore and FY26 GDPI of Rs7,762 crore, with the loss of crop business after re-tender cutting Rs124 crore in Q4 and over Rs590 crore for the year. The FY26 claims ratio rose about 2.71 percentage points, driven by motor OD claims and a stepped-up motor third-party reserve, pushing the combined ratio to 115.2%. FY26 PBT was Rs454 crore after labour-code gratuity provisioning, and ROE was 10.4% against a 3-year average peak of about 14.4%. Management will seek forbearance to move statutory accounting to Ind AS from April 1, 2027, and Rajive Kumaraswami takes over as MD from June 1.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 ROE on average net worth

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Market share 5.25%; mix of cars 49%+, CVs 40%+, 2-wheelers about 10.5%. Motor OD share grew to about 5.89% while TP share fell about 0.5 pp. 2-wheeler share cut from 19.6% to about 10.6%.

segments.name: Long-term non-motor
segments.commentary: Premium received in advance rose to about Rs570 crore at March 2026 from Rs250 crore at March 2025. Non-motor market share 3.3% for the year, with premium received in advance of Rs410 crore for the year.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Lost crop business after re-tender, a hit of about Rs598 crore for FY26 per the Q&A. Management expects to participate in the next tender cycle across states, awaiting Government of India guidelines.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV book about 40-42% of motor mix and stable. Management sees pricing pressure and is managing line sizes while using newly secured reinsurance capacity on favourable terms.

Motor OD price realisation up about 7-8% over the last 2-3 months; management expects motor OD loss ratio to start falling within about 6 months.
Statutory accounting to move to Ind AS from April 1, 2027 (FY28) under forbearance; significant drop in combined ratio expected in the year of adoption, then levelling out.
Management expects the 30% EOM norm to remain without further glide path; any regulator-mandated cut in commissions seen as positive, though it may lower premiums and float income.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity secured during the year on favourable terms, supporting commercial growth.
Chola Xceed operating app for sales staff and channel partners to launch soon, aimed at renewals and productivity.
Agency channel base built up; focus shifts to renewal rates.
Dividend withheld, with earnings retained to support growth and solvency.
demand_pricing: Direct premium declined in FY26; GWP growth came mainly from reinsurance inward business.
Motor TP premium unchanged for about 4-5 years; management is pressing regulator and government for two-way TP pricing correction.
Motor OD claims ratio rose across industry; Chola's rise about 10% versus about 5-7% for peers, per management.
Retail retention about 78%+ on weighted basis; blended retention about 72%.
Management says expected IFRS adoption (DAC and discounting of motor TP) will benefit P&L.

qa_highlights.question: Will the approach change under EOM compliance, and which lines will recover market share for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects crop business to return from the next tender cycle and aims to grow direct crop; motor 2-wheeler cut is near its floor; car and CV books to keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROE rise to 16-17% if leverage falls to 5.5% and combined ratio is 108-109%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the OD claims ratio is the area of correction (about 10% above peers), with 7-8% price realisation gains and a target ROE of about 15%. TP reserving is prudent and cash is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: What will the claims ratio look like under Ind AS/IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Motor TP provisions are discounted under IFRS, which brings a significant one-time benefit on transition and later P&L benefit through the unwind; no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did solvency drop to 1.96x and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher claims growth consumed more capital; solvency should recover with better claims ratio and retained earnings.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No combined ratio guidance; will aim for 15%+ ROE medium to long term, managing float income and combined ratio as EOM changes.

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects virtually no gross-subsidy business left, standalone accounts required to be individually profitable, and PSU bank group platform pricing corrections with migration to retail platform. Focus shifts to multinational single-mandate clients, SME and GPA cross-sell.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving (expected ULR), not pure reserve strengthening; motor TP is tariff-based so pricing lags claims cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor two-wheeler reduced and how does the Supreme Court ruling affect claims?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler reduction was deliberate given profitability; courts have not uniformly applied the Rs 30,000 threshold and evaluate cases individually. Solvency impact of an adverse outcome not quantified; reserves said to include margin for adverse deviation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IFRS/Ind AS profitability and ROE impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Implementation effective April 1, 2027 after one-year forbearance; no reliable estimate yet, special-purpose financial statements not yet filed with IRDAI. Preliminary observations possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is inward reinsurance growth sustainable and what is the CAT and reinsurance renewal outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inward reinsurance comes from commercial lines participation and selective group health; sustainable only as underwriting appetite allows. Hours-clause structure means separate deductibles per event, so P&L impact could be larger, supporting pricing discipline; reinsurance softness more visible at next renewal.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio (80-86% range) and whether it moves toward high-70s as guided.
Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment: review outcome and possible retrospective provisioning; solvency at 1.93x.
Reinsurance renewal terms after soft market and GIFT City capacity; loss of commissions or higher retention risk.
Health portfolio profitability and rebuilding of retail health capabilities; combined ratio of group health was flagged as a concern.
Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027, with impact on profitability and ROE still unquantified.

505010|2026-03.headline: Automotive Axles Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 18% QoQ to INR6,643 million, with PAT margin steady at 8%; FY26 revenue INR21,777 million (+5%).
505010|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR6,643 million, up about 18% QoQ and 18.5-18.7% YoY, with EBITDA of INR825 million (12.4%) and PAT of INR539 million (8%), matching Q4 FY25's PAT margin. FY26 revenue grew 5% to INR21,777 million, with EBITDA of INR2,692 million (12.4%) before a one-time workmen settlement of about INR120 million, which takes reported EBITDA to 10.6% (10.1% in FY25). Management said the industry's 7.5T+ CV market closed FY26 at about 480,000 units (+16%), and that the company operates at 70-80% of capacity in soft months after about 90% in Q4. Management said Phase 1 and 1A capacity will be complete by end-December 2026, with a next capex phase to be defined over the next 6-12 months.

financial_highlights.change: Flat QoQ; includes one-offs such as leave encashment (~8% of quarter cost)
Similar to Q4 FY25 PAT margin of ~8%

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 total income incl. other income

financial_highlights.value: INR2,692 million (12.4%); 10.6% after ~INR120 million exceptional (annualised workmen settlement)

segments.commentary: Management says the core is heavy-duty (50T+ tonnage) axles, with the 185 single axle, tandem and HR axles covering 70-80 tonne ranges. The 4x2 tractor-trailer product launched about 2-3 years ago is being ramped up across major customers.

segments.commentary: Less than 5% of revenue, per management. Company says it will not extend beyond certain GBW/GAW levels, with focus staying on heavier vehicles. Slipper suspension supply continues to the largest customer under a supply-chain handover agreement.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the domestic CV market to stay at 400,000+ units in FY27 (FY26 was ~480,000); analysts were told the range could be 420-450k-480k, and it is too early to call.
Long-term top line is targeted at roughly INR4,000-5,000 crore, with exports a larger share than today; management cited this as the direction over the next several years.
Capex in FY27 is expected to be similar in size to FY26 (~INR70 crore per Raman K.'s statement; a figure of INR30 crore was spent in FY26), with the next phase to be defined in 6-12 months.
Management declined to give forward margin guidance but said efficiency gains should offset inflation and product mix effects, with fixed-cost absorption improving as top line grows.
Technical fee payable to Meritor HVS is 4-4.5% of revenue, depending on the domestic/export mix, and is accrued monthly; all reported quarterly results are stated after this fee.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 and 1A capacity expected to be completed by end-December 2026, per management.
Management said current utilisation was about 90% in Q4 FY26 and is typically 70-80% in soft months such as April-May 2026.

Management said the capex will also bring in new technology and efficient equipment to offset fixed-cost inflation.

505010|2026-06.headline: Automotive Axles Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% (from 12.4% QoQ) on revenue of Rs 5,168 mn and PAT of Rs 455 mn.
505010|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 5,168 million, EBITDA of Rs 702 million (about 13.6%), and profit for the year of Rs 455 million (about 8.7%, EPS about Rs 30). Management now sees the FY27 M&HCV industry down 5-10% versus last year, against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption, with Q4 expected to be a peak quarter. Capacity expansion (Phase-1 and Phase-1(a)) is about 40% complete.

segments.name: Exports (to Meritor/CDBS global plants)
segments.commentary: Exports were about 13% of the quarter's revenue, versus a traditional 8-12% range; management guides to 8-12% for the year, with sea freight the main logistics challenge.

segments.commentary: Defence contributes about 5-10% of revenue depending on tender timing; long gestation of 3-10 years from RFQ to SOP.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a loss of share; the gap reflects product mix and seasonal/segment shifts. Confirmed Ashok Leyland share was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How was the cost of steel and gas handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel and other commodities are passed through fully. Conversion cost increases were absorbed in Q1 with recovery from customers being negotiated.

qa_highlights.answer: Industry down 5-10% versus the earlier 15-20%; best case is flat with last year, Q4 a peak quarter.

Forging expected to grow 15-20% in FY27 to about INR340-350 crores, with Q2 at double-digit growth and Q4 the strongest quarter; July and August reported as improving on June.
Longer-term targets: gasket about INR850-900 crores and forging about INR600-700 crores by FY30; export share target 35% by FY28.
Sustainable EBITDA margin cited at around 17%. Capex planned at about INR103 crores for FY27 across gaskets, forgings and heat shields.
Management expects OEMs to pass through steel, aluminium and labour cost increases in coming quarters; Marelli margins expected to recover by year-end.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 capex of about INR103 crores across gaskets, forgings and heat shields, to meet OEM demand.
Forging equipment is in place; manpower and leadership issues reportedly resolved, with new CEO Ashish (appointed April 1) spending about 50% of time on forging.
Stellantis programme in the chassis division started production in Q1 FY27 after about 2 years of design changes and start of production.
Plastic EV components for JLR at about INR25 crores in orders, maturing from next financial year; JLR EV rubber components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. with supply from Q1/Q2 CY27.
Possible chassis plant in Gujarat under discussion with Tata Motors (management to meet Tata Motors chief within 90 days).
demand_pricing: Industry context: PV sales about 1.27 million units (+26% YoY), 2-wheelers 5.63 million units (+~20%), CV about 2.83 lakh units (+15%), EV PV volumes +87%, EV 2W about +68%.
Data centres: about 5% of gasket revenue today; estimated INR30-40 crores annual potential, rising toward INR100 crores in 2-3 years; Cummins sales of INR25 crores in Q1 vs INR90 crores last year.
Management said 7 OEMs are looking to shift supply chains from China to India; BMW giving more business, Volvo a potential new gasket customer, and Stellantis opened for Marelli.
Cummins America expected to contribute INR30-40 crores by FY27-28 (wire harness, aftermarket and data-centre gaskets).
Forging orders: about INR500 crores over 5 years (about INR100 crores p.a.) cited; Marelli and Dana/Carraro orders maturing in Q3-Q4.
Gasket pricing: management said data-centre gaskets are the same product as regular gaskets, with pricing unchanged; margins not separately disclosed.
Management stated pricing pass-through of input costs from OEMs is expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How far along are the ~7 OEMs looking to shift supply chains from China to India, and what is the status of new Stellantis and Kia projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European customers are weak; BMW is giving more business, Volvo is a potential new gasket customer, and Marelli has opened doors with Stellantis. JLR is a new plastic EV component customer, Cummins America is a slow starter expected to yield INR30-40 crores by FY27-28, and a Gujarat chassis plant is being discussed with Tata Motors (meeting within 90 days).

qa_highlights.question: Any progress on the stake transaction in Marelli?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no firm update yet; they are in court proceedings and expect a clearer picture by end-September, with details to be discussed offline.

qa_highlights.question: What share of gasket revenue comes from data centres, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% of gasket revenue today. Cummins sales were INR25 crores in Q1 versus INR90 crores last year; data-centre business is estimated at INR30-40 crores a year, rising toward INR100 crores in 2-3 years. Talbros is single source to Cummins for the engine component.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth expectations for gaskets and forging, and the longer-term potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Gasket growth expected around 17% in FY27 (about INR680-700 crores). Forging Q1 was up 4%; Q2 expected at double-digit growth and FY27 forging growth of 15-20% to about INR340-350 crores. Longer term, gaskets INR850-900 crores and forging INR600-700 crores within 3-4 years, with management referencing FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why did forging Q1 growth lag and why has the forging guidance come down from earlier expectations of around INR400 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by manpower shortages, LPG price spikes, lower BMW and GKN schedules and some orders taking time to move into execution; productivity dipped. Loss of Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.) due to US tariffs is a key reason. Management said July was better than June and cited a INR500 crores, 5-year order book (about INR100 crores p.a.).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Marelli margins fall in Q1, and which segment will grow fastest in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other income plus new manpower and shared rental costs; management expects margins to recover by year-end. Marelli is expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, forging about 20%, gaskets about 16-17%, and Talbros Marugo 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is data-centre gasket margin different from the rest of the gasket business, and what is the EV revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Same gasket product sold for a new application, with pricing unchanged; margins not split out. EV-related supply was INR12.5 crores in Q1 (about 3.27% of sales) versus INR10 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR9 crores a year ago; management targets around 5% in 2 years and a minimum of 5% over 5 years. JLR rubber EV components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. start in Q1/Q2 CY27.

risks_watch: Pass-through of steel, aluminium and labour inflation from OEMs has not yet happened; FY27 margin guide of about 17-17.5% depends on it.
Forging recovery depends on European demand, execution of the INR500 crores order book, and resolution of manpower and productivity issues; Q1 growth was only 4%.
Marelli JV: stake transaction still pending court proceedings with update expected by end-September; Q1 JV margin dip to be reversed by year-end.
Data-centre revenue (about 5% of gasket revenue) is concentrated in a single customer, Cummins, and depends on engine orders.
Lost Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.) and Cummins America ramp-up timing (slow starter) could weigh on the forging and gasket revenue trajectory.
Export share at about 25% against a 35% FY28 target; EV share at 3.27% of sales against a 5% goal.
key_quotes: Talbros has delivered yet another record quarter, achieving its highest ever quarterly revenue and surpassing the previous high recorded in quarter 4 of '26.
But we are very positive that we will get these increases from the OEMs in the coming quarters.
We are pretty much single source to Cummins for this particular engine component.
Plus, we are supplying bushes to BMW of EV vehicles, where sale has gone up a little bit there.

On forging and Marelli it was more guarded, with several answers deferred to later updates such as the end-September Marelli stake update.

rows.why: Group revenue growth guided at 18-20% for FY27, gaskets about 17% to INR680-700 crores, forging 15-20% to INR340-350 crores with Q2 at double-digit growth, and Marelli 30-40%; Q1 forging was only +4%.

rows.when: Marelli and Dana/Carraro orders maturing Q3-Q4 FY27

rows.why: Cummins America expected to contribute INR30-40 crores by FY27-28, but management calls it a slow starter and Cummins Q1 sales fell to INR25 crores from INR90 crores a year earlier.
