505192|2026-03.headline: SML Mahindra FY26 revenue rose 18% and PAT 31%, but Q4 PAT grew only 2% on a 16% revenue rise as commodity inflation hit.
505192|2026-03.overview: This was the first investor call since Mahindra's 58.96% controlling acquisition completed on 1 August 2025, about eight months post-takeover. Management said FY26 volumes grew 28% in cargo and 12% in passenger vehicles, with market share up 20 bps in cargo and 80 bps in passenger for the full year. Q4 showed a cargo share dip, which management attributed to pre-poned institutional orders executed in Q3, while bus share gained 170 bps in the quarter. Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost (roughly 3.5-3.7% annualised), and a price increase of about 2-3% was taken from 15 April 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up two notches from AA minus

segments.name: Cargo (trucks)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 28% with market share up 20 bps for the year; Q4 cargo share declined, attributed by management to Q3 pre-ponement of institutional orders. Q4 cargo volume grew 10%.

segments.name: Passenger (buses)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 12% with market share up 80 bps; Q4 bus share gained 170 bps in the peak school-bus season. Q4 passenger volume grew 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a top-three position in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment, with focus on HCVs, and targets 10-12% combined market share by FY31 (currently about 6%).
Around FY31, the company targets about Rs 15,000 crore revenue, per the Global Investor Day, against a 3.5-tonne-plus revenue pool of about Rs 1.25 lakh crore last year.
Q1 FY27 plans are largely unchanged from original plans as of the call; management said a diesel price increase is the key swing factor.

Commodity inflation is expected to be partly temporary; management said price increases and commodity hedges should largely cover headwinds, and inflation is not expected to persist through FY27 if the Middle East situation eases.
First EV bus is to be launched in FY27; management gave no capex or volume figures for it.
A longer-format strategy session is planned for July 2026, close to the AGM.
capex_capacity: Service network: combined touchpoints to rise from about 300 to 450 by pooling 150 service setups across both brands; 70 are operational and 80 more are due by end of Q1 FY27.

Engineering and manufacturing synergies are being pursued to reduce product cost and capex outlay, including sharing engine (4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre) and ADAS development with Mahindra teams.
ADAS regulation compliance (due in about 1.5 years) is a joint project with Mahindra, with cost detail deferred to launch.
EV bus development is underway; management said capex for scale-up will depend on market evolution.
demand_pricing: Industry grew about 2% in H1 FY26 and about 22% in H2 post-GST reform; ICV trucks +42%, LCV trucks +20%, MCV trucks +28%, ILCV +8% in that period.
Management sees no demand deferment yet and cites pent-up replacement demand, though a diesel price hike and Middle East disruption could moderate demand.
Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost; Q1 FY27 saw further increases in some commodities (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases), with some volatility.
Price increases of about 2% (some 3%) on SML products effective 15 April 2026; more may follow based on analysis.
Electric bus industry share is below 1% of the segment; private buyers are not yet buying e-buses beyond STU purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook, market share trajectory and synergy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry shifted from about 2% growth in H1 to about 22% in H2. Management said synergies come on both the back end (sourcing, engineering, manufacturing) and the front end (common dealers in unrepresented territories), with growth as the main thesis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to merge the two companies or delist SML?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delisting plan. On a merger, it is working on long-term strategy and will update at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the supply chain and cost impacts of the current crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: No vehicle production was lost through Q4 despite gas, aluminium and polymer shortages. Steel, aluminium, copper and polymers rose, and gases trade at a premium; management expects most increases to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called ADAS a significant development and said cost and detail would be shared at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand deferment seen in March or April?
qa_highlights.answer: No deferment as of now; peak school-bus season is underway and Q1 plans are largely as originally planned, but management flagged diesel price risk.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 margin headwind and what pricing offset is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inflation was about 1.3% of cost (about 3.5-3.7% annualised). Price increases of about 2-3% began 15 April, and hedges will provide a partial offset, though steel cannot be hedged. Management said pricing should largely cover headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV bus and e-mobility strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EV bus launches in FY27 with product details to follow closer to launch. Capex scale-up will depend on market evolution, as private buyers are not yet buying e-buses.

risks_watch: Diesel price increase and Middle East disruption could moderate CV demand after Q1 FY27.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases) may persist; hedges do not cover steel, and pricing actions may lag.
Q4 PAT growth of 2% vs revenue growth of 16% indicates margin pressure that must be tracked in Q1 FY27.
Cargo market share dip in Q4 FY26 tied to order timing; watch whether share recovers in FY27.
Integration delivery: service network expansion to 450 touchpoints and cross-badging, plus dealer-channel sensitivity.
Timing and scope of the July 2026 strategy session and merger-related updates.
505192|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, integration progress and the demand tailwind, but cautious on the near-term outlook. Management was guarded on the diesel price, commodity inflation and EV timing, and avoided quantifying ADAS cost and merger plans.
key_quotes: We have outgrown the industry. We grew at 17% in the industry versus industry growth of 13%.
So, the main thesis behind this acquisition was growth.

We have not lost any vehicle production till quarter four in spite of several challenges, whether it is related to availability of gas or whether it is related to many other commodity availability, including aluminium, including polymers.

rows.why: Utilisation not quantified and management said no vehicle production was lost through Q4; capex is tied to synergies (shared engines, ADAS with Mahindra) and cautious EV scale-up, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.why: Shared 4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre engines and ADAS development are being pursued to cut product cost and capex outlay, though ADAS cost is not yet quantified and is due in about 1.5 years.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.name: Standalone TIL (cranes, material handling, defence)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Tulip Compression (TCPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover, but gave no numeric revenue guidance. Analyst's INR200 crore+ scenario was not confirmed.
Management expects no EBITDA margin harmonisation for the next six to eight quarters; medium-to-long-term TIL standalone EBITDA target 15-16%, timing 3-7 years.
Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.
Debtor days target 60-75 days maximum; long-term aftermarket share target 40-45% of revenue.
Board approved up to INR50 crore equity infusion into Tulip; commitment to raise stake to 74% over a few years.
CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27, worst case Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Kharagpur plant loaded only 30-35% with about 150 acres free; Kamarhati plant is old and fully loaded.
Bridging capex of INR5-10 crore per instance, mainly for the old Kamarhati plant.
Target to localise 75-80% in every product and above 90% overall, with Cummins engines for ReachStacker a key dependency.
Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.
Rough terrain crane market share about 50%+; truck crane share now below 5% from over 95% a decade ago, lost to Chinese competition.
Order delivery timelines range from 60-90 days (retail ReachStacker) to 6-9 months (defence), with the bulk of the order book typically exhausted within nine months.
Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; management said TIL will not compete on extended credit terms.
Tulip's market share is about one-third in India in a three-player market; clients include city gas distributors such as IGL, MNGL and IGL-type CGD operators.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.
qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: management called the working capital cycle stressed; debtor days and debt reduction are the key items to track.
Margin volatility: EBITDA margins depend on product mix, and management gave no margin guidance for six to eight quarters.
Supply-chain dependence: localisation of European and US inputs (Cummins engines, gearboxes) depends on OEM and defence approvals and could take several quarters.
Execution: converting the INR211 crore standalone order book and the INR328 crore TCPL order book on time; the FY26 shortfall was attributed to geopolitics and logistics.
Governance and bandwidth: the Chairman plans to devote 40-50% of his time to TIL from next quarter, versus about 60% needed, and the Gainwell merger question was left open.
Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is being passed on through pricing, and how much is being offset?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Volvo financing JV see profit benefits and will it be a capital-hungry business?

qa_highlights.question: What are the product pipeline and timelines, including the Bullet 650 and any plans below 350cc?

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Andhra Pradesh greenfield plant and its capacity ramp?

505200|2026-06.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 6,632 crore with record Royal Enfield volumes of 332,940 units.
505200|2026-06.overview: Eicher Motors posted its best-ever Q1 with consolidated revenue of INR 6,632 crore (up 32% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,591 crore and PAT of INR 1,463 crore (up 21%). Royal Enfield sold a record 332,940 motorcycles (up from 261,326), and VECV recorded its highest-ever Q1 sales of 24,815 units (up 14.8%). Management flagged a tight dealer inventory of 10-12 days ahead of festive season, with capacity ramp-up at Cheyyar and a greenfield Tada (Andhra Pradesh) plant approved. Commodity inflation of 4-4.5% of costs was partly offset by price hikes and value engineering, and softening was noted.

segments.commentary: Global volume 31,766 motorcycles; Brazil is the largest overseas market (about every fourth exported motorcycle), with a planned CKD facility. Europe remains in a market adjustment phase; US shows early green shoots after a tariff cut.

segments.commentary: Flying Flea C6 launched and deliveries started this quarter; about 100+ units delivered in two months, with Bengaluru expansion to 10 touchpoints and about 6 further cities planned.

segments.commentary: Allied businesses about 15% of revenue; about 9 lakh service job cards per month (up about 20% YoY); accessories and apparel growing above 30%, with accessory attach rate at about 87% per management.

demand_pricing: Royal Enfield India retail growth about 30-32% YoY in Q1; booking, walk-in and telephonic inquiries growing slightly faster than volumes.

Dealer inventory at about 10-12 days, described as lean; in-transit inventory about 5 days and depot inventory about 4-5 days additional, per Q&A. Management targets saving another 4-5 days via more direct billing (about 4.5-4.7x increase vs prior year).

qa_highlights.question: Where is the brownfield capacity ramp and what is channel inventory ahead of festive?
qa_highlights.answer: First module started July 2026, output about 5,000+ per day delivery; inventory about 10-12 days, lean; direct billing and vendor 3-shift planning aimed to build stock before festive; next module by October first week.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin bridge and the drivers of lower other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Net commodity/input impact about 4-4.5%, value engineering about 0.4%, price hikes about 1.2%, mix 0.2%. Other expenses down about 7%: INR 30 crore from Q4 timing (cricket ads, two launches) and INR 22 crore marketing cut. No forward commodity guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What is demand outlook into the back half given high base from October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management points to strong funnel growth, a middleweight segment that grew from 70,000 to 1.2 lakh units per month in three years, planned launches, and a marketing ramp-up after scaling back in Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap between standalone and consolidated and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Gap driven by subsidiary growth, mainly Brazil, with some offset from India-booked exports; international market size about 0.8-1 million units, Royal Enfield share 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up and what is driving non-vehicle revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: ASP up 2.8% QoQ: price hikes 1.2%, international mix 1%, currency 0.4%, allied 0.6%. Allied about 15% of revenue, service job cards about 9 lakh per month.

qa_highlights.question: Any plans to list or hive off VECV?

505255|2026-03.headline: GMM Pfaudler FY26 revenue rose about 10% and EBITDA about 11% to INR 403 crore; Q4 gross margin fell, with no FY27 numeric guidance.
505255|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA rose from INR 361 crore to INR 403 crore, with full-year margin up about 1 percentage point. India was the standout, with revenue up about 12%, EBITDA up about 24% and PAT up about 40%. Q4 margins fell year-on-year and sequentially on a large HE (heavy engineering) shipment and higher gas and metal costs, which management called quarter-specific. FY26 order intake reached INR 3,714 crore (up about 20% from INR 3,100 crore) and opening backlog on April 1 was up about 34%. Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance and said it would present a three-year plan to the market later.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 12%, EBITDA about 24% and PAT about 40% in FY26. Heavy engineering (Ahmedabad) did about INR 300+ crore revenue in FY26, and the Vatva facility (GMM Inox, Poland) grew double digits.

segments.name: Europe / International
segments.commentary: Execution was slow; international EBITDA margin cited at about 10%. German restructuring is expected to save INR 45 crore a year once fully absorbed. Europe order intake was much stronger in FY26, including large systems orders.

segments.commentary: Edlon (semiconductor-linked high-purity linings) is now about USD 25 million revenue, which management called high margin. SEMCO (South America) won a USD 12-13 million agitator order in Q1 FY27; MixPro (Canada) is growing and profitable.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; management said it expects improvement in FY27 on a 12-month basis, citing order intake, backlog and restructuring.

Two large systems orders (one US, one Eastern Europe) drove much of the increase; open systems opportunities could yield USD 20-30 million order intake per year.
Chemicals (especially agrochemicals and European chemicals) remain slow; pharma (CDMO, GLP drugs) improving; China business recovering in some segments.
Raw material pass-through depends on contract: long-term projects have a 5% expedition clause; fast-moving contracts absorb cost changes.
Q1 FY27 order intake continuing at a decent level, including an Edlon order of USD 8-9 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross and consolidated EBITDA margins (55.4% gross) drop, and what are sustainable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to a large HE order shipped at lower margin and higher gas and metal costs that have since stabilised. It said quarterly margins are volatile and FY26 margin was up about 1 pp; it prefers 12-month views.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance for FY27, and what drives the growth and margin plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% order-intake rise includes systems orders that convert over 2-3 years, so it avoided a bullish number. It plans a three-year strategy to be presented to the capital markets once confidence improves, targeting at least double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the German restructuring saving and will exceptional items recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The German restructuring saves INR 45 crore a year, starting next year. No significant one-off cost is planned for FY27, though future restructurings would be reported as one-offs. FY26 exceptional items were about INR 65 crore, including German severance and the India labour code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the finance cost high relative to a small net debt, and how does the company plan to reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FX on an intercompany loan between Germany and Luxembourg, and a financing agreement in place until 2028, which it intends to restructure within the next year. It said the high cash balance is partly customer prepayments needed to finance large systems orders.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to a 15% consolidated EBITDA margin in the medium term, as a minimum, versus about 11.4-11.5% today, and said it could come faster if initiatives work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reporting format will change from next quarter (Q1 FY27), with a new organisation aligned by product, vertical and industry, rather than mid-year.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 255 crores (+23% YoY); order intake INR 367 crores (+64% YoY). Covers mixing, filtration, drying, and sealing; pharma and food & beverage adoption cited.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 crores (flat YoY); order intake INR 58 crores (up more than 700% YoY). India-led, oil and gas, petrochemicals, with nuclear and power entry and EIL approvals.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 131 crores (+46% YoY); order intake INR 80 crores vs INR 363 crores in Q1 FY26, which included one large defence order. Skids and engineered systems for semiconductor, defence and pharma.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 15%, described as a minimum target; management said current verticals are roughly around this range, with no timeline given.
Management expects improvement YoY across all businesses but declined to give a specific margin number; quarter-on-quarter margin tracking was framed as the approach.
Debt: about EUR 7 million to be repaid by end of Q2 FY27; further reduction via refinancing over 12 to 18 months. No year-end debt target disclosed.
Tax rate: work with around 30%, possibly slightly lower in the long term, expected within 18 to 24 months after refinancing and entity restructuring.

Possible investor day around Q2 FY27 (management said 'hopefully').
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Global engineering centre (GEC) with about 12 people in place; Poland and India being developed as low-cost engineering hubs.
Workforce reductions in UK (prior year) and factory workforce in Germany (last year) expected to flow through to costs in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: India pharma improving, driven by CDMO and API investment in Hyderabad; glass-lined inquiries and conversion rates up vs 12 months ago. Management says Q1 and Q2 look strong for glass-lined.
Chemicals flat in India and remain challenging in Europe; no structural change seen.

International pharma improving in Europe and Americas; US has large glass-lined pharma orders; China back with glass-lined orders; Europe still slow overall though several large glass-lined orders won.
Peptide investment is a new pharma driver, with a large peptide order supplied last year and two large Hyderabad system orders.
Pricing pressure in a shifting business mix cited as a reason for lower YoY EBITDA. Management expects pricing to improve as markets recover.
Opening backlog for FY27 was about 30% higher than a year earlier, which was partly flattered by a large defence order (~EUR 30 million) in the prior-year base.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of recovery in chemical and pharma markets, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharma is improving in India (Hyderabad CDMO), the US and Europe; chemicals remain flat. India traditional markets are better than 12 months ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India standalone margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from HET (lower-margin, longer-cycle project business); a mix shift plus investment in people for the new organisation. Management expects margins to recover over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the target EBITDA margins and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15% EBITDA as the aspiration and said margins would be tracked quarter-on-quarter. It declined to give a year-end debt target.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book executes within 10 to 12 months, and what is the debt repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Large majority of the roughly INR 1,000 crore Q1 intake is executable in 10 to 12 months. Debt repayment of EUR 7 million now, with a further reduction over 12 to 18 months; no amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state tax rate and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 30%, possibly slightly lower long term, achieved in 18 to 24 months after debt refinancing and entity rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there severance cost in Q1, and will employee costs keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off severance in Q1. Management aims to lower employee costs over time by shifting non-critical work to low-cost locations, though some sales hires will be added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost and order intake outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Average interest cost of 6% to 7%, mostly hedged SOFR/EURIBOR-linked debt. Order intake is flat YoY but with a different profile, with most Q1 orders at 10 to 12 month cycles.

Investment in people and organisation raises employee costs ahead of the revenue benefit.
Debt of about INR 835 crores (March 2026) with refinancing and entity clean-up (24 to 25 entities) still incomplete; tax rate depends on this.
Chemicals demand remains weak in India and Europe.
Q1 order intake was flat YoY and the prior-year base contained a large defence order, so the YoY comparison is not like-for-like.
Whether Q2 order intake is strong enough to sustain the backlog and build momentum.

505283|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 21% to INR706 crore and FY26 PBT hit a record INR356 crore, but management flags 18-20% EBITDA as sustainable, not the 21.7% delivered.
505283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were INR706 crore versus INR583 crore a year earlier, with raw material-to-sales falling to 50.06% from 56.35%. FY26 EBITDA was INR388 crore (21.7% of total income) and PBT INR356 crore (19.6%), supported by in-house backward integration and a selective order-acceptance stance. The unexecuted order board rose 15% to INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, including Precision Components, and the company remains debt-free with about INR460 crore net cash. Management called FY26's margin an exception and guided to 18-20% EBITDA going forward, while reaffirming a 20%+ growth aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR588 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: 600% of face value (INR12 per share), including final of INR8.50 and interim of INR3.50
About INR460 crore as on April 1, 2026

segments.name: Compression (only reportable segment)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 93.4% of total income; segment operating profit margin was 24.9% in FY26 versus 21.7% in FY25. Management said Q4 margin was a one-off and sustainable range is 18-20%.

segments.name: Air compression / ACD
segments.commentary: Roughly 18-20% of business. Tezcatlipoca centrifugal compressors gaining share (about 130 machines in field, 85 commissioned); reciprocating gas compressor orders at record highs; screw compressors lagged.

segments.name: Refrigeration (KC/KCX, Khione)
segments.commentary: Roughly 40-45% of business. Record KC/KCX volumes in FY26 and several large packages executed, some in Q4; Khione sales picking up.

segments.name: Process Gas Systems (PGS)
segments.commentary: Roughly 35-40% of business. Management described FY26 as lagging in oil and gas due to slower order finalisation; O&M base spans over 1,000 CNG stations; CNG order activity picking up in Q4.

segments.name: Precision Engineering (non-reportable in FY26)
segments.commentary: New division using Nashik and Hadapsar forgings, castings and machined components. Part of the INR1,863 crore order board; about INR500 crore executable beyond FY27. Will be reportable from Q1 FY27 per management.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin: 18-20% is the sustainable range; FY26's 21.7% is described as an exception, though management said it could reach 21% in good quarters.
Growth aspiration of 20%+ on top line and bottom line over a long period; management said it expects to deliver sales above order board conversion and reach 20%+ in FY27.
Equipment business (short-cycle, 4-12 weeks) targeted at 20-25% of revenue; new products targeted at 10-15% of sales.
Zephyros air conditioning package to be commercialised in Q1 FY27; A-800 centrifugal frame launch expected in about one month.
Capex of INR320 crore is a PLI commitment, of which about INR60 crore spent; balance to be incurred over about 2 years.
Board approved sub-division of equity shares from INR2 face value to INR1, subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Tezcatlipoca incremental capacity installed and commissioned; available from Q1 FY27.
INR320 crore PLI-linked capex, of which roughly INR60 crore incurred, covering backward integration in motors, heat exchangers and sheet metal for Zephyros at Saswad and Nashik.
Backward integration at Nashik feeding Hadapsar (air compressor and PED) and Saswad; this drove lower raw material cost ratio.
Continued capex to support growth and PLI-linked new product development; depreciation rose to INR31.1 crore in FY26 from INR28.9 crore.
Management said capacity is not a constraint at present; a subsidiary is being restructured and will take time to turn positive.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order board INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, up 15% from INR1,624 crore a year earlier; includes Precision Components. About INR500 crore executable beyond FY27.
Order inflow in the last two quarters about INR650 crore (per analyst); the order book is skewed toward products, which management said should shorten execution cycles.
Export about 6% of sales; MENA was a large share earlier but is slowing due to the Middle East conflict, with focus shifting to Southeast Asia and North Africa.
Management said price increases are passed to customers on short-cycle work, and large packages have had vendor pricing finalised, so no direct margin hit expected.
Gas package competition: specified vendor lists and lower-cost competitors make cost innovation difficult in Middle East gas packages.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and what is the Precision Engineering share?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Birajdar said the INR1,863 crore book includes Precision Components; about INR500 crore is executable beyond FY27, and the equipment business brings in INR600-700 crore a year that is executed and dispatched within the year.

qa_highlights.question: Zephyros go-to-market and returns on the INR320 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target markets are small machine shops, restaurants and banquet halls, with channel build-out via dealers. Margins will be below the 25-30% sought, and returns will come from volume; INR60 crore has been spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and ability to win gas packages?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Kirloskar said the Middle East is a key market for packages but is not a large share of total business; near-term dispatch and new orders are difficult, and the company has won Middle East packages before.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 growth not follow a book-to-bill near 1 last year, and what changes now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed reliance on the gas business, where growth has been difficult, and said actions are being taken to improve competitiveness. Equipment and Precision Engineering are expected to carry growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is 21.5-21.7% EBITDA sustainable versus the 18-20% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Kirloskar said investors should not judge quarter to quarter; 18-20% is the base, with 21% possible. Ramesh Birajdar said Q4 gross margin crossed about 23% but 18-20% remains the sustainable core-business range.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the CNG and CGD demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said daughter stations are about 70% of new stations, with mother stations needed for long-haul supply, and demand should rise for both over time. Ramesh Birajdar pointed to ONGC's about INR200 billion investment over five to six years as an opportunity.

risks_watch: Margin normalisation: management guided to 18-20% EBITDA after a 21.7% FY26; watch whether Q1 FY27 holds above 20%.
Gas segment growth has been weak; PGS is 35-40% of business and CNG/PGS order conversion needs to show.
Precision Engineering order sustainability is unclear; management declined to give a backlog split or say whether INR500 crore inflows will repeat.
Middle East conflict is slowing dispatches and new export gas orders, with MENA share of exports falling.
Zephyros commercial launch in Q1 FY27 with unproven demand; a subsidiary restructuring is under way with no timeline for positive results.
Equity sub-division from INR2 to INR1 face value and final dividend are subject to shareholder approval.
505283|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and order board growth, but cautious on margins, explicitly guiding down to 18-20% EBITDA. Evasive on Precision Engineering sustainability, backlog split and the subsidiary's timeline, and on gas-segment growth, which management called a difficulty.

505533|2026-03.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q4 FY26 same-store sales grew 1.5% on mid-single-digit guest count growth; revenue up 9% to INR 6.6 billion.
505533|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 6.6 billion and same-store sales grew 1.5%, driven by mid-single-digit guest count growth, with positive footfall in all three months and momentum continuing into April. Full-year revenue grew 5% to INR 26.3 billion. Gross margin held near historic highs at 68.1% (up about 60 bps QoQ), and full-year cash PAT was INR 2.4 billion (9% of sales). Management said it is too early to call a sustained revival, and it guided to 60+ restaurant openings in FY27 versus a record 48 in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: About +60 bps QoQ; near historic highs

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: Management described West as the strongest growth driver, though it was affected by LPG disruptions; no specific West SSS figure was given.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Same-store sales ended the quarter nearly flat, a meaningful improvement on prior quarters, with guest count turning marginally positive after the company rolled back to everyday value (except Chennai, where it is a trial).

segments.name: Digital and delivery (McDelivery, app)
segments.commentary: Cumulative app downloads crossed 52 million with about 3.5 million monthly active users growing at double-digit YoY; delivery grew about 6% vs dine-in about 9%.

guidance_outlook: Open 60+ restaurants annually going forward (FY27), with all new stores fully digital-equipped and including McCafés; Vision 2027 target of 580-630 restaurants retained.
Gross margin in the near term indicated at around 67% or higher, reflecting current inflation partly offset by cost optimisation.
Price increases of 2-4% a year are the policy, but none taken in the last four to five months and no immediate plan; some small increases possible.

Vision 2027 target: first reach about INR 3,000 crore in sales; Ind AS EBITDA margin improvement to 13-15% expected mainly from operating leverage, with a breakup for the next two years to be given closer to FY27 start.
Aim to lift SSSG towards mid-single digits as early as possible.
Toys for Happy Meals expected to take about 9 to 12 months to return; books being used meanwhile.
Store closures of about 6-7 a year expected as part of portfolio management.

Plan to open 60+ restaurants annually; partnerships with HPCL, BPCL and Jio-bp to expand highway footprint, plus airports, malls and six key metros.
Store closures in FY26 were about 6-7, attributed to malls shutting, highway access changes and lease tenure; management said this is not South-specific.
Store modernisation investment helped resilience: all restaurants operational, with fewer than 10% on limited menu due to LPG shortages.
demand_pricing: Q4 SSSG of 1.5% came with mid-single-digit guest count growth; management said it would not break out the Navratri and LPG effects, and that around 10% of stores were hit by LPG shortages from 10 March.
Growth is being driven by the 99 everyday value meal, with McCafé subscription (10 coffees a month for INR 55) and merchandise campaigns (sipper, tote bag) aimed at Gen Z.
Commodity pressure: cocoa and coffee inflation in FY26, offset by supply chain efficiencies and contract timing; management said last year's inflation tailwind may not repeat.
Management said it would hold product-mix margin dilution where it is and is not planning further value price cuts beyond current levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised SSG for Q4 after Navratri timing and supply disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to adjust further and said 1.5% SSSG is the number, with mid-single-digit guest count growth; momentum of 8-10% growth is seen in recent weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gross margin expanding and what is FY27 pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain initiatives and an internal cost project offset inflation; FY26 inflation was a tailwind that may not repeat. Pricing policy is 2-4% a year, but no price increase has been taken for four to five months and none is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why is store opening guidance 60+ versus the usual 40-50, and why the closures?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60+ number reflects Vision 2027 (580-630 restaurants) and penetration headroom; closures are portfolio management of about 6-7 a year and were not South-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion target hold if the LPG and raw material pressure persists for six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the store target holds, citing cost levers and industry-wide price increases as options if inflation rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the health and protein-led consumer read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mid-single-digit guest count growth shows no health-driven issue; it cited the Aloo Tikki balanced meal, lower sodium fries, reduced mayo fat, protein slice and millet bun as menu choices.

risks_watch: LPG shortages and geopolitical-driven commodity inflation (cocoa, coffee, supplier costs) could pressure gross margin below the 67% indication.
Delivery growth (about 6%) lags dine-in (about 9%); management wants equal growth from both channels.
Toy supply for Happy Meals still blocked by the BIS issue for about 9-12 months.
Store closures expected at 6-7 a year; whether the FY27 60+ opening pace is achieved.
SSSG remains only 1.5%, well below the mid-single-digit target; management would not call it a sustained revival.

505533|2026-06.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 7.36 billion with SSSG of 4.3%, though operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable amid inflation.
505533|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY, with same-store sales growth of 4.3% and positive SSSG in all three months. Growth was guest-count led, with double-digit footfall growth and the South turning SSSG-positive. Operating EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 946 million, but the operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable as over 200 bps of inflation (fuel, food, packaging, utilities, labour) was absorbed. Management said Q1 marks the peak of gross margin pressure and expects improvement from here, while restaurant additions were only 5 in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Positive in all three months; May and June mid-single-digit

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Management described West as continuing to deliver a very strong performance, with growth aided by a rollout of the value platform and expanded store clusters in Gujarat, Pune/rest of Maharashtra and Mumbai (each ~100 restaurants).

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: South ended the quarter with positive SSSG and double-digit guest count in all three months; management cited close to 4.5% SSSG this quarter. South has more than half of the store base per management, and Bangalore has 60+ restaurants, Hyderabad 35+ and Chennai 20+.

guidance_outlook: Over 60 new restaurants in FY27, reiterated as on track; 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027 (Vision 2027).

Management expects some cost pressures to ease as geopolitical conditions improve; targets 100-150 bps YoY improvement in pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin as an internal long-term guidance, and aspires to 100+ bps expansion in FY27 (FY26 pre-Ind AS margin cited as 7.6%).
Mid-single-digit SSSG confidence for the year, with South expected to reach mid-single-digit; management declined to give high-single-digit targets.
G&A expected at 6% to 6.5% of sales for the remaining year.
Interim dividend of INR 0.40 per equity share approved by the Board.
No price increase taken yet in FY27; annual price increase guidance is around 3%, to be taken later after consumer research.
risks_watch: Operating EBITDA margin only stable despite 11% EBITDA growth; inflation in fuel, food, packaging, utilities and labour could persist if geopolitical conditions do not ease.
Store additions of 5 in Q1 versus 60+ guided for FY27; the back-ended ramp is needed to reach 580 to 630 by December 2027.
Lower historic store economics and margin trend questioned by analysts over five to seven years; management declined to engage on the data.
Sustainability of SSSG momentum beyond Q1, and the reliance on guest-count growth while ticket growth remains weak.
Management reliance on deferred price increases (none taken yet) to protect margins.

key_quotes: Q1 FY27 marks our strongest topline growth, highest same -store sales growth and fastest guest count growth in the recent past.

505537|2026-03.headline: Zee Q4 FY26: digital revenue up 71% YoY to INR4,700 mn and ZEE5 EBITDA positive for FY26, but ad revenue fell 4% on a March West Asia hit and a INR4,084 mn one-off charge.

505700|2026-03.headline: Elecon Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR746 crore (from INR798 crore) as Gear sales dropped 21%; FY27 guidance held back.
505700|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue declined moderately YoY to INR746 crore, with EBITDA of INR158 crore (21.2% margin) and PAT of INR108 crore before a INR102 crore goodwill impairment. Gear Division revenue fell 21% YoY to INR472 crore on customer-led delivery deferrals, mainly in steel, while MHE grew 37% to INR274 crore. Management attributed the March shortfall to geopolitical-driven deferrals and said it will not give FY27 guidance, citing limited visibility. Open order book rose to about INR1,292 crore from INR948 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Material Handling Equipment (MHE)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR274 crore (37% of consolidated) vs INR200 crore, up 36.8%; EBIT INR62 crore vs INR59 crore. Q4 order inflow INR107 crore (described as a 10-quarter low); order book INR398 crore vs INR365 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Gear-to-MHE mix moved to 63:37 from the historical 75:25, and does it affect EBITDA margin?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook given ROCE fell from 29% in FY24 to 20.4% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR800 crore of capital employed is in investments yielding about 8%, and only about INR95 crore of the INR400 crore capex has been spent so far. Management expects capex to lift capacity and margins over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill impairment, and was there a tax benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR102 crore impairment relates to goodwill from the 2010-11 Benzler and Radicon acquisitions, held only in consolidated accounts. The tax deduction sits with the UK entity, with about GBP1 million of claims left over about five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 gear shortfall was caused by geopolitical events in March?

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to the earlier 22%-24% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot commit to margin levels given the geopolitical situation, but if domestic orders execute smoothly, EBITDA margin could return to the earlier 22%-24% range.

qa_highlights.question: What are the sustainable margins for MHE?

505700|2026-06.headline: Elecon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore, but management guided only low double-digit FY27 growth on raw-material-driven order conversion delays.
505700|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore over adjusted Q1 FY26 revenue of INR465 crore, with EBITDA up 3.9% to INR109 crore at a stated 21% margin and PAT of INR70 crore (13.5% margin, up 2.3%). Gear division drove growth, with revenue up 16.3% to INR416 crore, while MHE revenue fell 2.9% to INR105 crore on project execution delays and EBIT fell 25.3% to INR27 crore. Order intake rose 23% to INR755 crore and the consolidated open order book rose 36.8% to INR1,518 crore, yet management guided only low double-digit FY27 revenue growth, citing raw-material price spikes that slowed enquiry-to-order conversion and PSU-linked capex delays.

segments.name: Gear division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR416 crore (~80% of consolidated), up 16.3% YoY; order intake INR570 crore (+18.8%); open order book INR1,043 crore (+46.9%). EBIT INR75 crore at 17.9% margin vs FY26 full-year EBIT margin of 18.8%; mix 54% catalogue / 46% engineered.

segments.name: MHE division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crore (-2.9% YoY) on project execution delays for power-sector orders; order intake INR185 crore (+38.1%); open order book INR475 crore (+18.8%). EBIT INR27 crore at about 25.6% margin vs FY26 full-year 24.7%; secured overseas port order of about INR21 crore.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crore (+21.9% YoY), led by Middle East and US; overseas order intake INR194 crore (+63%), including INR21 crore from MHE; overseas open order book INR256 crore (+73%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided to low double-digit percentage, described as conservative given macro uncertainty; management said it could be revisited next quarter.
Consolidated EBITDA margin to be maintained at the FY26 level (about 21%).
Gear division EBITDA margin guided to about 24%; gear EBIT margin expected around 19-20% over the next year and one year after.
MHE sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for the year.
Exports expected to grow at least double digits in FY27; Europe recovery expected to take at least two quarters.
Mid-term FY30 revenue target of INR5,000 crore described as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue.
Gear revenue conversion expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as stabilised prices are accepted; Q2 to show only gradual pick-up.
capex_capacity: Previously announced capex programme of approximately INR400 crore over FY26 to FY28 stated as on track; further capex under evaluation for board approval in near future.
Assembly centres outside India (Middle East, US and others) set up for customer proximity; some sub-assemblies locally outsourced.

Defence business has dedicated manufacturing and operating vertical built over the last 3-4 years; defence orders expected to execute over 2-3 years with working capital about 15-20% higher than the gear average.
Gear manufacturing cycle is 2-3 months for catalogue products and 4-5 months for engineered products.
demand_pricing: Gear order intake drivers: power (about 27% of order intake, including a large single order flagged in Q4 FY26), steel, cement and MHE; catalogue vs engineered order mix 27% / 73% in the quarter.

Raw-material BOM cost up about 5% on average (steel 5-7%, bearings 6-7%, fabricated gear cases about 7%, tooling 6-10%); most Q1 orders accepted with price increases and raw materials locked back-to-back on order acceptance.
Management attributed slower conversion to a sharp raw-material price increase that lengthened enquiry-to-order cycles, and to competitors holding low-cost inventory that pressured quotes.

MHE margin decline attributed to about 2.5-3% from input costs, about 3% from sales mix, and about 3% from lower throughput; MHE delays linked to design-engineering clearances on two large power-sector orders routed through EPC contractors.
Middle East growth came from orders on hold in Q4 FY26 that resumed dispatch; Middle East weakness mainly in cement and mining and minerals; Europe weak.
Sugar outlook muted due to prolonged monsoon; defence orders showed no significant update in the last 90 days; aerospace certification not being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the MHE margin fall is mix versus input costs, and what is sustainable MHE margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the decline into about 2.5-3% input costs, about 3% sales mix and about 3% lower volume; sustainable MHE EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gear revenue growth lagging order book growth and why only low double-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw-material spikes slowed enquiry-to-order conversion; about INR70 crore of finished goods could not be recognised as sales in Q1 because title transfer criteria were not met by 30 June; Q2 expected only gradual pick-up, with Q3-Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Can gear costs be passed on given the small share of gear in customer capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PSU-linked demand (thermal power, cement, steel) is sensitive to budgets; Q1 was a correction phase in pricing, with Q2 expected to be an acceptance phase. About INR160 crore of the gear order book extends beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for gear standalone margins and does the business return to mid-20s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gear EBITDA to about 24% and gear EBIT around 19-20% over the next year and one year beyond, versus 18.8% EBIT in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 aspiration and segment split?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR5,000 crore FY30 revenue target was reiterated as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue; Gear includes marine.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital impact of defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders over 2-3 years carry higher working capital days, about 15-20% above the gear average in past similar orders, which management said would be absorbed by higher margins.

505700|2026-09.headline: Elecon Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% YoY to INR639 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 23.1%; FY27 guided to mid-double-digit growth.
505700|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue grew 10.5% YoY to INR639 crore, up 22.7% QoQ from INR521 crore, with EBITDA up 17.7% to INR148 crore and margin up 140 bps to 23.1%. Gear revenue rose 10.6% to INR488 crore, led by 30.3% overseas growth, while MHE revenue rose 10.4% to INR151 crore with MHE EBIT margin about 20.2% in Q2. Management attributed domestic softness to monsoon-related project slowness, steel price volatility and delayed project clearances, and said orders are firm and dispatch should pick up after Diwali. Management guided to medium double-digit consolidated revenue growth for H2 FY27 (around 15%) with minimum EBITDA margin at FY26 level.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Open order books are up 37% in Gear (INR1,056 crore) and 27.3% in MHE (INR579 crore), and overseas order intake rose to INR230 crore in Q2 from INR172 crore a year earlier, supporting around 15% H2 revenue growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

505726|2026-03.headline: IFB Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.0% to INR 1,456 crore and PAT to INR 33.7 crore, but FY26 commodity and forex hits of INR 84 crore were only partly offset.

PAT rose to INR 33.7 crore from INR 22.3 crore after a INR 0.58 crore Labour Code exceptional charge. For FY26, revenue grew 10% to INR 5,476 crore, while PAT rose 3.5% to INR 133.3 crore and PAT margin fell to 2.4% from 2.6%. Management said INR 67 crore of the INR 84 crore FY26 commodity and forex hit was recovered through cost initiatives and price increases. April-May commodity and forex headwinds of about INR 49 crore are only partly offset (INR 29 crore from cost initiatives so far).

505726|2026-06.headline: IFB Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.65% to INR 1,529 crore, with PAT up to INR 38.06 crore, but commodity and forex costs were not passed on.
505726|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.65% YoY to INR 1,529 crore and PBDIT rose 26.46% to INR 88.46 crore, with margin at 5.79% of revenue versus 5.34%. PAT was INR 38.06 crore (2.5% of revenue) against INR 25.36 crore a year earlier. Management said commodity and forex headwinds are not behind the company and that it has not been able to pass them on in price, relying instead on cost initiatives (INR 42-43 crore in Q1). Home Appliances (HAD) revenue grew about 18%, with July described as good, while gross margin fell about 160 bps.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Sales up 17% YoY and above budget; EBITDA in line with budget. Management expects similar growth going forward, with festive season supportive. Stated FY ambition of about INR 2,000 crore revenue; current base about INR 1,000-1,100 crore.

505729|2026-03.headline: Singer India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 37% to Rs 166.3 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 557 crore, up 29%, led by Sewing Machines.
505729|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 166.3 crore (up 37%), PBT of Rs 8 crore (up 43%) and EBITDA of Rs 9.3 crore (up 49%). For FY26, revenue was Rs 557 crore (up 29%), EBITDA Rs 21.5 crore (up 70%) and PBT Rs 17.3 crore (up 73%), after a one-time labour code cost of Rs 73 lakh; adjusted EBITDA was Rs 22.2 crore and adjusted PBT Rs 18.1 crore. Sewing Machines drove growth, while Appliances revenue grew about 10% in Q4 but its segment result fell by about Rs 2 crore. Management gave no formal guidance and did not answer questions on promoter exit or M&A.

segments.name: Sewing Machines
segments.commentary: Grew about 45% in Q4 and more than 40% for FY26; trade channel up about 20% in Q4 and over 15% for the year. Zigzag up over 30%, industrial up over 13% in Q4 and over 20% for FY26, cast-iron straight stitch and accessories up over 50% for the year. E-commerce up over 50% in Q4 and about 30% for the year.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% in Q4 on e-commerce range and fans, but segment result was lower by about Rs 2 crore due to EPR costs and fan business build-out. Demand muted, trade inventory blocked, dealer cash flows tight.

segments.name: Fans
segments.commentary: Fan business grew about 50% in Q4 with a new range covering economy, base, decorative, BLDC, TPW and exhaust fans; supply chain constrained by labour shortage and cost inflation.

505790|2026-09.headline: Schaeffler India says automotive demand is growing about 29-30% on GST 2.0 and localization is at 80%, with no explicit numbers on Q2 FY27 financials.
505790|2026-09.overview: This was an investor group meeting (Sept 28, 2026), not a formal results call, so no quarterly financial figures were given. Management said automotive growth of roughly 29-30% was driven by GST 2.0 and BS-VI product transitions, while industrial growth was mixed, with infrastructure, steel, cement and railways strong and construction equipment and mining weak. Exports were framed as a by-product of localization, with management targeting 15-20% of revenue from exports. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input costs, with about 70% of cost increases typically recovered from customers, and that Vitesco's India integration has no timeline. E-mobility was described as loss-making and early-stage, with adoption under 5% today and about 15% expected by FY31.

segments.commentary: Growing about 29-30%, driven by GST 2.0 demand uplift and BS-VI new clutch and engine systems; management says the West Asia crisis affects automotive only through input costs, not demand.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Mixed: steel, cement and infrastructure strong, renewables (wind) growing, railways booming; construction equipment fell last year and mining has not recovered; industrial growth described as single digit.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: About 13-14% of revenue, expected to keep growing at double digits for at least six months; benefits from full electrification via insulation-coated traction motor bearings, which the company says it makes 100% locally.

segments.name: E-mobility
segments.commentary: Small base with strong growth on e-axle wins; currently loss-making, with e-axle content 100% imported and Phase 2 localization under way; industry EV adoption below 5% today.

segments.commentary: Company says it holds about half the Indian wind bearings market; 1.6 m bearing produced last quarter for 6 MW turbines, and Savli Hall 3 under construction. No direct wind exports; about 85% of turbine output is exported by customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook given geopolitical tensions, and what is the geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 50% Europe (intercompany), 25% Southeast Asia, with the rest China and the Americas; 13% of exports go to China. Exports are a by-product of localization, with the company expecting 15-20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does the West Asia conflict affect costs and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the crisis hits industrial exports and input costs (fuel, LPG), not automotive demand. About 70% of cost increases are typically recovered, with the remaining 30% absorbed by efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Where does Vitesco stand and is there an integration timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no legal hurdle, but there is no timeline. Parent holds 74.13%, with 26% public; the group must integrate Vitesco entities worldwide first.

qa_highlights.question: How are EV economics and competition shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: EV is loss-making at start; profitability depends on volume. EV adoption is below 5% today and about 15% by 2030-31 per internal research; hybrids are expected at about 15% by 2031.

qa_highlights.question: Is Vitesco's e-axle content imported, and what does Vitesco bring?
qa_highlights.answer: The e-axle is a Schaeffler portfolio product, with the CFO noting 100% import content at Phase 1. Vitesco adds BMS, sensors (NOx, knock) and power electronics; 800-volt capability is now under development.

qa_highlights.question: Is railway demand secular or lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tendering-driven lumpiness will persist; electrification and the move to larger loads (Vande Bharat, freight Class K bearings) add structural demand.

505872|2026-03.headline: WPIL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 11% YoY to INR511 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 3% to INR1,855 crore and EBITDA margin reached 17.16%.

506222|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores and PAT rose 58.6% to INR84.3 crores, despite total income down 6.3%.
506222|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income fell 6.3% to INR658 crores while EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores, with margin up 734 bps to 19.2%. Management attributed the stronger profitability to product mix (lower GPPS volumes) and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, and said there was no significant inventory gain. Volumes fell 4.6% YoY to 46.1 KT, driven by GPPS weakness, while ABS and HIPS grew. Management declined to quantify the Thailand breakeven change or the power-savings benefit, citing short-term market distortion from the Middle East supply crisis, and reiterated that India ABS capacity additions remain on track for the second half of FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven targets should not change; short-term tightness gains are arbitrage that may not last. Thailand still needs to reach 60-70% utilisation to generate returns.

qa_highlights.answer: India dip was from GPPS only; ABS and HIPS grew YoY. Thailand comparison was distorted by prior-year pre-buying ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch, and Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker. Most business was retained.

qa_highlights.answer: Contract and formula margins are similar or slightly better. Spot margins are better for specific grades where Korean suppliers' quality is weak, but this is opportunistic.

qa_highlights.answer: ABS: 60-70% formula or contract. HIPS: well above 50% formula/OEM. GPPS: formula-based pricing above 70% for the business overall, with volumes dropping as the company avoids unformulated segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thailand ever reach breakeven given normalised spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that returns start at 60-70% utilisation and the plant is still below that level.

506222|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
506222|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.

segments.commentary: Hit harder than ABS, mainly in the non-OEM/unorganised segment; OEM is about 50% of PS sales. Management did not give volume numbers.

segments.commentary: Merchant sales run at about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a year against roughly 100,000 tonnes of capacity; most output is used captively, and merchant sales will continue after the ABS expansion.

506395|2026-03.headline: Coromandel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR 494 crore, but reported PAT fell to INR 115 crore on last year's land-sale gain.

segments.name: Fertilizers (DAP/NPK/SSP/Nano)
segments.commentary: Record fertilizer production of 3.5 million tons and record DAP+NPK sales of 4.3 million tons (+7%), with 17.5% phosphatic market share; Q4 fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA was below INR 3,500 per ton versus over INR 5,000 per ton last year. SSP sales hit a record 8.4 lakh tons, and Nano DAP volumes grew 60% to about 42 lakh bottles.

segments.name: Crop protection (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to INR 3,054 crore and profit 55% to INR 569 crore for FY26; FY26 revenue mix was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore. Q4 standalone crop protection growth was about 2%, attributed to export sales being moved into Q1 and a bio export order shipped earlier.

segments.name: NACL (Nagarjuna Agrichem, 53% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated crop protection with NACL reached about INR 4,000 crore; NACL FY26 revenue INR 1,585 crore (+28%) and EBITDA INR 103 crore, with margin at 6-7% and guided to 9-10% next year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew over 30% in FY26 with more than 300 new stores in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and entry into Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.name: Dhaksha (drones, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Impairment of INR 71 crore taken on investments and goodwill due to long lead times in order execution; management expects recovery after first large order executes this year.

guidance_outlook: Crop protection (standalone) revenue growth guided at 20-25% for the coming year, with domestic formulations growing 20-25% and six new product launches.
Sarigam active ingredient expansion of 20,000 tons is due around mid-2026 with payback under two years; Dahej Mancozeb debottlenecking of 10,000 tons has payback under one year.
Granulation capacity expansion expected to commission by December 2026.
Rock phosphate output in Senegal to rise 30-40% in FY27 from more than 3.5 lakh tons in FY26.
Trading margin of roughly 4-5% per ton; trading volumes may fall in Q1 FY27 on DAP availability, with second-half recovery expected.
Management declined to give fertilizer EBITDA per ton or margin guidance for FY27, citing fluid conditions and pending subsidy compensation.
Raw material cover secured for Q1 FY27; Q2 cover depends on Middle East resolution. Sulphur visibility is up to June.
capex_capacity: Kakinada: 2,000 tpd sulphuric acid and 650 tpd phosphoric acid plant commissioned in March 2026 (about 200,000 tons per year phosphoric acid); in trial runs, with stable operations expected from April-May 2026.
Dahej: technical plant commissioned in FY26 and Mancozeb capacity expanded by 10,000 tons; Sarigam expansion of 20,000 tons under way.
Technical MAP plant and seaweed granulation capacity under development.
Fluorination chemistry investment planned for CDMO opportunity; small-scale capacity to be created this year, production next year.
Coromandel has invested over INR 3,000 crore across segments in the last two years.
Coromandel's stake in the Senegal mining company increased to 71.5%.
demand_pricing: Industry: IMD forecasts below-normal monsoon for kharif 2026, though key southern markets are likely to see normal rainfall; updated IMD forecast due in late May.
NBS rates for kharif 2026 raised about 10% for N, P and S, which management said do not reflect the sharp rise in raw material prices and rupee depreciation.
Ammonia and sulphur are trading around USD 840-850 and USD 800 per ton respectively; phosphoric acid price for the quarter fixed at USD 1,360 versus USD 1,290 previously.
Q4 rupee range of 89.75-95.23 per USD; management said depreciation helps the crop protection export business.
Crop protection raw materials said to be covered, with input cost increases passed through; Mancozeb cost increases passed through to customers.
Rabi season demand was muted due to late monsoon withdrawal, with lower-than-expected liquidation.
Unique grades remained at about 35% of fertilizer sales on an annualized basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between consolidated and standalone P&L, and how will BMCC's depreciation and profitability evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BMCC (mining) has turned profitable on better volumes and fixed-cost absorption, and the gap is mainly consolidation amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, not operating loss.

qa_highlights.question: How will fertilizer margins hold up given only about a 10% NBS increase against sharp raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking additional subsidy and cost-to-cost reimbursement for June-September, with discussions at an early stage; it declined to quantify the amount. Any remaining gap may be passed on through MRP corrections, and industry has already made some MRP corrections in the last one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the crop protection growth, margin and NACL margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone crop protection targets 20-25% revenue growth with margins sustained near 19%; NACL margin improved to 6-7%, can reach 9-10% next year, and restoring 7-8% needs no major investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year split of subsidy versus non-subsidy EBITDA and of crop protection revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy share of EBITDA was 57% in Q4 and 66% for FY26. Standalone FY26 crop protection revenue was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore; NACL FY26 revenue was INR 1,584 crore and Q4 INR 361 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertilizer finished goods inventory and trading exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished fertilizer inventory is about 5.5 lakh tons, of which trading is about 60,000-70,000 tons. Trading margin is roughly 4-5%, and FY27 trading volume may fall in Q1 because of DAP import shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone crop protection growth only about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is off-season, export sales were deliberately moderated to shift into April-May, and a bio export order was executed earlier in December; full-year crop protection growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sulphur and ammonia sourcing position, and is Q2 covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur has visibility up to June, with diversified spot sourcing from Canada, South Asia and Japan; ammonia and sulphur prices are about USD 800-850 per ton. Management said Q2 coverage depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Dhaksha, the drone subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical gaps are fixed and a large order is awaiting execution, with the first order this year expected to build confidence; a larger facility is due around May 2026.

506395|2026-06.headline: Coromandel Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 3% YoY to INR761 crores on West Asia input-cost spike, while revenue rose 15% to INR8,215 crores.
506395|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 15% YoY to INR8,215 crores, helped by higher fertilizer realisations and non-subsidy growth, with NACL now consolidated. EBITDA declined 3% to INR761 crores and net profit fell to INR382 crores from INR502 crores as ammonia and sulphur costs outran NBS subsidy rates. Management said phosphate production was deliberately cut to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to protect inventory economics, while Crop Protection (revenue +20%, EBIT +44%) and Retail (revenue +85%) carried the quarter. Management is pressing the government for a kharif NBS revision and says no near-term fertilizer capacity additions are planned.

segments.name: Fertilizers (phosphatic)
segments.commentary: Production cut to 6.9 lakh tons from 8.4 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to optimise inventory; phos acid output 1.2 lakh tons, flat YoY. Sales volume fell 9-10% to 10 lakh tons, but primary market share rose to 22% from 18%; point-of-sale up 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, 16% share.

segments.name: Specialty nutrients and organics
segments.commentary: Described as strong, aided by higher organics and micronutrient offtake; launched 3 new products. Management says this business grows 25-30% with about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Record Q1: revenue +20% to INR870 crores, EBIT +44% to INR159 crores, with exports and B2B strong. New products are 32% of domestic B2C sales vs 23% last year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +85% YoY; 76% of stores profitable vs 61% last year; 22 new stores take network above 1,200 outlets.

segments.name: Nano and bio products
segments.commentary: Nano business volumes +2% YoY with nearly 60% market share; UP and Maharashtra bans are restraining growth. Bio business steady, with 2 new products launched.

guidance_outlook: Phosphoric acid price for Q2 settled at $1,700/t vs $1,360/t in Q1, following higher DAP and raw-material prices.
Granulation project on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27; Crop Protection capacity expansion for key molecules expected by September 2026.

Management wants kharif NBS rates revised to the 6-month average policy formula; says the industry has taken a 25-30% price increase across grades, and that further price rises are not feasible without subsidy correction.
Sulphur expected to stay high for some time; management says the acid-backed production economics are unattractive until sulphur falls, with NACL-type steady-state EBITDA well below Coromandel.

No near-term fertilizer capacity additions planned; target is 4 million tons own fertilizer plus 1 million tons trading, with management citing 8-9 million tons of nutrient visibility for about 2 years.
Normal sustainable capex guided at about INR300 crores per year; ~INR7,000 crores invested over the last 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Phos acid and sulphuric acid plants commissioned; sulphuric acid at rated capacity and generating power; phos acid stabilising with a new rock-utilisation technology.
Granulation project on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; new capacity is 750,000 tonnes, 50% to be sold via own retail and the balance into UP, Rajasthan, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Crop Protection key-molecule capacity to be commissioned by September 2026; further spending to focus on marketing and channel rather than assets; no new AI capacity planned given spare NACL capacity.
Senegal rock mining produced over 1.1 lakh tons in the quarter; BMCC operating close to 5 lakh tons/year target; evaluating a 100,000-150,000 ton SSP plant at $5-6 million.

Kakinada T-MAP plant and seaweed granulation plant progressing; Ankleshwar fluorination launch facility being set up; IIT Chennai research park planned; PA-SA plant gives about 60% acid self-sufficiency.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit was 23% through the quarter, moderating to 17% by late July; reservoirs at 34% of capacity vs 57% last year. Pulses acreage down 15%, oilseeds and cotton down 6%, and paddy back to normal.
Management says there is no fertilizer shortage; Urea and DAP stocks are comfortable for kharif, but industry production and imports must hold for two more months to build rabi carryover.
NP/NPK production and imports fell 21% and 38% respectively; management ties this to weak NBS subsidy for these grades.
Crop protection: domestic demand muted due to delayed sowing; export markets improving but cautious on price. Active ingredient prices are firmer than before because China keeps AIs low.
NACL export revenue hit by price moderation on molecules sold to global MNCs, while Coromandel passed input-cost increases through to exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a structural shift to NPK or a fertilizer shortage on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortage; the early-season pick-up of low-MRP packs was an advance purchase, and current uptake depends more on monsoon than on availability.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FX contribute to Crop Protection EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX is at most 5-6% of consolidated EBITDA, under a netting-based hedging policy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the depreciation spike and how much is from new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental depreciation from new capex is about INR16-18 crores; the rest is mining overburden amortisation (about INR30 crores) and NACL intangibles amortisation (about INR20-21 crores).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ask from government and how is the EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants the 6-month average NBS rate applied, and says NP/NPK rates need significant correction; the target is nutrient EBITDA of about INR6,500/t from INR5,000/t, but not in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided normal sustainable capex of about INR300 crores, but will consider higher spending for attractive-return projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dhaksha drone contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Coromandel bought 100-150 drones this quarter and targets a fleet of 500 during the year; management said Dhaksha is not a significant EBITDA drag.

risks_watch: Subsidy under-recovery on NP/NPK: sulphur and ammonia costs are not covered by NBS rates, and kharif revision is still pending.
Sulphur and phos acid pricing: phos acid up to $1,700/t in Q2; management says sulphur needs to fall to about $800/t for backward integration to pay.
Subsidy receivable of INR3,254 crores at June-end.
State bans on Nano fertilizers in UP and Maharashtra are holding back volumes.
Crop Protection export pricing: AI prices are firmer, but export demand is cautious and NACL revenue fell on price moderation.
Whether industry production and imports can hold through the next two months to build rabi carryover inventory.

rows.why: NACL EBITDA margin rose to 11% from 8% in Q1 (EBITDA INR41 crores, +9%), and management guides a path from 3-4% to 7-8% and then 10-11%.

rows.why: Nano volumes grew only 2% YoY despite nearly 60% market share, with the state bans restraining growth and no lifting signalled on the call.

506401|2026-03.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 13% YoY to INR383 crore, margin 18%, with PAT INR220 crore; management guides Q1 FY27 better than Q4.
506401|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,127 crore, down from INR2,202 crore a year earlier but up from INR1,983 crore in Q3, while EBITDA rose 74% QoQ and 13% YoY to INR383 crore. Phenolics EBIT reached INR287 crore at a 20% margin, and Advanced Intermediates EBIT rose to INR34 crore. Management attributed the gains to favourable pricing, feedstock bought on dips before the Middle East disruption, and integration benefits. The nitric acid plant ran at about 45% utilisation in Q4 because of technical issues, so the expected INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition is delayed.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR708 crore vs INR654 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR652 crore in Q3; EBIT INR34 crore vs INR15 crore in Q3. Gains came from stable volumes, end-product pricing and product mix, while exports slowed on logistics disruption.

segments.name: Phenolics
