qa_highlights.question: What was nitric acid utilisation in Q4 and is the INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant was at about 45% utilisation in Q4 due to technical issues; the balance was bought from the market. Target achievable once stable, but no timeline given. Concentrated nitric acid plant operating normally.

qa_highlights.question: Phenolics feedstock availability and China-India spread outlook for Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance was preponed by about 10-11 days in early April; intermediate stock covered supply. Management guided Q1 profitability higher than Q4 and expects no propylene constraint. Declined to comment on other companies' spreads.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products and fluorinated molecule add to FY27 standalone performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Validation batches are supplied or in transit to customers; commercial production on a regular basis from Q3 FY27. Management did not anticipate customer approval concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved some customers to dealership and CSA models to secure outstanding amounts amid volatility, and said realisations, not capacity utilisation, are the lower metric in Advanced Intermediates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China nitration tailwind already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCP-led safety and transport audit is a structural tailwind, not tied to a specific province or product, and that it has already started happening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the polycarbonate project (about INR11,000 crore) be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Upadhyay: debt tied up with banks at 60:40; equity is being infused, and debt will be drawn after 25% equity per the bank condition. Management said funding is not an issue and cash generation is sufficient.

Feedstock cost volatility (benzene, xylene, toluene, propylene); inventory bought on dips is expected to support costs only until around mid-Q2 FY27.
Working capital: receivable days rose, and some customers have moved to dealership and CSA models.

Geopolitical risks in the Middle East and the US tariff and China policy environment.

rows.why: Management declined to give volumes; Advanced Intermediates capacity is reported as running full and domestic demand is stable, but phenol ordering is mixed and export revenue fell with logistics disruption (export INR292 crore in Q4).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is weak at about 45% in the nitric acid plant, and the INR11,000 crore PC project and Praxair BOO HyCO plant already absorb the capex agenda, so a new capex announcement is not signalled and the funding is 60:40 with debt drawn after 25% equity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides Q1 FY27 better than Q4 (Q4 EBITDA INR383 crore) and expects no propylene constraint, but it is cautious about extrapolating the current quarter and feedstock costs are volatile.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Nitric acid plant at about 45% utilisation delays the INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition, feedstock inventory support fades by mid-Q2 FY27, and receivable days rose as some customers moved to dealership/CSA models.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New products and fluorinated molecules are in validation batches with commercial production on a regular basis from Q3 FY27, in time for CY2026 export customer requirements, and management did not anticipate customer approval concerns.

rows.label: China nitration structural tailwind (DASDA, OBA)
rows.why: Management says China's CCP-led safety and transport audits on nitration chemistries are a structural tailwind that has already started, but no volume or price numbers were given.

rows.label: Receivable days rising, shift to dealership/CSA models
rows.why: Receivable days rose and some customers were moved to dealership and CSA models to secure outstanding amounts amid volatility, with no receivable-day figure disclosed.

rows.label: Feedstock bought on dips supports costs until mid-Q2 FY27
rows.when: until about end-Q2 FY27 or mid-Q2 FY27
rows.why: Inventory bought before the Middle East disruption is expected to cushion costs until price stabilisation, after which the cost tailwind fades.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 FY27 being better than Q4 and on a stronger FY27 standalone margin, but evasive on nitric acid timing, IPA and phenol volumes, and the China-India spread, and analysts pressed on those specifics.

506401|2026-06.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
506401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.
demand_pricing: Management said phenol demand in India is roughly balanced with no new global capacity, and some supply is short. Imports were duty-free for most of Q1 until the government reimposed the duty.
Raw material costs were high in April, but procurement secured feedstock for continuous operations. Management said feedstock costs are competitive domestically and globally.
Freight and insurance costs rose. The company responded with CIF to FOB shifts, larger parcels, and a product reformulation for a Middle East customer that changed its hazard class.
Consolidated export mix is about 20%. AI is roughly 50-50 domestic to export; Phenolics is almost entirely domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Did phenol run rate reach 1 lakh tonnes per quarter, and how is propylene covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 lakh tonnes was a run rate reached in significant periods, not the full quarter, because of raw material sourcing and a short maintenance shutdown. Debottlenecking is aimed at the 4 lakh tonne mark in the short to medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Phenolics spread in Q1 and outlook for Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose spreads and said Deepak buys feedstock below international index levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the phenol capacity now exceed earlier maturity assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main change was confidence. Advanced process controls, costing about INR 80-100 crore cumulatively, enabled higher throughput, with INR 70-odd crore more planned for debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol supply-demand balance sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new capacity, China is largely self-sufficient, demand is balanced and India is short of supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt and capex plan for the INR 11,500 crore project?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore has been spent. Peak borrowing is about INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, for total peak debt of INR 8,000-8,500 crore. Management said D/E will stay below 1x.

qa_highlights.question: Could you quantify incremental revenue and EBITDA margin from the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, but said the margin profile of new products is in line with or above the AI average.

risks_watch: Phenol throughput depends on propylene and feedstock availability; April showed how a shutdown and raw material shortage can cut volumes.
Ramp-up timing for the Q2 AI projects and the MIBC run rate; management said the alkylation and multipurpose plants slipped because of manpower and gas shortages.
Polycarbonate and BPA commissioning (H2 FY28-29) and the debt drawdown schedule.
Freight and insurance costs and the reimposed phenol import duty could change domestic realisations.
Management declined to give Phenolics spreads, AI product-level margins, and the MIBK/acetone ratio, so these remain unverified.
506401|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the phenol and integration outlook, but guarded on spreads, margins and specific product economics, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Timelines for the polycarbonate project and the AI ramp-up were described as on track but were given loosely.
key_quotes: We're no longer a nitration company that buys nitric acid. We're now a nitrogen company that nitrates.
I think the only thing that has changed is confidence.
So there is a short supply today, if I can tell you.
So, when I said 1 lakh tonnes, what I meant was on a run rate basis.
We are approved with what one would call sunrise sectors.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 21% vs 18% in Q4 FY26 and 11% a year ago, but April was hit by shutdown, propylene shortage and gas curtailment, and management declined to quantify Phenolics spreads or AI product margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 for MIBK/MIBC and remaining AI projects; phenol push
rows.why: MIBK and MIBC commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026 and the rest due in Q2 FY27, while phenol debottlenecking from 3.5 to 4 lakh t/yr (14% size uplift) is funded at about INR 70 crore, though the 1 lakh t/quarter run rate was not sustained through Q1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Phenol run rate has touched about 1 lakh t per quarter (about 4 lakh t/yr) in parts of Q1 and management targets 4 lakh t/yr, with Q1 revenue up 35% YoY, while management says there is no new global phenol capacity and India is short of supply.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was given, and management described Q1 as partly disrupted with April affected by shutdown and feedstock shortages, so there is no clear basis for a formal raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The AI alkylation and multipurpose plants slipped on manpower and gas shortages, the reimposed phenol import duty could move domestic realisations, and polycarbonate timing (H2 FY28-29) was given loosely.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MIBK and MIBC are commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026, the multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility is due in Q2 FY27 with commercial volumes from January, but management declined to quantify their revenue or margin.

rows.label: Polycarbonate and BPA commissioning (propylene-polycarbonate project, INR 11,500
rows.why: Debt is closed and funded 60:40 with 25% equity already in, INR 1,200 crore spent to date and about INR 3,000 crore planned for FY28, but commissioning is only loosely timed.

rows.label: Peak debt INR 8,000-8,500 crore, D/E below 1x
rows.why: Current D/E is 0.27x on INR 6,214 crore net worth, with management saying D/E will stay below 1x even at peak debt.

rows.label: Freight and import duty pressure on domestic realisations
rows.why: Freight and insurance costs rose and phenol import duty was reimposed after being waived for most of Q1, which could change domestic realisations.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter, the phenol supply-demand balance and the integration outlook, but declined to quantify Phenolics spreads, AI product margins and new-product economics; analysts pushed on spreads, propylene coverage and the phenol run rate.

506405|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 177 crore from INR 150 crore QoQ, mostly raw-material pass-through; FY26 revenue INR 582 crore.
506405|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the quarter's sharp top-line rise to pass-through of higher sulfur and boron raw-material prices rather than volume, and said absolute margins were maintained though percentage margins fell. Sulfur supply was constrained by Middle East/Hormuz disruption, and the Roha plant ran at about 60% capacity for roughly 15 days in March before supply was restored. Working capital and short-term borrowings rose substantially on higher inventory, debtor and advance-payment requirements for boron, at about 8.75-9% interest. Management declined to give quantified guidance beyond saying FY27 specialty utilisation should be better than FY26.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 150 crore in the previous quarter (QoQ)
described as one of the highest top lines in the company

financial_highlights.metric: Interest rate on incremental working capital lines

financial_highlights.change: described as well within industry norms

segments.name: Sulfur / sulfuric acid (bulk chemicals)
segments.commentary: Dahej running at about 95% capacity per management; Roha slowed to about 60% for roughly 15 days in March due to imported sulfur shortage. Each site keeps about 15-20 days (about 1,500 tons) of sulfur inventory. Both plants have roughly 350 tons per day sulfuric acid capacity.

segments.name: Boron chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 H1 output was lost due to boron ore supply disruption from Turkey; plants were back at full capacity in H2 with adequate stock now. Company moved from credit purchases to paying advances with 90-120 day supply lead times, raising working capital.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Europe business declining; growth in Latin America (replacing most lost European volume), with sales to China and Japan. Specialty portfolio is below management's 50% target; the company reports a single segment only.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to project FY27 utilisation, calling the situation too volatile; said it expects specialty capacity utilisation to be better than FY25-26.
Plants currently operating at capacity with no restriction, per management, but situation described as highly dynamic.
Supply chain would take a few months to normalise even if Strait of Hormuz reopens; prices expected to keep rising until supply eases.
Management does not expect boron/borax distressed selling to continue, though overall non-boric demand is lower until gas supply normalises in Morbi and other ceramic/glass centres.
Long-term target: specialty portfolio at least 50% of revenue; previous mix was about 30% commodities and 60-70% bulk chemicals at name change.
capex_capacity: Dahej expansion undertaken earlier to increase manufacturing footprint and sulfuric acid volumes.
Roha plant reduced to about 60% capacity in March 2026 due to imported sulfur unavailability; now back to normal.
Some specialty products in boron and an enhanced-oil-recovery polymer product have started commercial sales; no volume or margin projections given.
Research pipeline: several specialties expected to reach commercial stage in FY27 or FY28, unquantified.

Land parcel near Ambernath (Nalimbi), declared forest land; Supreme Court ruled in company's favour but Maharashtra government has not transferred title, so monetisation is blocked. Proceeds could go to capex or debt reduction.
demand_pricing: Sulfur supply remains short; prices at all-time highs, partly from new Indonesian nickel smelter demand (about 3 million tons) before the war and then Hormuz disruption.
Specialty pricing passed through with a lag because contracts are quarterly and negotiated in advance; margins expected to average out over time.
Non-boric borax/frit demand weak in Morbi and similar centres due to gas shortages and customer stock liquidation, causing glut and distressed pricing.
Chinese sulfuric acid export restrictions; management sees customers seeking diversification away from China, but no significant single order won yet.
Sulfuric acid is low margin; company limited by specialty market access, not production, so it does not prioritise sulfuric acid sales over captive use.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Roha's disruption cost in volume or revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha was slowed to about 60% capacity for roughly 15 days in March rather than shut down, as imports were unavailable; no quantification given. Dahej has domestic sulfur sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: What interest rate and when does working capital ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental lines cost about 8.75-9%; the issue is absolute quantum, not rate, driven by higher stock values, debtors and boron advances. No date given for easing.

qa_highlights.question: Latin America progress and pass-through of raw-material inflation in specialty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says most lost European business has been replaced by Latin American business; Japan, Korea and China are being explored. Specialty prices pass through with a lag due to quarterly contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Ambernath land monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Land is actually near Ambernath at Nalimbi, forest land with a favourable Supreme Court order, but state has not transferred title, so no monetisation yet; options being examined.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report specialty vs bulk margins separately, and when is it a true specialty company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep reporting a single chemicals segment, saying the split would be subjective; it considers 50% specialty share the right threshold for a specialty identity.

qa_highlights.question: R&D intensity and plans?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is mainly process development and largely people cost; management said plans to increase R&D spend will show in coming quarters, with no figures given.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 utilisation and sulfur inventory cost?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 projection given; sulfur inventory kept at 15-20 days (about 1,500 tons per site); management did not disclose purchase or current sulfur prices.

risks_watch: Sulfur availability and price: Hormuz disruption; supply may take months to normalise even after reopening.
Working capital and short-term borrowing build-up; interest cost rising on the larger absolute debt.
Roha dependence on imported sulfur; utilisation may fall again if imports stay unavailable.
Non-boric borax and frit demand weak until gas supply in consuming centres normalises.
Europe specialty business shrinking; replacement depends on Latin America, Japan, Korea and China developments.
Low specialty share versus 50% target, and limited R&D spend, questioned by analysts.
Ambernath/Nalimbi land monetisation timing depends on state government title transfer.
506405|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and cautious on near-term visibility: management repeatedly declined to give forward projections, citing volatility. Confident about supply recovery and pricing pass-through at a qualitative level, but evasive on quantification of disruption, margins by product and R&D plans.
key_quotes: We will continue to report a single segment.
It's really my style not to give futuristic projections.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 revenue rise of INR 177 crore vs INR 150 crore was mainly price pass-through rather than volume, and Latin America is replacing lost European volume, but no volume number was given.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Several research specialties are expected to reach commercial stage in FY27 or FY28, and boron specialties and an enhanced-oil-recovery polymer have just started sales, but none are quantified.

rows.label: Latin America replacing lost European specialty volume

rows.why: The Supreme Court ruled in the company's favour, but Maharashtra has not transferred title, so no monetisation or proceeds are expected in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident that supply and pricing pass-through would recover at a qualitative level, but cautious and evasive on FY27 utilisation, disruption cost, margins by product and R&D; analysts pushed on working capital, the low specialty share versus the 50% target and limited R&D.

506590|2026-03.headline: PCBL Q4 FY26 carbon black volume rose 8% YoY to 161,865 MT while consolidated EBITDA was INR248 crores; management guides double-digit FY27 EBITDA growth.
506590|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by the West Asia conflict, which raised raw material, packing, freight and logistics costs and disrupted export routes. Consolidated revenue was INR2,066 crores and EBITDA INR248 crores, with carbon black domestic volume up 21% YoY and international volume down 10%. FY26 revenue fell to INR8,189 crores and EBITDA to INR1,081 crores from INR1,384 crores. Management says spreads have found a floor, pass-through and spot price hikes are under way, and net borrowings fell by INR454 crores to INR4,536 crores.

financial_highlights.change: -INR454 crores in FY26; INR750 crores capex funded

segments.name: Carbon black (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 161,865 MT (+8% YoY); tyres 88,591 tons, performance chemicals 53,888 tons, specialty 19,386 tons (+26% YoY). Management says EBITDA per ton was flat QoQ, so the QoQ EBITDA jump was mainly volume-driven.

segments.name: Aquapharm
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,443 crores and EBITDA INR162 crores; Q4 EBITDA INR29 crores on significantly lower capacity utilisation. FY26 volume 94,445 MT; home care +11%, water solutions -12%, oil and gas -19%, application-specific solutions +18%.

segments.name: Power generation
segments.commentary: Q4 generation rose 12% YoY to 196 MUs (175 MUs in Q4 FY25); external sales 116 MUs vs 100 MUs. FY26 generation up about 14% and sales volume up 17%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit EBITDA growth as volumes recover, cost and pricing improve; it expects FY27 carbon black EBITDA growth of more than double-digit.
Carbon black volume growth of high single digits expected in FY27 with the added 90,000 tons capacity.
Cost initiatives (yield, throughput, feedstock diversification) expected to unlock INR200-250 crores of savings over the next 4-6 quarters.
Full cost pass-through expected to reflect in numbers by Q2 FY27, when margin profile should normalise; Q1 FY27 profitability expected to improve.
Aquapharm top-line growth of 20-25% expected in FY27; management aims to return to INR50-55 crores quarterly EBITDA and the INR75 crores quarterly run rate over the next 2-3 quarters.
Working capital requirement of about INR100 crores incremental even if crude stays at $90/bbl; management still targets the 2030 EBITDA goal of INR40 billion.
risks_watch: Crude volatility (Brent near $120 at the call) and the lag in formula-based pass-through; the full cost impact flows through by Q2 FY27.
Logistics and freight costs remain elevated because of Cape of Good Hope rerouting; key US and EU export routes are affected.
Gas shortage delaying commissioning of the 1,000 MTPA Palej superconductive specialty line.
Competition from Chinese and Russian carbon black; industry overcapacity limits pricing power.
Working capital needs and net debt if feedstock costs stay high.
Aquapharm utilisation and the timing of green chelates approvals from P&G and Henkel.
506590|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term recovery and FY27 double-digit EBITDA growth, but openly acknowledges weak Q4 profitability and that the initiatives are not yet visible in numbers. Management is evasive on the coal tar project and the battery timeline, and gives no firm quantification on Aquapharm green chelates volumes.
key_quotes: As the environment normalizes and volumes recover, we are confident of delivering double-digit EBITDA growth fueled by volume momentum, leaner cost structure and better pricing realization.
Raj Gupta: So, from 2030 perspective, we are very confident ,we remain on track and with all the initiatives that we are taking, we believe that we should be able to deliver those numbers.
Q4 results are not what we aspire to be.
The platform we are entering FY27 with is materially stronger than we were 12 months ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the jump in carbon black profitability this quarter, and how does management see FY27 volume and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Gupta said the QoQ jump is largely volume-driven (about 20,000 tons more) with EBITDA per ton unchanged, and the real impact of initiatives is not yet reflected. Nilesh Koul cited a contribution increase and inventory valuation lag; he expects high single-digit volume growth in FY27 and more than double-digit EBITDA growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per ton bridge for FY27, given ~14,900 per ton in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Koul said a 14-15% rise is achievable, driven by volume growth, product mix shift to value-added products, general price increases and cost initiatives.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost pass-through and pricing work across tyre and non-tyre segments, and what is the Q1 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tyre contracts are Q-1 or M-1 linked while a significant volume is spot-priced with early price hikes; prices are expected to be strong in Q1 FY27 and profitability to improve, though some gains will reverse as crude eases.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and leverage: how will the company manage it while growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Gupta said borrowings fell about INR450 crores in FY26 and working capital investment fell; even at $90/bbl crude, about INR100 crores of incremental working capital is needed, and net leverage is expected to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2030 EBITDA target of INR40 billion still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Gupta said the long-term fundamentals remain intact, the headwinds are short-term, and the company is confident of delivering the INR40 billion target by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume and EBITDA uplift is expected in Aquapharm from P&G and Henkel green chelates allocations?
qa_highlights.answer: Pankaj Kedia said trial orders have started with supplies from Q2-Q3 FY27 and sales to rise significantly after approvals; capacity is 4,000 tons and will be expanded after approvals; the INR75 crores quarterly EBITDA run rate is targeted in the next 2-3 quarters, with no volume quantification given.

506590|2026-06.headline: PCBL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 17% to INR2,474 crore, EBITDA up 23% to INR400 crore, PAT up 65% to INR155 crore, helped by low-cost inventory gains.
506590|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR2,474 crore and EBITDA rose 23% to INR400 crore, with PAT up 65% to INR155 crore. Management attributed part of the margin to spot-market pricing during the crude spike (Brent averaged USD 97/bbl vs USD 78 in Q4 FY26) and to low-cost inventory, which it said will partly reverse. Carbon black volumes were flat at 153,513 tonnes as export volumes were diverted to higher-margin domestic spot, and management guided Q2 volumes lower on customer destocking before a recovery in H2. Aquapharm (new CEO Rohit Narang) delivered revenue of INR394 crore and EBITDA of INR47 crore, with oil and gas weak YoY.

INR40-50 crore expected to reverse next quarter

506655|2026-03.headline: Sudarshan Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA INR73 crore, business EBITDA INR118 crore; net debt cut to INR755 crore from INR934 crore in Dec-25.
506655|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery as insolvency-era customer destocking ended and volumes returned, with the acquired Heubach/Clariant pigments group delivering EUR11 million business EBITDA versus a EUR9-10 million plan. Inventory was cut by EUR29 million against a EUR20 million plan, which released INR82 crore of overhead from the balance sheet and lifted P&L EBITDA. Reported EBITDA of INR73 crore included a one-time non-cash PPA credit of INR37 crore, and depreciation fell to about INR50 crore for the quarter after the final purchase price allocation. Management guided to EUR35 million EBITDA for FY27 and reiterated EUR90-100 million over three to four years, while flagging Middle East-driven raw material, energy and logistics pressure.

segments.name: Legacy Sudarshan
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was flattish, hit by distributor rationalisation in Europe and LatAm; integration costs slightly dented EBITDA. Management guides 8-10% growth for FY27 and expects to keep healthy margins.

segments.name: Acquired group (Heubach/Clariant pigments)
segments.commentary: Q4 business EBITDA EUR11 million, with FY26 EBITDA turning positive on value capture. Management guides EUR35 million EBITDA for FY27 and EUR90-100 million over 3-4 years. Gross margin is 4-5 percentage points above Legacy, offset by higher fixed costs.

segments.name: RIECO (engineering)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR268 crore (+17.5%) and EBITDA turned to INR10 crore from negative INR17 crore on restructuring and project cost control. Management says transformation is not finished and numbers have not improved as expected.

guidance_outlook: FY27 acquired-group EBITDA guided at EUR35 million, with only moderate growth assumed given geopolitical risk.
EUR90-100 million acquired-group EBITDA targeted over the next 3-4 years, driven by synergies, value capture and sales growth; no investment needed for that volume.

Tax: ETR is somewhat high for the acquired group due to conservative accounting and deferred taxes not recognised in some entities; similar range expected for FY27.
Annualised depreciation after final PPA is about INR347 crore.
capex_capacity: Enough capacity headroom in both Legacy and acquired plants to grow; the 3-4 year EBITDA plan needs no volume-driven investment.
Some commodity production moved from Frankfurt to the Indian Heubach site at Roha; Frankfurt is being kept for specialty products.
Legacy Indian plants debottlenecked after expansion; management did not give a utilisation percentage.
Management is exploring disposal of non-core assets; thinking is at an early stage.
Captive energy cost is 6-7% of revenue post-increase, per management.
demand_pricing: Q4 volumes recovered sharply; management says growth came from volume (customers ending destocking and buying again), with no price increases in Q4.
Management says Q4 was not industry growth but a recovery from winning back customers; pigment industry growth is about 3-4% globally, tracking GDP.
Near-term demand is described as muted due to the Middle East conflict, customers cutting inventory building and complementary products being unavailable; US housing and paint markets are weak.

Raw materials are petrochemical-derived, with price increases and supply constraints. Management says raw material cover is adequate and costs are being passed on region by region, though some competitors lag.
Management says it does not want to profit from price rises and is passing through only the cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EUR29 million inventory reduction is done, and what happens to the remaining inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: The EUR29 million cut is done; a further EUR15-20 million reduction is targeted gradually, which management sees as the normal state, when reported and business EBITDA should converge.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition debt be reduced given that most cash sits in India and most debt sits in the acquired entities?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said acquired-group debt will be serviced from its cash flows, and the repayment schedule is ballooning, starting this year and stepping up.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Q4 growth came from restocking versus true demand, and was it broad-based?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was not restocking; customers resumed buying after destocking ended, with broad recovery across segments, mainly coatings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall to about INR50 crore in Q4, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The final PPA gave a one-time depreciation reduction after fair-valuing fixed assets; the annualised depreciation run rate is about INR347 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 EUR35 million EBITDA guide comes from integration versus recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix of value capture and recovery, with only moderate growth assumed given the geopolitical situation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Legacy business's healthy margin sustainable through raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain healthy Legacy margins by passing cost increases through to customers.

Pass-through lag in some regions and competitor-origin countries could squeeze margins or volumes.
Debt repayment schedule is ballooning from FY27; coverage depends on the acquired EBITDA ramp to EUR35 million and beyond.

506655|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs.2,642 Cr and business EBITDA Rs.247 Cr for One Sudarshan; FY27 guidance held pending Q2 review.

506687|2026-06.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
506687|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.commentary: 22.5% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: 10.11% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others

demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

506767|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue and profit were flat (within ±1% YoY); management sees margin improvement next year but guides only 5-10% volume growth.
506767|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as challenging, with both top line and bottom line roughly flat YoY, and volume down about 1% and prices down about 1%. The March 2026 ammonia sourcing disruption from the Middle East war was short-lived, with inventories bridging the gap and plants kept running at roughly 60-85% utilisation. Ammonia cost rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg, and the company passed through price increases, with aceto prices now above INR200/kg versus about INR140-150/kg last year. Management believes the margin trough has passed but cautioned that gains from price pass-through are temporary and that competition will settle margins later.

financial_highlights.value: Roughly flat; combined volume and price decline about 2%
About 1% above last year; capacity 2 lakh tons, output about 110,000 tons per analyst estimate (not confirmed by management)

financial_highlights.change: Up roughly 30-40% from last year's average of INR140-150/kg
Up from about INR50/kg before the war

segments.name: Ethylamines
segments.commentary: Margins have improved as alcohol prices rose and prices stabilised; management says the market is a duopoly with Balaji and has enough capacity for 4-5 years. Market share is stable.

segments.name: Methylamines
segments.commentary: Still under pressure from new capacity: Aarti Industries commissioned a plant, taking the domestic players to four (RCF, Balaji, Aarti, Alkyl Amines). Management expects overcapacity and low utilisation to persist for some time.

segments.commentary: Pharma is 50-60% of sales and agro 15-20%, together about 70-75%. Management sees no pharma slowdown yet but flagged agro risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at 5-10% for the next year, in line with expected industry growth of about 5-7%; value growth higher because of elevated prices.
Management expects some margin improvement next year, but says it is difficult to predict continued growth beyond that.
Raw material and finished goods prices are not expected to return to pre-February 2026 levels soon; supply-chain normalisation is expected to take 3-6 months.

FY27-28 capex estimated at INR80-90 crore, mainly the balance of the Dahej new product plant and engineering projects; maintenance capex INR20-30 crore per year.
A product launch from the R&D pipeline is expected in July 2026; further R&D investment decisions deferred until volatility settles.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at most plants is about 60-85%; enough capacity for the next few years without new investment in existing products.

Kurkumbh project delayed by about one quarter; mechanical completion expected end-June 2026.

demand_pricing: Ammonia supply was disrupted for a week or two in March 2026, but sourcing recovered and inventories covered the gap; ammonia contracts are now short-term because suppliers are reluctant to commit longer.

Price increases have been passed through, with customers absorbing them because the company's products are a minor (C-item) cost in their bill of materials. Management believes competition, not customers, is the main pricing pressure.
Margin widening from inventory of cheaper raw materials is temporary; management expects margins to settle at competitive levels after one to two months.
Chinese imports of acetonitrile fell after Chinese players raised prices; the anti-dumping duty took effect only towards end-FY26.
Methylamines face overcapacity after Aarti's commissioning; ethylamines margins have recovered.
Peptides and acetonitrile demand expected to grow, but the company sees much of the optimistic peptide demand forecasts as unproven.

qa_highlights.question: How has user demand held up after raw material-driven price increases, and what is expected next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not yet seen demand destruction. Its products are a minor cost for customers, so pressure is expected from competition rather than customers. Prices are unlikely to revert to pre-February levels soon.

qa_highlights.question: Is ammonia available broadly across the industry, and how does this affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg. Government allocation is expected, as aliphatic industry needs only 10,000-15,000 tons per month. Stabilisation is expected in 3-6 months, and any spread gain is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capacity utilisation and the Balaji and Aarti capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 60-85%. Methylamines are overcapacity after Aarti's entry, which is expected to take a long time to absorb. Ethylamines have adequate capacity for 4-5 years. Balaji's 18,000 ton ACN plant will add competition, but the company believes it is the lowest-cost producer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR80-90 crore, mainly completing the Dahej plant and engineering projects. Apart from this, there is no major planned capex for existing products; maintenance capex is about INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company diversifying ammonia sourcing or looking at green ammonia?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia is bought mainly through distributors linked to fertiliser plants, with direct manufacturer links in only one or two cases. Green ammonia is still 3-5 years away from cost parity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin improvement is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some margin improvement next year. It noted that margins widen temporarily when raw material prices rise and fall, and that the company cannot predict whether it will keep growing.

risks_watch: Ammonia availability and price, with contracts now short-term and the Middle East war (Hormuz Strait) unresolved.
Demand response to 30-40% higher prices; agro demand at risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.
Methylamines overcapacity after Aarti's entry, with no near-term recovery expected.
Balaji's 18,000 ton acetonitrile plant and possible Chinese re-entry as import pricing normalises.
Pass-through reversal: competition may pull prices down faster than costs fall, reducing the temporary margin gain.
Kurkumbh commissioning timing (Q1 to Q2 FY27) and R&D product launch in July 2026.

506854|2026-03.headline: TANFAC FY26 revenue hit a record INR711 crore (+27% YoY), but operating EBITDA fell to INR112 crore (16% margin vs 23%) on sulphur costs and a plant outage.
506854|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations reached a record INR193 crore, up 11% QoQ from INR173 crore in Q3. FY26 operating EBITDA fell INR17 crore YoY to INR112 crore and PAT fell INR18 crore to INR70 crore, with management attributing this to normalising margins after an exceptional FY25, higher sulphur prices, an HF plant outage and higher depreciation. The company is building a INR495 crore downstream project (INR405 crore for HFC-32 refrigerant gas) targeted for Q3 FY27, with about 65% of its 20,000 MTPA capacity reportedly contracted. Management was evasive on HFC-32 production quotas, which are yet to be allocated by the government.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY from INR557 crore in FY25
+11% QoQ from INR173 crore in Q3 FY26
Down INR17 crore YoY from INR129 crore; margin down from 23% in FY25
Down INR18 crore YoY from INR88 crore; margin down from 16%

segments.name: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) and sulphuric acid
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid plant ran at 101% capacity utilisation and HF plant at about 95% in FY26. About INR70 crore of HF output was lost to unplanned maintenance and a distillation column bottleneck in the old HF-1 plant, which is now at 100% capacity.

segments.name: Specialty fluorides
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 41% in FY26, and management expects it to improve as value-added product demand scales.

HFC-32 plant of 20,000 MTPA at the Cuddalore site, about half complete, for commissioning around Q3 FY27 (Oct-Nov). Environment clearance and consent to establish are in hand.

Long-term contracts cover about 65% of the 20,000 MTPA HFC-32 capacity (about 13,500 tonnes), with management aiming to sell a further 15-20%. Management says about 75-80% of that volume is export and 15-20% domestic.
demand_pricing: Management says India HFC-32 demand is about 22-23 KT and could roughly double to 45-50 KT in 4-5 years, driven by room AC growth of about 16-17% CAGR. Global HFC-32 demand is about 380 KT (2025), going to about 485 KT by 2030.

Indian merchant AHF demand is about 40 KT in total: solar about 15 KT, surface treatment 15-18 KT, specialty 10 KT. Solar capacity in India is expected to rise from about 36 GW to about 216 GW in five years.
Sulphur cost rose from about INR30/kg in FY25 to INR38-40/kg on average in FY26 and rose further in Q4. Pass-through to customers lags by about 30-45 days, and HFC-32 contracts are formula-based.
Q4 included a mark-to-market loss of INR2.5-3 crore from rupee depreciation.
Management says domestic methylene dichloride supply of about 425-430 KT exceeds demand of 310-320 KT, so chloromethane sourcing is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will the HFC-32 quota be allocated to TANFAC, and on what basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quota will be decided in 2027 by the government. It cited an office memorandum of 1 April 2026 and said the 2027 calendar year is free for production. Quota applies from 1 January 2028, and management declined to comment further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the break-even and cost of production for HFC-32?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated cost of production at about INR240-280/kg, including operating expenses, and said it was not in a position to give break-even utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR495 crore capex separate from the 30,000 MTPA AHF plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the AHF plant is not included. It will be announced in the next two to three months, and the company expects to start it about four months later, with the solar grade expansion running alongside.

qa_highlights.question: What penalties apply if HFC-32 supply is missed because of quota non-allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no penalty for quota-related non-supply. Penalties are mutual and apply only once production starts. Management did not quantify any contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a strong, unusual Q3 FY25, sulphur prices rising from about INR30/kg to INR38-40/kg, a Q4 M2M loss of INR2.5-3 crore, about INR70 crore of HF output lost to an outage, and INR7 crore of extra depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR400 crore will be raised: INR100 crore from promoters via preferential allotment and about INR300 crore via QIP and term debt. Beyond that, funding depends on accruals and market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any overlap with parent Anupam Rasayan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product lists are fully distinct, with no overlap in fluorine downstream or other products.

506854|2026-06.headline: TANFAC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.3% YoY to INR187 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% on sulphur and power cost spikes; HFC-32 commissioning guided for end-Q3 FY27.

506879|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 crore and EBITDA margin hit 47.5%, while the company pursues a debt- and equity-funded acquisition of MicroBiopharm Japan and Sanofi brands.
506879|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR43.8 crore (up 22.1% YoY) on higher sales volumes, with EBITDA up 49.4% to INR20.8 crore at a 47.5% margin and PAT of INR11.1 crore (up 22.1%). Management described the business as sold out in capacity for years and said the expanded fermentation capacity (about 540 KL, roughly doubling capacity) starts full operation by end-August 2026. The call focused mostly on the strategic pivot to a fermentation-based CDMO, the MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) acquisition, and the Sanofi brand portfolio, with funding (up to INR1,000 crore equity, debt mix undecided) and deal timing left open.

Management expects some synergy projects with MBJ within the first year.
capex_capacity: Fermentation capacity has been roughly doubled (additional 540 KL); some capacity is for R&D and cGMP pilot facilities. Management said utilisation is effectively 0 or 100 and all output must be commercialised.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was flat but sold out; capex was late by about a year. API could not start because intermediate capacity was fully contracted to long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore acquisition make sense given interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sanofi deal is expected to close later, with long-stop June 2027, and that interest rates in the target geographies are much lower than 10%. It said the business is cash-flow positive from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure for the MBJ and Sanofi deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raise of up to INR1,000 crore is planned; the debt component is undecided and will depend on the optimal mix, with options kept open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the base business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex remains, and total base-business capex including maintenance is about INR20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from Sanofi brands to manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: A 3-year transition services agreement will move marketing authorisations country by country, with manufacturing moved to CMOs; management hopes for faster transfer, with tech transfer complete in year 1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Themis Medicare merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an external strategy review led it to focus on a fermentation-based CDMO and avoid diluting focus with predominantly domestic businesses.

507205|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 148% YoY to INR 949 crore and EBITDA margin was 16.3%, with Imperial Blue consolidated; FY27 guided to 16-18% combined EBITDA margin.
507205|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes rose 135% YoY to over 8 million cases, of which Imperial Blue (IB) contributed 4.6 million cases, while ex-IB volumes were roughly flat as Andhra Pradesh base effects reversed. Reported net revenue was INR 949 crore (INR 941 crore subsidy-adjusted) and EBITDA was INR 155 crore at a 16.3% margin, or INR 146 crore and 15.5% subsidy-adjusted. Management changed presentation so trade discounts and schemes are netted from gross revenue, which lowers reported revenue and gross margin but lifts EBITDA and PAT margins without changing absolute figures. FY27 guidance covers high-single to low-double digit volume growth and a 16-18% combined EBITDA margin over 24-36 months.

Mainly TSMA fees and labour code impact

segments.name: Ex-IB base business (TI)
segments.commentary: Ex-IB volumes were flat in Q4 against a high Andhra Pradesh base from the route-to-market change in Oct/Nov 2024; secondary sales grew about 5%. FY26 ex-IB volume was 13.6 million cases, up 14%.

segments.name: Mansion House brandy
segments.commentary: Crossed 10 million cases in FY26 and is India's largest P&A brandy. TI holds close to 40% P&A IMFL share in Southern India in Q4 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth of high-single digit to low-double digit for the combined business, then double-digit volume growth over the next couple of years; double-digit volume CAGR over 3 years.
Combined EBITDA margin of 16-18% over the next 24-36 months, with 15.5% FY26 as the base; the lower end implies about 50 bps improvement.
Net debt to EBITDA below 1.0x by FY29; net debt of about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027.
Capex about INR 25 crore each in FY27 and FY28, maintenance only.
TSMA fees to decline quarter on quarter, with a full-year FY27 impact of INR 55-60 crore; all TSMA states to transition by March 2027.
Working capital cycle of 53-55 days of gross revenue on an ongoing basis.
Combined-business margin benefit of 60-100 bps from the India-UK FTA scotch duty cut, mostly on IB; Telangana price increase is possible but timing is unknown.
Q1 FY27 margins expected to see some short-term pressure from input cost inflation.
capex_capacity: Prag (Andhra Pradesh) bottling capacity raised from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum after government approval; investment about INR 59 crore, fully spent; bottling savings of about INR 10 crore per year expected.

Shrirampur ENA distillery was under qualification issues; recommissioning investment is under consideration with no timing set.
Capex of about INR 25 crore a year in FY27-FY28, maintenance only.

Brandy P&A (prestige and above) expected to grow at a similar clip to TI's overall growth; northern brandy launch planned in FY27.
Selling expenses under the new presentation are about 6-6.5% of grossed-up revenue, per management.
Amara Vodka (SSL portfolio) expected to gain traction from the usership arrangement.

Q4 FY26 NSR up 5.4% to INR 1,177 per case; a Karan Kamdar estimate of IB at about INR 2,400 crore annualised revenue was described as directionally right with the NSR adjusted for the accounting change.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ex-IB volume flat in Q4, and what is IB seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY25 Andhra Pradesh sales were inflated by the route-to-market change; secondary ex-IB growth was about 5%. IB is fairly evenly spread across quarters, with H2 about 52% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 250-400 bps margin expansion comes from the India-UK FTA duty cut versus operational initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: The duty cut is worth 60-100 bps on the combined business, mostly on IB. The rest comes from cost optimisation and possible price increases, including Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IB run rate and the growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: IB growth should be similar to or slightly above the combined business because of its lower FY26 base; Maharashtra impact is largely in the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 IB NSR?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand-wise NSR is not disclosed. Under the new net-of-selling-expense presentation, IB NSR is about INR 20-30 above the combined NSR.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no gross debt guidance, and what is net debt at March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is less relevant because of a 2-year moratorium; net debt is expected at about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027, with upside bias.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin path and the Q1 outlook?

507514|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore and EBITDA to INR89.7 crore after the Bhopal licence suspension; FY27 guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore.
507514|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore, EBITDA declined to INR89.7 crore and PAT was INR10.2 crore. Beer volumes dropped 20% to 187.19 lakh cases, driven by the temporary licence suspension at the Bhopal plant and weak demand in Karnataka and Odisha, while IMFL grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases. Management said the Bhopal licence renewal is pending with authorities, with no definite timeline; the UP greenfield brewery has begun trials and commercial production is expected from June 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR1,400-1,500 crore and FY27 EBITDA margin to close to 10%, with FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

segments.commentary: Volumes grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases in FY26, led by premium portfolio penetration. Mahavat Whisky was launched in the mid-premium segment, and supply was halted when Bhopal stopped.

segments.commentary: Management said roughly 50% of company volume historically came from Bhopal. Production has been halted since February and Delhi, UP and Jharkhand supplies from this plant stopped; finished goods were cleared and sold.

Management expects Bhopal market share to return to earlier levels about six to seven months after the plant restarts.
UP plant expected to start commercial production in June 2026; full capacity ramp-up expected to take 2-3 years.

UP brewery (1 crore cases per annum): trials under way, commercial operations expected from June 2026; Phase 1 is the brewery and no further capex is needed beyond working capital.

Andhra Pradesh business expected to start in the next 3-4 weeks; Tamil Nadu share is growing.
Input cost inflation in glass bottles, aluminium cans, barley and logistics is the main margin pressure; long-term supply contracts are not holding price.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore, with the Bhopal licence assumed. FY27 EBITDA margin close to 10%; FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the UP plant contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: 15-20 lakh cases from UP in FY27 at roughly INR600 per case, about INR120 crore; plant capacity is 1 crore cases per annum with a 2-3 year ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 going to be as loss-making as Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects Q1 to be better than Q4 on higher Hassan and Odisha utilisation and lower annual costs booked in Q4. Only labour cost at Bhopal will fall; no salary cuts were made.

qa_highlights.question: How long to regain Bhopal and MP market share once the plant reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to recover the similar market share within about six months, though the main season makes it harder now. Management said the sales and distribution team is ready and waiting.

qa_highlights.answer: No one-time impact. The MRP cut lowers consumer prices; management said revenue would rise slightly and margins would not suffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the licence lost and what internal steps are being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some matters are sub judice and cannot be discussed. It is appointing a dedicated compliance officer and improving compliance processes. The company said the rating downgrades stem only from the licence suspension.
