507789|2026-03.headline: Jagsonpal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR64 crores and PAT 31% to ~INR9 crores; MAT growth 12.2% vs IPM ~7-8%.
507789|2026-03.overview: Management says Jagsonpal returned to growth in Q4 after two sluggish quarters, with Pharmarack data showing 14.2% Q4 growth against 10.5% for the industry. FY26 revenue grew about 7% to INR287 crores, while profit from operations grew 19% to about INR45 crores before the one-time labour code charge taken in Q3. The board announced a INR40 crore buyback at INR250 per share (no promoter participation) and a 200% dividend including a 75% special, together returning over INR66 crores. Management reiterated a target of 1.5x IPM growth, which it translates to 12-15% currently.

segments.name: Gynaecology
segments.commentary: Roughly half of business per management; named as the largest growth driver with Dermatology, with prescription momentum and improved doctor conversion.

segments.name: Orthopaedics
segments.commentary: Roughly 25% of business; overweight therapy, but management said in Q&A it is in line with IPM currently. A dedicated Ortho franchise is still being built.

segments.name: Dermatology
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-15% of business; second growth driver after Gynaecology. Ranked third on MR productivity.

guidance_outlook: Target growth of 1.5x IPM; management translated current IPM of 6-9% into 12-15% company growth and said it maintains this guidance for FY27.
Planned 9-10 product launches in FY27, of which about half are legacy brand extensions and 5-6 are new products in existing strength therapies.
Expects growth to get better over the next two quarters on Pharmarack-reflected numbers.
Buyback of INR40 crores at INR250/share (up to 16 lakh shares) approved by shareholders on 27 April; record date 4 May 2026. Expected to lift ROE from ~16% to ~18% and ROCE from ~22% to ~26%.
Dividend of 200% (INR4/share incl. 75% special), total cash outgo ~INR26 crores, subject to AGM approval.
Management said it can raise over INR200 crores of fresh debt and has balance-sheet capacity for acquisitions up to ~INR400 crores; an acquisition announcement is not yet made.
capex_capacity: MR headcount unchanged; no new MRs added in the last quarter. Growth to come from productivity of existing field force and geographies.
Asset-light model using CMOs; management says cost pressure is mainly packaging material and insurance costs, passed on over time under longer-term CMO agreements.
Price increases are SKU-based and taken after 12 months; ~92% of portfolio is outside NLEM price control, allowing up to 9.9% increase per management.
Strategic initiatives on field-force retention, internal promotions and MR upskilling are in progress.
demand_pricing: Pharmarack MAT (FY26) Jagsonpal growth 12.2% vs IPM ~8.5-9% (volume ~1-2%, new products ~3%, price ~5-7%); Q4 Jagsonpal 14.2% vs industry 10.5%. Management noted reported Pharmarack figure is 7% vs 12% on its mirrored basis, attributed to lead-lag.
Top 10 brands ~58-60% of sales; nine of them rank in top five in their categories. Growth of top 10 brands said to be in line with the rest of portfolio.
Management says the Middle East situation has no demand impact; cost pressure is on packaging materials, with vendors passing on increases.
Management said e-pharmacy channel is almost insignificant for revenue. A mature brand moderation in some therapies was offset by Gynae and Derma.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 recovery structural or seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the portfolio has hardly any seasonal products and the growth is driven by operational strengthening, brand building and MR productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why distribute so much cash rather than deploy it in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Board says the pharma business is brand-intensive, not capital-intensive; surplus cash is for inorganic growth only, and it could raise over INR200 crores of debt for acquisitions of up to INR400 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin and other expense trends in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year gross margin about 64.2%, down 20-30 bps from product mix; other expenses up ~30 bps from timing of annual cycle meeting, with structural cost increases only inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1.5x IPM target stand after the outperformance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained the 1.5x IPM target, which it says means 12-15% now, and said it expects the market to improve as metabolic and anti-obesity launches come through.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of growth into price, volume and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry: volume ~1%, new products ~3.1%, price ~4.8%. Jagsonpal: volume ~2%, new products ~3.2%, price 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 numbers a one-off and how is the portfolio diversifying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says focus stays on 2-3 power brands per vertical, and new products are targeted at 3%+ contribution; new product establishment takes a year-plus to build prescriptions.

risks_watch: Sustainability of the outperformance: Q4 growth 14.2% vs industry 10.5%; management says the next two quarters should improve, which is a near-term test.
Cost pressure from packaging material and insurance costs passed on through CMO contracts; management says no significant profit impact.
Dependence on top 10 brands (58-60% of sales) and moderation in some mature brands.
Management said the new product launch announcement is expected by late May or early June 2026, which will show whether the pipeline holds.
Capital allocation: cash will fall after buyback and special dividend; management is open to an acquisition funded by debt of up to INR200 crores.
Trade generics and Jan Aushadhi competition; management says no validated data shows it eroding branded volumes.
507789|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 turnaround and the 1.5x IPM target, but vague on segment-level detail: several answers deferred figures (therapy-wise growth, MR productivity by therapy, top 10 brand growth). Some responses were evasive on capital allocation.
key_quotes: Jagsonpal is back on growth in Q4 after two quarters of sluggish performance.
So any use of real cash that we have is only for inorganic strategy and not otherwise.
We continue to maintain that guidance, sir.
So technically we do have wherewithal to undertake an acquisition of up to INR400 crores with our own balance sheet.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 gross margin fell ~20-30 bps to ~64.2% on product mix, packaging and insurance cost pressure is only partly passed through CMO contracts, and FY26 operating EBITDA margin was ~21%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Asset-light model using CMOs with no plant or line additions disclosed, and MR headcount flat with no new MRs added last quarter.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 1.5x IPM (12-15% company growth) for FY27, Q4 grew 14.2% vs industry 10.5%, and volume is only ~2% of MAT growth of 12.2%, so growth relies mainly on price and new products.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with no utilisation figure disclosed and capex not discussed; the board is returning cash through a INR40 crore buyback and ~INR26 crore dividend instead.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects growth to improve over the next two quarters on Pharmarack-reflected numbers, but the 12-15% target is only held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 outperformance must be sustained, with top 10 brands at 58-60% of sales and some mature-brand moderation, and FY26 growth was only ~7% reported against the 12.2% MAT Pharmarack figure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: late May / early June 2026 announcement; launches through FY
rows.why: Management plans 9-10 launches in FY27, of which 5-6 are new products in existing strength therapies, with new-product contribution targeted at 3%+ and the launch announcement expected by late May or early June 2026.

rows.label: INR40 crore buyback at INR250/share and 200% dividend
rows.when: record date 4 May 2026; dividend subject to AGM
rows.why: Buyback of up to 16 lakh shares approved 27 April, expected to lift ROE from ~16% to ~18%; total cash outgo from buyback plus dividend exceeds INR66 crores, with dividend ~INR26 crores.

rows.label: Debt-funded acquisition capacity
rows.why: Management can raise over INR200 crores of fresh debt with balance-sheet room for acquisitions up to ~INR400 crores against cash over INR190 crores, but no acquisition is announced yet.

rows.label: SKU-based price increases
rows.why: About 92% of the portfolio is outside NLEM price control, allowing up to 9.9% increases, and price contributed 6-7% of Jagsonpal's growth against ~5-7% for the market.

tone.note: Management was confident about the Q4 turnaround, the 1.5x IPM target and the buyback, but gave vague segment and therapy detail and was evasive on capital allocation; analysts pressed on sustainability and the use of surplus cash.

507789|2026-06.headline: Jagsonpal Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 9% YoY to Rs.82 crores, with operating EBITDA up 21% to nearly Rs.19 crores and PAT up 22% to Rs.13 crores.
507789|2026-06.overview: Management said the growth seen from Q4 FY26 carried into Q1 FY27, with revenue up about 9% YoY and gross margin above 65%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded about 240 bps to above 23% and PAT margin rose 176 bps to 16%. The company completed the Rs.40 crore buyback and acquired 85% of Aequitas Healthcare for Rs.20.8 crores (enterprise value about Rs.25 crores) to enter the hospital segment. Management guided Aequitas to Rs.10 crores EBITDA by year two post-integration, though analysts questioned the step-up from about Rs.50 lakh EBITDA in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: after Rs.40 crore buyback (about half added back to cash)

segments.name: Branded prescription (core)
segments.commentary: Power brand portfolio grew 19% vs market 16%; five brands are #1 in their molecules and 14 are in the top five. Maintane (Pharmarack ~Rs.46 crores: injections Rs.34 crores, tablets Rs.13 crores) is one of the top three brands. Management is shifting mix from acute to semi-chronic and specialty therapies; new brand run-rates have almost doubled.

segments.name: Aequitas Healthcare (hospital pharma, 85% owned)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.53 crores and EBITDA about Rs.50 lakh per analyst. Portfolio is ICU and perioperative injectables, including latest-generation antibiotics, all branded, sold to corporate hospital chains (no government tenders). Management targets about Rs.100 crores revenue in FY28-FY29 and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two; gross margins are structurally thinner than JPL's branded business.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow at 1.5x industry growth rate in coming quarters (management reiterated on Pharmarack vs secondary-sales variance question).
Aequitas: about Rs.100 crores business within two and a half years (FY28-FY29) and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two post-integration; synergies expected over 36 months.
Productivity target of upward of Rs.2,50,000 per-person productivity (PCPM varies by vertical).
Dividend of 200% recommended, including 75% special dividend, subject to AGM approval.
Aequitas expected to contribute meaningfully from second year onwards; numbers expected to show in about the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Aequitas acquired as a subsidiary (not a BTA route); working capital cycle is longer than JPL and will not be aligned with JPL.
Aequitas network: about 49 institutional medical representatives, access to over 1,000 hospitals, around 50 hospitals contribute the majority of top line.
Lean and green productivity programme rolled out company-wide in Q1.
demand_pricing: Secondary (Pharmarack) growth of 18.9% vs reported primary sales growth of about 9%; management attributed the gap to stockist data and geographic statistical correction, and said it is reviewing the variance.
Hospital channel pricing is price-led; management said margins are structurally thinner than in branded prescription business.
Top 10 Aequitas products are over 50% of its sales.
Management reported one first-wave product launch in Q1 and expects one more in the current quarter.
Brand focus for growth: Indocap, Maintane, Endoreg (gynae), Pru and Eukroma (derma).

qa_highlights.question: Why is reported sales growth (about 9%) far below the 18% IPM growth cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the data is secondary (stockist) sales and the variance is partly statistical correction for geographies; it is reviewing why the gap is so wide and reiterated the 1.5x industry growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aequitas Rs.10 crore EBITDA target achievable from Rs.50 lakh in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited brand equity, lean team, corporate-chain focus, cross-selling of JPL brands and new-age brands with high value per patient; promoters remain with 15% and continue to run the business, so their salaries are not a one-off saving.

qa_highlights.question: Size of Maintane and its impact on portfolio growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharmarack value about Rs.46 crores (Rs.34 crores injections, Rs.13 crores tablets); growing ahead of molecule market; one of top three brands, but management did not disclose internal values.

qa_highlights.question: Aequitas gross margin looks low for a branded business; why?
qa_highlights.answer: In hospitals, price comes before brand, so margins are thinner; management plans mix improvement and differentiated innovative launches, but said it is too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp working capital improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to inventory control and stricter collections, and said payments now go out on due date; the big step-down was in FY22-FY24 (cash conversion cycle from 59 to 22 days).

qa_highlights.question: Any first-in-India or breakthrough molecule pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it never mentioned such a pipeline; it is targeting first-wave launches (about 5-10 companies) in gynae, ortho and derma, and launched one such product in Q1.

risks_watch: Aequitas execution: hospital working capital is longer and margins thinner; Rs.10 crore EBITDA in year two is an aggressive target from Rs.50 lakh base.
Concentration risk: Maintane and Indocap drive much of recent growth; management acknowledges the portfolio effect depends on a few brands.
Gap between secondary (Pharmarack ~18.9%) and reported primary growth (~9%) needs explanation next quarter.
Attrition and sales-force productivity: management claims improvement but gave no hard numbers.
Board change: Pallavi Dinodia Gupta stepped down; Anil Kumar Matai joined as Independent Director.
507789|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the Aequitas thesis, but evasive on specifics: declined to give Maintane MAT value, exact PCPM, and the reason for the primary-versus-secondary sales gap, and said it is still too early to judge Aequitas margins.
key_quotes: This 9% growth in sales has translated into a 21% growth in operating EBITDA as well as a 22% growth in net profits for the company.
Aequitas alone, we are looking at around Rs.100 crores of business within two and a half years' time, starting from now.
Growth without margins, improvement is hollow.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin expanded about 240 bps to above 23% and gross margin is above 65%, but Aequitas's thinner hospital margins will dilute the consolidated figure as it is integrated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Power brands grew 19% vs market 16% and Pharmarack growth was 18.9% vs industry 11.6%, with Aequitas adding a Rs.53 crore revenue base targeting about Rs.100 crore in FY28-FY29.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given, so no capex call can be made.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the 1.5x industry growth target rather than raising it, while reported growth of about 9% sits well below the 1.5x-of-11.6% (about 17%) implied by that target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Reported primary sales grew about 9% against Pharmarack growth of 18.9%, and management is still reviewing the gap, so a shortfall versus the 1.5x industry target is possible; Aequitas's Rs.10 crore EBITDA target from a Rs.50 lakh FY26 base also looks aggressive.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management reported one first-wave launch in Q1 and expects one more in the current quarter, and targets about 5-10 first-wave launches in gynae, ortho and derma.

rows.label: Aequitas contribution from year two
rows.why: Management said Aequitas numbers should show in about the next two quarters, against FY26 revenue of Rs.53 crore and EBITDA of about Rs.50 lakh, with a Rs.10 crore EBITDA target by year two.

rows.label: Working capital and collections discipline
rows.why: Cash conversion cycle fell from 59 to 22 days over FY22-FY24 and management says payments now go out on due date, though Aequitas's longer working-capital cycle will not align with JPL's.

rows.label: Hospital channel pricing pressure
rows.why: Management says hospitals are price-led, Aequitas gross margins are structurally thinner, and it is too early to quantify the mix improvement it plans.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter, the 1.5x growth target and the Aequitas thesis, but evasive on Maintane's value, PCPM and the primary-versus-secondary gap; analysts pressed on the Rs.50 lakh to Rs.10 crore EBITDA step-up and the thin hospital margins.

507815|2026-03.headline: Gillette India FY26 sales rose 8% to ₹3,100 crore and PAT rose 23% to about ₹650 crore, with the company citing a ~300bps structural margin gain.
507815|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) sales of about ₹3,100 crore, up 8%, and PAT of about ₹650 crore, up 23%, attributed to productivity across cost buckets. Management said the topline slowdown was largely due to one-time export impacts from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, and that domestic sales were growing quarter on quarter. The call focused on new launches (Gillette Guard 3in1, Gillette trimmers, Oral-B Sensitive), Venus growth, productivity, and raw material inflation linked to the West Asia conflict. Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Male grooming (Blades and Razors)
segments.commentary: Management says the category grows about 12% and Gillette remains market leader; male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M. Gillette Guard grew double digit and premium razors grew in early teens.

segments.name: Female grooming (Venus)
segments.commentary: Venus contributes double digits to grooming and is growing upwards of 20%; female grooming overall is growing upwards of 20%. The focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal.

segments.name: Manual oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing high single digits, driven by the Oral-B Sensitive range, which is growing double digit and is among the fastest growing segments in the category.

segments.name: Power oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing at roughly 1.5x this year and at double digits steadily; business has doubled in the last 3 years.

segments.name: Trimmers and appliances
segments.commentary: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call; management expects the trimmers category to grow at early double digits.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 sales or margin guidance was given; management said it expects some challenges to continue in the near term.
Management aims to grow ahead of the male grooming category and keep balancing topline and bottom-line growth.
A multi-year savings and productivity plan is in place by business unit to support margins and offset input-cost inflation.
Management said it cannot comment on future margins but expects productivity to fund investment and provide cover against macro volatility.
Management expects growth may fluctuate in the mid-term; it sees India growing at 6.5% for the year.
capex_capacity: About 85% of products are manufactured domestically; finished goods are exported to more than 10 countries.
Bhiwadi manufacturing plant issue was resolved within a few days with zero supply-related shortfall, per management.
Management is constantly assessing the locally manufactured vs imported supply chain mix.
Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half of the business; over 2 million automated on-shelf availability checks are run daily.
demand_pricing: Gillette Guard 3in1 (launched about 2 months earlier): about 1 million razors sold in the launch month, distribution reached over 6 lakh stores, and a new copy reached 20 crore viewers in month 1.
Numeric distribution rose by a couple of points in FY26 for priority SKUs; premium Mach3 and Fusion distribution grew at mid-single digits for 3 years.
Gillette Guard added 20 million new users over the last 3 years.
Management said raw material costs were hit by crude up ~50% and resins up ~50%, with availability challenged; the company said it did not go out of stock.
Management said rural consumption remains higher than urban, but rural is softening because of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth subdued and volatile in FY26 and the March quarter, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time export impacts from affiliate-company decisions, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, weigh on the base. Excluding them, growth would roughly double, and domestic sales are growing quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin gains sustainable, and what about FY27 margins and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structural margins improved upwards of 300 bps through premium innovation and productivity. It would not comment on FY27 but said a multi-year savings plan is in place and it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth plan over the next 3 to 5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will double down on its five-vector integrated strategy: daily-use portfolio, superiority, productivity, constructive disruption and an enabled organisation. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth drivers in Venus and female grooming?
qa_highlights.answer: Venus is double digit in grooming and growing upwards of 20%; the focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal through influencers and myth-busting content. No Venus salience figure was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trimmers and appliances opportunity, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Four trimmers were launched about 2 months before the call; the category is expected to grow at early double digits. Management aims to grow faster than the category but gave no share target.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhiwadi plant issue fully resolved, and were there supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue was resolved within a few days, with zero supply-related challenges, and the stock exchange was alerted.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: crude and resin up about 50%, with tight availability tied to West Asia conflict; the margin impact was not quantified.
Export revenue volatility from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh agreement closure.
Softening rural consumption and inflation-driven pressure on consumer spending.
Competition in men's shaving, which management acknowledged in Q&A without giving share data.
Next quarter: whether domestic growth and margin gains hold, and the early traction of Guard 3in1 and trimmers.
507815|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term record and category growth, but cautious on near-term challenges from inflation and supply costs. It deflected several quantitative questions (FY27 margins, share targets, Venus salience, the innovation pipeline) and said some information would be withheld as price sensitive.
key_quotes: We have consistently grown topline AND bottom-line for the last 5 years!
Gillette continues to be the market leader in the Blades and Razors segment, and we have grown year on year.
As an example, crude has been highly volatile and prices have gone up by 50%. As an outcome, resins have gone up by about 50% as well.
Despite these significant disruptions, we have not gone out of stock… or made compromises on product performance.

rows.why: Structural margin gain of upwards of 300 bps in FY26 and ₹38 crore productivity savings, but management would not comment on FY27 margins and flagged crude and resin up ~50% with the margin impact unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M, Venus growing upwards of 20%, and Guard 3in1 sold about 1 million razors in its launch month, though FY26 sales grew only 8% and export base effects weigh.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given and management expects some challenges to continue in the near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material inflation (crude and resins up ~50%) and softening rural consumption could pressure growth and margins, though no quantified cut was signalled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: already launched; traction through next 2-3 quarters
rows.why: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call and Gillette Guard 3in1 launched about 2 months earlier with about 1 million razors sold in launch month.

rows.label: Input cost pass-through and freight recovery
rows.why: Management said it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges under a multi-year savings plan, but gave no pricing figure and the crude and resin rise is ~50%.

rows.label: Export recovery from affiliate distribution changes
rows.why: The Bangladesh distribution agreement closure is a one-time export drag on the base; management said excluding it growth would roughly double, but the closure itself is not reversing.

rows.label: Supply 3.0 advance ordering
rows.why: Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half the business and over 2 million automated on-shelf checks run daily, supporting availability through the input shortage.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term record, male grooming category growth and launches, but cautious on near-term inflation, rural softening and export drag; it declined FY27 margin, share and Venus salience figures, and analysts pushed on sustainability of margins and FY27 outlook.

508814|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 37% to Rs 1,021 crore and EBITDA rose 53% to Rs 130 crore, with net debt cut to Rs 1,159 crore.
508814|2026-03.overview: Cosmo First reported Q4 FY26 consolidated sales of Rs 1,021 crore (up 37% YoY on 41% volume growth) and EBITDA of Rs 130 crore (up 53% from Rs 85 crore), helped by new BOPP/CPP capacity, specialty volumes and a Rs 7 crore EBITDA rise at the specialty chemical subsidiary. PAT growth was moderate due to higher depreciation and interest, a Rs 7.2 crore exceptional provision at a Netherlands subsidiary and a Rs 5.3 crore deferred tax asset reversal in South Korea. For FY26, revenue rose 26% and EBITDA rose 32% to Rs 479 crore. Management said the capex cycle is largely complete, net debt fell Rs 75 crore over six months to Rs 1,159 crore, and it expects double-digit topline growth in FY27.

segments.name: BOPP/BOPET films
segments.commentary: BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg in Q4 vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter; BOPET about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter. Films are about 90% BOPP-CPP and about 10% BOPET; specialty films are about 60% of films in Q4 (56-57% for full year).

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales Rs 54 crore with 25%+ EBITDA; FY26 sales Rs 204 crore. Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked pricing was lower, though volume grew about 20%.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Q4 topline up over 70% YoY; reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a small PBT loss likely. FY26 turnover about Rs 92 crore. Management targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and mid-to-high teens in FY28.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 topline up 54% YoY; annualised run rate about Rs 90 crore. Plan to move it into a separate subsidiary in FY27, with possible external capital.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 23 crore; exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore. Gross margin expected at 35-40%; still loss-making due to brand marketing. Management says at least two years to profitability and targets Rs 100 crore revenue first.

guidance_outlook: FY27 topline to grow in double digits, driven by utilisation of BOPP/CPP capacity added in FY26 and new businesses.
No EBITDA guidance given; management cited industry-cycle uncertainty but expects decent margins from new businesses, specialty growth and the US subsidiary.
Film volume growth potential of 15-20% from existing capacity; chemicals potential about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% utilisation.
Capex for FY27 expected below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over next year and the year after.
Net debt to fall further; target to bring debt below 2x EBITDA within 12-18 months (currently 2.4x).
US tariff refund of more than Rs 60 crore expected over 6-12 months, partly payable back to customers; flows to both P&L and cash flow. Management expects Q1 FY27 to be better than Q4 FY26.
Operating cost (employee and other) expected to hold at Q4 run-rate plus inflation in FY27.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share recommended for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
risks_watch: BOPP/BOPET spreads remain volatile as 7-8 new Indian BOPP lines arrive over three years; possible short-term core-film oversupply.
Speciality pricing lag (one to three months) can compress margins during raw material price swings.
Cosmo Consumer and Plastech still loss-making at PBT level; Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 as marketing continues.
Net debt of Rs 1,159 crore (2.4x EBITDA) and potential interest-rate pressure from inflation; deleveraging target below 2x within 12-18 months.
Timing and size of US tariff refund (above Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers) remains uncertain.
Management gave no quantitative EBITDA guidance and called the outlook highly uncertain.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 7.2 crore provision at Netherlands subsidiary
Rs 5.3 crore, South Korea subsidiary reorganisation

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 33 crore FY25; sales Rs 204 crore, 25%+ EBITDA margin
Down Rs 75 crore in last 6 months

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook for BOPP and BOPET prices and spreads in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee and other cost base likely to keep rising after FY26 (employee expenses Rs 250 crore in FY25 vs Rs 336 crore in FY26)?

508989|2026-03.headline: Navneet FY26 revenue fell 3% to INR1,683 crore; management guides FY27 publication growth of about 15% and stationery growth of about 15%, with margins to recover to around 9% after brand spend.
508989|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR394 crore versus INR389 crore, while FY26 revenue declined to INR1,683 crore from INR1,733 crore on US tariff disruption and weaker export pricing. Domestic stationery grew 4% in value to INR366 crore on 6% volume growth, but margins were hit by GST exemption on paper stationery (blocking input tax credit) and falling paper prices passed on to customers. Management is shifting to a two-year brand-building push (about INR30 crore in FY27 and INR40-odd crore in FY28) and expects a state curriculum cycle in Maharashtra and Gujarat from FY27. Indiannica (CBSE subsidiary) posted INR42 crore sales and a INR16 crore loss, and is to be merged into Navneet.

509079|2026-03.headline: Gufic Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR252 crore with EBITDA margin at 17.7%, while FY26 PAT fell to INR63.2 crore.
509079|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter in company history, with revenue of about INR252 crore (vs INR205 crore in Q4 FY25), EBITDA of INR44.7 crore (17.73% margin vs 13.17%) and PAT of INR20.5 crore (vs INR8 crore). Full-year revenue rose to INR940.5 crore (from INR820 crore), but EBITDA margin eased to 16.26% and PAT fell to INR63.2 crore from INR69.9 crore, reflecting Indore fixed costs, a domestic critical-care working-capital reset worth about INR22 crore of revenue, and higher overheads. Indore reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 at about 30% capacity utilisation, as committed. Management guided to about 15% revenue growth in FY27, around 18% EBITDA margin for FY27, and gross debt held at about INR400 crore.

segments.commentary: Reached 30% capacity utilisation by year-end as targeted and EBITDA breakeven in Q4. 40 tech transfers complete, 27 under development; 200-plus state FDA approvals; more than 20 Indian pharma companies use it as CMO base. Management expects Indore margin of about 31-32% at full utilisation, with overall Indore margin around 20%.

segments.commentary: Management said Navsari margin was about 20% and expects it to settle at 18-18.5% as costs rise. Navsari is building cartridge and pen GLP-1 capabilities.

segments.name: Domestic / Critical Care
segments.commentary: About 48-50% of revenue. Hospital direct-billing receivables of 140-150+ days were reset to CFA/stockist distribution, costing about INR22 crore of revenue across Q2-Q4 FY26; collections now essentially complete. Critical care growth guided at 6-8%, maximum 9%, before new launches.

segments.name: Women's health (fertility and gynaecology)
segments.commentary: Strongest year ever. Gonadotropin flagship hit its highest annual sales; a hormone launched two years ago beat its annual target and was ranked among top new launches by IQVIA. IVF expected to grow at a decent rate, with recombinant launches planned over the next two years.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claimed the number 2 botulinum toxin brand in India at about 23% share. Toxin is about 3.5% of revenue. A Canadian in-licensed filler is targeted for launch in Q3 or Q4 FY27, India only.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international business. Shifting from distributor-led model to holding marketing authorisations (Gufic Ireland for EU), with direct supply, out-licensing and tech transfer income. Exports about 20-22% of revenue. Approvals in Myanmar, Philippines, South Africa, Colombia, Germany, Ecuador in Q4; dossiers filed in 18 countries.

segments.name: CMO
segments.commentary: About 18-19% of revenue, boosted this year by GLP-1 contract work. Management guides to about 15-18% at peak. GLP-1 revenue not quantified.

segments.name: Nutraceutical and Ayurveda
segments.commentary: Focus on pain, arthritis and GI chronic therapies; a first-in-India formulation launched in heritage orthopaedic brand in Q4. No financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 15% YoY, described as an internal target that management considers achievable.
Gross margin to improve by 0.5-1% YoY, driven by mix, geography, new launches and pricing.
FY27 EBITDA margin around 18%, with 0.5-1% annual improvement thereafter and above 20% by FY30.
Gross debt to stay around INR400 crore, given higher working-capital needs; no new greenfield capex for about 2 years, with replacement capex of about INR20 crore a year.
New launches to add about INR20-25 crore net each year, with blockbuster launches potentially adding INR40-50 crore.
US FDA inspection possibly by end-FY27 after July-August batches; US operations targeted for FY28-FY29 as CMO first, then CDMO.
capex_capacity: Indore at about 30% utilisation at FY26-end, EBITDA breakeven in Q4; now moving to qualification, validation and tech transfer phase. Focus on complex injectables, depot, liposomal and suspensions.
EU GMP audit by Portuguese authority completed in early December 2025; certificate pending.
Navsari machines aged 15-20 years; replacement capex about INR20 crore per year; no greenfield capex expected for about 2 years.
INR30-35 crore invested over the last two years in GLP-1 CMO readiness (machinery, validation, dossiers).
Peptide and API backward integration: outsourced share of API reduced from about 80-85% to about 65%, target about 50% in-house over time.
demand_pricing: Critical care: volumes growing at double digits but price erosion limits value growth to about 6-8%.

GLP-1: management called the revenue too premature to quantify; partnerships in cartridge/pen (Navsari) and lyophilised vial (Indore) with partners; role is CMO/CDMO only.
Sakar Healthcare comparison: management declined to comment on competitor margins, citing Gufic's near-term investment load in dossiers, employee costs and depreciation.
Management said R&D spend is about 8-10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and is it operating leverage or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gross margin gains to domestic and international reset, new launches and moving to more profitable geographies, guiding 0.5-1% YoY improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GLP-1 work a confirmed contract and how big could it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a CMO role with partners, too premature to quantify, and not in prior projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR6.5 crore invested in a cooperative bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Saraswat Bank relationship of over 15 years; investment earns about 15% dividend vs about 8% borrowing cost. Total exposure about INR250 crore across fund-based, non-fund-based and term loans. Shares can be sold back at face value.

qa_highlights.question: Size of botulinum toxin revenue and capex needs for fillers?
qa_highlights.answer: Toxin is about 3.5% (plus or minus) of revenue. The filler in-licence needs no capex, as it is imported from Canada and sold in India under the partner's brand.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on top-line, margins and debt over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% revenue growth YoY; FY27 EBITDA about 18%; debt flat at about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Indore cost sit in P&L and what is the Indore vs Navsari margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari margin about 20%, expected 18-18.5%; Indore at 31-32% at full utilisation and about 20% blended.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt and cash evolve, given the analyst's cash figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term debt is enough for working capital for 2-3 years; long-term debt is falling; no debt-funded projects; growth investments funded from internal cash flow.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 PAT year-on-year despite revenue growth; FY27 margin recovery depends on Indore ramp-up and cost control.

US FDA and EU GMP certificate timing (EU certificate pending); US CDMO start targeted FY28-FY29.
GLP-1 volumes and margins may compress as competition rises; CMO share is supported by GLP-1 this year.
Currency and Middle East disruption affecting gross margins; INR400 crore debt plus rising working capital.

509079|2026-06.headline: Gufic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR260.8 crore and PAT rose 86% to INR22.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.09%.
509079|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR260.8 crore versus INR226.9 crore a year earlier and INR252.1 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (18.09% margin) from INR33.2 crore (14.6%), and PAT reached INR22.46 crore (8.61% margin) versus INR12.1 crore. Management said Indore is running to plan, with capacity utilisation expected to reach 40-45% by year-end and the GLP-1 CMO ramp expected to build from Q2 and more in Q3. Management reiterated 15-20% annual growth as a minimum commitment, with EU and US certifications for Indore still pending.

segments.name: Critical Care
segments.commentary: Launched monobactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combination on innovator patent expiry; Sparsh completed a full quarter on the rebuilt channel with outstanding days within trade terms. Focus is on own-manufactured brands and depth within existing hospital groups.

segments.name: Women's health / IVF (Puregraf, Ferticare, Zenova)
segments.commentary: Ferticare retains leadership in recurrent implantation failure; Puregraf entered major corporate IVF chains. Zenova is shifting from injectables to prescription chronic therapies, with two first-mover launches (osteoarthritis, metabolic ovarian) due ahead.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claims to be number 2 in toxin type A in India, made from its own strain. Filler partnership with Revanesse (Prollenium, Canada) expected to launch in India around December-January, subject to registration in Q2 or mid-Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Shifted to a model that earns fee income alongside supply revenue. Licensing progressed in Europe, a contract manufacturing and licensing arrangement was signed with a North American partner, and first CMO orders were received in Australia. Approvals were secured in 8 countries in the quarter.

segments.name: GLP-1 (semaglutide, via Hetero)
segments.commentary: Operates purely as a CMO for Hetero, which received permission in May 2026; Q1 revenue contribution was residual. A 10-15 day plant shutdown in Q1 was for a new machine. Management expects traction from Q2 and the main contribution in Q3, with 70% of capacity targeted for international use.

guidance_outlook: Management commits to 15-20% year-on-year company growth as a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond that.
Indore capacity utilisation expected to rise from about 30-35% now to around 40-45% by year-end, with the Indore liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within three years.
Margin expansion from Indore expected once EU certification is in place. Management says the 18% operating margin is the start of an improvement trend, not a new normal.
Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28.

Indore revenue potential is INR800-1,200 crore from current capex (about INR300 crore), so combined with Navsari the maximum is about INR1,600-2,000 crore; management also cited INR1,600-1,800 crore with no further capex.
Botulinum toxin and biostimulator in-licensed products are to launch this financial year with no significant capex. Stunnox and Zarbot registrations in SE Asia and Africa take 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Indore has about 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial capacity and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Depot and liposomal lines are in installation and qualification, with both targeted to be operational this year.
Indore has four lines: two lyophilisation lines, one suspension/liquid vial line, and one ampoule line. Target mix is roughly 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation, and 20-30% complex injectables.
Indore is fully operational as a unit; new product lines are being added within the existing capex of about INR300 crore, with no major new infrastructure.
Indore utilisation has risen from 18-22% last year, to 20-25%, to close to 30-35% this year.
Navsari is largely capped at about INR800 crore revenue, with toxin and penem blocks not yet saturated.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred until after next year pending cash flow.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per vial is about INR80-100 on current product mix (pantoprazole 10 ml vial at about INR60-80). Management aims to move to INR300-400 and eventually an average of INR500 per vial with depot, liposomal and complex injectables.
Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

Employee additions are mainly at Indore (around 50-60 for domestic expansion), with international headcount capped at 20-25. Management says the previous-year contract-to-payroll conversion was one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gufic participating in GLP-1 (semaglutide) under its own brand, and has third-party CMO revenue started?
qa_highlights.answer: Pranav Choksi said GLP-1 is purely a CMO role for Hetero, which got permission in May 2026, so Q1 revenue was residual. CMO traction is expected to build from Q2, with the main contribution in Q3; about 30% of capacity is for domestic CMO and about 70% for international use, where Hetero and Gufic have filed in more than 22 countries. No front-end role is planned in India or abroad.

qa_highlights.question: How does the shift in international model (distributor-led to own-registration, field-force led) change economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is moving to own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia once registrations and scale allow, aiming to lift margins from 40-50% under distributor models by 15-20% or more. A regional team was recruited in Q1 (one person in Mexico, one in the Philippines, two in Mumbai); the company also says it is building IP and trademarks in these markets.

qa_highlights.question: When will Indore get EU certification and does margin expansion follow, and is 18% the new normal margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari already holds EU certification. The Indore EU certificate is awaited, with feedback expected in about one to two months; a US partner has also filed from the site. Indore utilisation was 18-22% last year, 20-25% the year before, and close to 30-35% this year, targeted at 40-45% by year-end. Management said the 18% margin is the start of an improvement trend rather than a new normal, and that the earlier 18% period had Indore costs, depreciation and interest capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fillers (Revanesse tie-up) scale, and how big is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: The Indian filler market is estimated at about INR200 crore. Launch is expected around December-January, after registration in Q2 or mid-Q3. Management gave no first-year revenue number and aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth conservative, and can growth go beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% year-on-year company growth is a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond it. Some low-yielding product mix is being squeezed out, and it was not conservative in that guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from current capacity without further capex (analyst cited about INR2,700 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Roonghta first put FY27 expected revenue at about INR1,100 crore, with 15% annual growth taking it to about INR1,600 crore on existing facilities. Pranav Choksi said Navsari is capped at about INR800 crore, with toxin and penem not saturated, and Indore could add INR800-1,200 crore on about INR300 crore capex. The combined no-capex figure was cited as INR1,600-1,800 crore, and the total maximum as INR1,600-2,000 crore. The INR2,700 crore figure was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned employee addition strategy, and what productivity metrics are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Most additions are at Indore, with about 50-60 people for domestic expansion, while international headcount is capped at 20-25. The previous year's increase reflected contract staff moving to payroll in Indore and Navsari for quality roles, which management called a one-time step. Employee cost growth is in line with the company's overall growth.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating leverage from Indore's product mix start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28. Indore has 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Target mix is about 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation and 20-30% complex injectables, with the liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within 3 years.

509152|2026-03.headline: GRP Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 94 million (7% margin) from INR 331 million as EPR income, exports and raw-material costs weighed.
509152|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income declined 10% YoY to INR 1,450 million, with the prior-year base inflated by INR 305 million of EPR gains versus INR 66 million this quarter. FY26 total income fell about 3% to INR 5,380 million and EBITDA dropped to INR 429 million from INR 694 million, with adjusted PAT of INR 46 million after a INR 14 million Labour Code charge. Export volumes fell about 15% while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, and raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs. Management said the Pyrova (pyrolysis) and rCB platforms are still stabilising, and that the revised pricing from April 2026 passes through the full raw-material impact.

segments.name: Reclaim Rubber (RR)
segments.commentary: Export volumes fell about 15% in FY26 (export revenue down about 11-12%), while domestic revenue grew about 11%; domestic margins run 200-250 bps below export. Management expects the lost US volume to be fully restored in FY27; 38% of capacity has moved to the new process platform, saving about 5% on power.

segments.name: Pyrova Energy (pyrolysis, crumb rubber, rCB)
segments.commentary: Continuous pyrolysis started in H2 FY26 at Solapur; operating above 85% utilisation monthly. Cumulative investment about INR 79 crore to March 2027 target; TPO sales are currently fuel-only, with industrial furnace and petchem approvals still in validation. Recovered carbon black facility (12,000 t) expected in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Non-Reclaim standalone businesses
segments.commentary: Grew about 13% YoY and 22% QoQ in Q4 FY26, mainly from pyrolysis start-up. Custom Die Forms volumes rose 4%; plastics (PP, nylon) faced low-cost Chinese virgin PP imports, hitting packaging margins and volumes. Polymer Composite business was closed, with a INR 79 lakh write-off.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth capex targeted at about INR 90-100 crore, mainly for Pyrova Phase 1b (rCB and additional pyrolysis lines, phased completion by February 2027).
Second new-technology reclaim rubber line to be commissioned by end of Q1 FY27 in Solapur, taking capacity from about 350 to about 700 tonnes per month.
Pyrova is expected to deliver high double-digit EBITDA margins; a few hundred bps improvement in RR EBITDA margin is expected; full impact in FY28, with some improvement in FY27.
EPR accrual for the pyrolysis business expected by H1 FY27 once PCB approvals come through, with credits accrued retrospectively.
Revised pricing from April 2026 is said to fully pass through raw-material inflation, subject to current conditions.
Management expects operating leverage to improve progressively in the medium term as the new businesses stabilise.
capex_capacity: Cumulative Pyrova Energy investment about INR 79 crore to March 2026; Phase 1A (15,000 t single-line reactor plus crumb rubber) completed by October 2025 and stabilised in Q4 FY26.
Capex FY24-FY26 about INR 170 crore: roughly 50% Pyrova, 30-35% Reclaim Rubber (capacity and new technology), about 15% other (including solar/wind and an SPV for power offtake in Solapur).
Post-expansion capacity: pyrolysis about 45,000 t (two added reactors), rCB about 12,000 t, crumb rubber about 65,000 t versus over 45,000 t currently.
Solar/wind and renewable projects in Ankleshwar and Panoli expected in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: US tariffs hit about 33% of RR revenues from key US customers and about 44% of associated raw-material margins in FY26; after February revisions the impact moderated to about 41%.
Domestic rubber consumption grew about 4% and reclaim rubber consumption about 7% in FY26; GRP's share in the tyre industry rose.
Raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs; margin erosion was seen in Q2, Q3 and part of Q4 because tyre-company contracts are annual or half-yearly.
Management said the order book is stronger than most of FY26, with North American direct volumes largely recovered but indirect volumes via Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia only partly recovered.
Pyrolysis oil realisations in Q1 FY27 are marginally above Oct 2025-Feb 2026 levels, but road-construction volumes are down because of bitumen shortages from the West Asia conflict.
EPR credits are priced at about the floor of INR 2.52/kg; about 85% of credits are contracted with tyre companies and about 15% sold on the spot market.

qa_highlights.question: How much one-time loss came from Polymer Composite in Q4?

qa_highlights.question: Did pyrolysis oil realisations improve with high crude prices, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Some benefit in March; Q1 FY27 realisations are marginally above Oct 2025-Feb 2026, but road-construction demand is weaker, so volumes are affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery trend in exports and order inflows, and have RM costs stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: North American direct volumes are largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26. Revised pricing from April 2026 captures the full raw-material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capex breakup, and what is the feedback on TPO and the new reclaim technology?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about 50% Pyrova, 30-35% RR and about 15% other. TPO is in validation for industrial furnaces, with petchem approvals longer. A second new-technology RR line will be added by end Q1 FY27, taking capacity to about 700 t/month from about 350 t/month.

qa_highlights.question: How much EPR income will pyrolysis and rCB generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Pyrolysis EPR accrual awaits PCB approvals, expected within weeks, with retrospective accrual in Q1 or Q2 FY27. Credits accrue at about 0.8 weightage with about 1.5x conversion; the mix of crumb, char and TPO is not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA margin after Pyrova stabilises, and how will capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Pyrova expected at high double-digit EBITDA margins, with full impact in FY28. Funding will mix DFI Proparco undrawn limits, internal accruals and possibly unsold EPR credits; serviceability is described as strong.

risks_watch: Pyrova approvals (PCB) for EPR accrual; the timing of catch-up accrual affects H1 FY27 earnings.
Petchem and industrial-furnace TPO approvals are still pending, and oil-price deltas between FO, LSHS and CBFS are unstable.
Debt-to-equity rose to 1.15 from 0.76, and the company is considering debt, accruals or a QIP after the earlier QIP approval lapsed.
Recovery of indirect US-linked volumes via Southeast Asia, and the status of US tariff revisions.
Chinese virgin PP imports continuing to erode recycled PP competitiveness in packaging.
Gross margin of 46% in Q4 versus 54% in FY25; the EBITDA trajectory needs to recover toward FY25 levels.
509152|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid about a weak FY26 and attributed the decline to tariffs, raw-material inflation and start-up costs, while expressing confidence in the Pyrova and reclaim-rubber expansion. Answers were often evasive on forward margins and petchem pricing, and some questions were repeated or deferred because of line disturbance.
key_quotes: FY '26 represented an important transition year for GRP.
Export volumes for the company declined by about 15%, while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, supported by a proactive market development and selective pricing actions.
As far as the new Reclaim Rubber is concerned, approvals are coming through trickling in slowly, but surely, customers are taking a slow approach in improving or increasing the volumes.
But we are expecting that the Pyrova Energy as a business in itself will be high double-digit EBITDA margins is the expectation.

rows.why: Management guides a few hundred bps RR EBITDA margin uplift and high double-digit Pyrova EBITDA margins at full impact in FY28, with pricing passing through raw-material inflation from April 2026, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 7% from 21% and gross margin to 46% from 54% in FY25.

rows.why: Second new-technology reclaim line under construction for end Q1 FY27 doubling Solapur capacity to ~700 t/month, and rCB facility expected H2 FY27; Pyrova Phase 1A already stabilised with utilisation above 85% monthly.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects lost US reclaim volume fully restored in FY27 after export volumes fell about 15% in FY26, and reclaim consumption grew about 7% in FY26; however domestic volumes grew only ~10% and Q1 FY27 road-construction volumes are weaker on bitumen shortages.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 growth capex of INR 90-100 crore is already approved for Pyrova Phase 1b and utilisation is above 85% monthly, so the capex is committed rather than speculative.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 total income fell 10% YoY to INR 1,450 million and EBITDA fell about 72% to INR 94 million, and no revenue growth % was guided, so upside revisions look remote.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EPR accrual for pyrolysis depends on PCB approvals expected by H1 FY27, petchem and industrial-furnace TPO approvals still in validation, and debt-to-equity rose to 1.15 from 0.76, so timing slippage is a real risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TPO sales are fuel-only today with industrial furnace and petchem approvals still in validation, and the 12,000 t rCB facility is expected in H2 FY27, so new product grades depend on approvals.

rows.label: Pyrolysis EPR accrual on PCB approvals
rows.why: Management expects PCB approvals within weeks and retrospective EPR accrual by H1 FY27; EPR credits are priced near the INR 2.52/kg floor, so the catch-up accrual could lift H1 FY27 earnings.

rows.label: Order book stronger than most of FY26
rows.why: North American direct volumes largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26, though indirect volumes via Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia are only partly recovered and US tariffs still hit about 41% of RR revenues after February revisions.

rows.label: Revised April 2026 pricing passes through RM inflation
rows.why: Revised pricing from April 2026 is said to fully pass through raw-material inflation of up to 43% in some SKUs, after margin erosion in Q2 to part of Q4 FY26 under annual or half-yearly tyre contracts, subject to current conditions.

tone.note: Management was candid about a weak FY26 from tariffs, raw-material inflation and start-up costs, and confident on Pyrova and the reclaim expansion, but was evasive on forward margins and petchem pricing; analysts pushed on EPR accrual timing, pyrolysis oil realisations and capex funding.

509152|2026-06.headline: GRP Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 60% to INR174 million, margin 11% (+233 bps), PAT more than doubled to INR42 million on 26% total income growth.
509152|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 26% YoY to INR1,573 million, driven by Pyrova Energy utilisation, export recovery and better realisations. EBITDA grew 60% to INR174 million with margin up 233 bps to 11% despite sharp raw material inflation. Management re-segmented into Rubber Recycling and Others, and for the first time gave a directional FY27 outlook of close to 20%+ revenue growth. Pyrova cleared a 25-day monthly continuous run threshold in July 2026, and the rCB plant is slated for commissioning by October 2026.

segments.name: Rubber Recycling (Reclaim Rubber, Custom Die Forms, Pyrova Energy)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue grew 34% on a stand-alone basis with reclaim volumes +12%; margins expanded on realisations and efficiencies. Pyrova is still below stand-alone profitability; cumulative Pyrova investment is about INR91 crore.

segments.name: Others (Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefin, Windmill, residual polymer composite)
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly flat against a higher base that included polymer composite, which was permanently shut after the tariff hit. Engineering plastics volumes +27%; plastic verticals EBITDA margin up 14 pp YoY on a 10-pp gross margin improvement.

guidance_outlook: FY27: close to 20%+ overall revenue growth, driven by Pyrova, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling.
FY27: reclaim rubber volumes to grow close to 20%; management hopes to hold double-digit volume growth for the year.
Reclaim rubber, mid-term: mid-teen volume growth over 3 years, double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin from ~9-10% toward 10-14% after Pyrova synergies.
Pyrova: capacity to 45,000 tons, then +30,000 tons in FY28; EBITDA margin to 18-20% after rCB is mature (later described as 15-20%); FY28 seen as maturity year.
Plastics: over 20% growth in FY27, mid-teen growth through FY30, EBITDA margin 10-15%. Management said current margin is not one-time and should keep improving.
FY27 capex INR90-100 crore; FY28 capex decision in 2H FY27. Remaining ~INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan still to be deployed.
capex_capacity: Pyrova: two more pyrolysis lines to take capacity to 45 KTA; longest continuous reactor run achieved; July 2026 met threshold of 25-day monthly run with 4-day shutdown.
rCB (recovered carbon black) plant: commissioning starts next month (August 2026), target commissioning by October 2026; meaningful contribution expected by Q4 FY27.
Reclaim rubber debottlenecking capex included in FY27 plan.
Long-term: another 30,000 t pyrolysis and 12,000 t rCB capacity in Gujarat; Pyrova stand-alone revenue potential INR250-300 crore.
Renewable energy was ~48% of stand-alone power in FY26 (37% a year earlier); target 50% by FY28, expected to be reached in the current fiscal.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth ~30% YoY vs volume +12%; the balance is price, largely passed through to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually.
Management does not expect rubber prices to reverse soon; cited El Nino effects on natural rubber and oil-linked synthetic rubber pricing.
Reclaim is being pitched as a value alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches.
US exports recovered (export volumes +20%, mostly North America); Europe and other markets starting to contribute. Non-US indirect tariff-related volumes not fully recovered.
Domestic reclaim market share up ~1% YoY per management; export share flat overall but higher in focus geographies.
Engineering plastics growth driven mainly by automotive OE demand, with early appliance approvals contributing; polyolefin volumes flat as customer selection tightened.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin moderated on higher raw material costs (management cited ~180 bps decline)
More than doubled; after prior period items
vs INR46 million in Q1 FY26

qa_highlights.question: Has the tariff disruption led to permanent changes in the competitive landscape, and did GRP win customers from global competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer composite was permanently shut, a real one-time loss. Reclaim and Custom Die Forms volumes are back to pre-tariff levels, with currency adding a margin benefit versus pre-February 2026. Some customers are starting to receive tariff credits, which may lift margins later, but visibility is limited. Indirect non-US export volumes are not fully recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Which business will be the largest contributor to earnings growth for the rest of FY27, and does management expect double-digit revenue growth and further margin expansion in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated close to 20%+ revenue growth for FY27, driven by Pyrova Energy, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling. It said the Q1 margin is not one-time and should keep improving, but it did not give a separate gross margin number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rCB project status, including customer trials, expected revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pyrolysis phase was commissioned in October 2025 and stabilised by March 2026. The rCB plant starts commissioning in August 2026 and is targeted for October 2026. Meaningful contribution is expected from Q4 FY27. Pyrova can reach 18-20% EBITDA margin once rCB is mature, subject to customer approvals; FY28 is seen as the maturity year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 27% growth in engineering plastics volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly automotive OE demand for nylon, with early appliance approvals from Q4 FY26 contributing some commercial volume. Polyolefin revenue grew but volumes were flat because customer selection was tightened, with a push into specialty polyolefin sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How much has rubber inflation risen over the past year, and when will prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict how long rubber inflation will last. Revenue grew about 30% against 12% volume growth, so the balance is price, largely passed to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually. Prices are not expected to reverse soon given El Nino and oil-linked synthetic rubber.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 capex plans, and what is the deleveraging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR90-100 crore, covering two more pyrolysis lines to reach 45 KTA, the rCB plant and reclaim debottlenecking. FY28 capex will be decided in 2H FY27. About INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan remains. Deleveraging timing is not in management's control, and there are no firm plans, though it would be needed to accelerate the Gujarat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers shifting toward sustainability-led material solutions rather than buying on price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a combination of value and sustainability. Reclaim is increasingly considered an alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches. In plastics, regulation drives conversion and cost drives adoption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery is demand normalisation versus share gains, and is the export order book back to pre-tariff levels? What is the sustainable EBITDA margin, and when does Pyrova become EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose 20%, mostly North America, with early Europe contribution. Domestic market share is up about 1% YoY, and export share is flat overall but higher in focus geographies. Pyrova crossed a 25-day monthly continuous run with a 4-day shutdown in July 2026. Management did not give a date for EBITDA breakeven. Stand-alone EBITDA margin targets are Reclaim 10-14%, Pyrova 15-20% and plastics 12-15%.

risks_watch: Rubber and raw material inflation: gross margin fell about 180 bps and management would not guide on gross margin; pass-through lags 1-4 quarters under quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts.

Pyrova execution: still below stand-alone profitability, with margins in single digits during ramp-up. rCB commissioning targeted October 2026, but several quarters may be needed for tire-industry product approval.
Indirect non-US export volumes not yet recovered; polymer composite closure is a permanent revenue and margin loss.
Capex and leverage: FY27 capex of INR90-100 crore, FY28 capex decision deferred to 2H FY27, and no firm deleveraging plan.
Plastics: polyolefin volumes flat on tighter customer selection; nylon growth depends on automotive demand; EPR enforcement and waste collection remain challenges.
Possible tariff credits to customers could affect margins, with timing and size not yet visible.
key_quotes: The threshold in the industry from a performance perspective is for a run of minimum of 25 days in a month and a 4 -day shutdown on the pyrolysis.
I do believe that this margin that we have generated in Q1 is not a onetime margin generation.
So, I wouldn't want to comment on the gross margin number.
At least as things stand now, we do expect these businesses to start generating cash flow.

Management declined to forecast rubber price direction or gross margin and framed several targets as conditional on customer approvals.

rows.why: rCB commissioning starts August 2026 with target October 2026, and two more Pyrova pyrolysis lines to 45 KTA are under construction, with a further 30,000 t in FY28 planned; FY27 capex of INR90-100 crore is committed.

509480|2026-06.headline: Berger Paints Q1 FY27 standalone value growth 12.7% on ~8.4% volume; operating margin 17.4%, PAT up 25.5%.
509480|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 12.7% in value with volume up about 8.4%, driven by decorative (value +13.5%, operating profit up nearly 20%). Gross margin was 39.3%, held back by delayed and partial price pass-through in industrial and protective, GI and powder coatings, where price increases landed late in the quarter. Consolidated revenue rose 12%, PBDIT rose 12.6%-15% (management cited 15% operating profit growth) with margin up about 40 bps, and PAT rose 28.6%, with the Bolex and STP subsidiaries lagging on growth. Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth, a slightly better Q2 than Q1 on a year-on-year basis, and operating margin within the 15-17% range.

financial_highlights.change: Above 15-17% guided range; Q1 seasonally higher on value sales
Consolidated operating margin just short of 17%

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,424 crore as of end June 2026
financial_highlights.change: Up from Rs 992 crore (transcript reads 992 to 11.98 to 1424, likely a transcription error)

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth about 13.5%, the highest in 12 quarters, with operating profit up nearly 20% and margin expansion. Exterior emulsions outperformed; Color Plus premium interior emulsion gaining traction; Luxol metallics new range doing well.

segments.name: Protective, GI and powder coatings
segments.commentary: Relatively lower growth because price increases were taken late in the quarter after a prolonged battle in the field; expected to show up more in Q2.

segments.name: Automotive coatings
segments.commentary: Healthy double-digit value growth.

segments.name: Wood coatings and HomeShield
segments.commentary: Strong growth; wood coatings reported strong double-digit volume growth.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and waterproofing
segments.commentary: Robust volume and value growth; now about 10-12% of the paint business and growing well above paint. Roof pool and seal gaining momentum.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Bolex had flattest revenue on seasonality and UK remained subdued, though Bolex profitability improved. STP profitability improved on mix and price. BNPA and Becker JVs posted strong revenue and profit growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth expected to sustain, supported by full-quarter price increase impact in Q2 and festive demand.
Q2 revenue growth expected slightly ahead of Q1; Q2 volume growth around 7.5-8%, slightly below Q1's 8.5%.
Price increase contribution expected at about 7.5-8.5% in Q2 versus about 5% in Q1.
Operating margin to stay within the 15-17% guided range; Q2 year-on-year operating margin expected to improve, and Q2 should be slightly better than Q1 on that basis, though not sequentially.
Management expects good top-line and operating profit growth in Q3, with no firm margin call beyond that because of raw material volatility.
Capex for FY27 roughly Rs 600-800 crore; Panagar plant to start at end of this fiscal, plus a plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex roughly Rs 600-800 crore, per management.
Panagar factory to start at end of FY27; second plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda, both funded partly from the cash surplus.
Tinting machine installations crossed 2,100 in the quarter; annual target about 10,000, mostly in under-indexed markets.
Store count above 1,900, with urban stores around 900+ and growing.
Backward integration: emulsions and most resins now made in-house; thickeners being produced in-house; a Dow-linked monomer to be made at Sandhila, Lucknow.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 8.4%, value growth 12.7%, with price contribution about 5% in Q1 (mostly time-weighted) and mix improvement of roughly 2-3%, per management, which differs from management's normal 0.4-0.5% mix change.
Secondary sales were better than last year because rains were lighter; July growth described as reasonable, and August expected to be similar.
Dealers stocked up ahead of price increases; management expects this to be absorbed by stronger sell-out, with little Q2 destocking risk.
Competition intense: challenger brands aligned dealer price lists within about 5%, raised rebates to large dealers, and continue 10% free-material offers in most packs outside the economy segment.
East India muted; West Bengal government transition expected to take 3-4 months before government contracts restart. Northeast hit by floods in Assam. South and North grew faster.
Retail is the bulk of growth; project business 1-2% faster than retail.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 value growth came from price and mix, and what price increase is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 price impact about 5% (time-weighted, mostly industrial). Q2 price impact expected around 7.5-8.5%, depending on mix. Management said mix improved in Q1 and should improve further in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 margins expand year-on-year, and what about the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 operating profit growth to be decent and year-on-year margin to improve, helped by industrial price pass-through and operating leverage. Beyond that, margins depend on raw material prices, so no firm full-year call.

qa_highlights.question: Why is decorative growth below the industry leader's?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect: the leader degrew last year while Berger grew. Management cited a 3.6% value growth differential and an 8.6% profit differential in the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk from price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain high single-digit volume growth through network expansion, the branding campaign, new products and the price increase being absorbed, and sees no volume downside risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be post-Diwali price cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; it depends on crude and raw materials. If prices fall substantially, some price reduction in H2 is possible to avoid a price war.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand or pricing reason for the weak Bolex and STP subsidiary growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Bolex was seasonally weak in Q1; STP was disrupted by the Jamshedpur plant but has normalised. Corrective measures on less profitable lines in Bolex and STP are expected to lift profitability.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (crude oil, geopolitics): a sharp fall could widen margins, but could also trigger price cuts and discounting in H2.
Industrial and protective price pass-through still lagging; full effect expected in Q2 and August.
Competitive intensity remains elevated; challenger brands' rebates and free-material schemes could persist.
Mix shift toward low-value, high-volume construction chemicals could keep value growth below volume growth.
Eastern India and Northeast demand; West Bengal transition period.
Subsidiaries: UK operations subdued; Bolex and STP growth flat in Q1 with profitability turnaround still to be proven.
Monsoon and the timing of Diwali for festive-season sell-out.

509496|2026-03.headline: Cemindia FY26 revenue crossed INR10,000 crore (INR10,061 crore, +9%) and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 15.1%, helped by one-time claims and provision releases.
509496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income rose to INR2,973 crore for the full year and Q4 EBITDA jumped 66% YoY to INR450 crore at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the margin spike to one-time items: INR150 crore of claims realised (INR100 crore in Q4, partly booked as other income) and release of provisions held for metro jobs now completed. Management guided that the normal EBITDA margin is about 10-10.5%. Order book stands at INR29,000 crore, including L1 positions of about INR1,600 crore and an April win of about INR3,200 crore. FY27 guidance is revenue growth of at least 20-25%, with an order-inflow target of about INR25,000 crore.

segments.name: Group / captive EPC (Adani-linked) and data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre is a new division with 3-4 jobs secured from the group; cumulative data centre order book about INR3,000 crore. Management is keeping it within the group for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

segments.name: Metro and tunnelling
segments.commentary: Bangalore and Mumbai metro jobs completed and contributed to Q4 margin. Chennai Metro has about 40% of value left, with completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028; the company owns 4 TBMs at Chennai and sold a Bangalore TBM. Tunnelling market (metro, road and other) is cited at about INR1 lakh crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow at least 25% per MD's opening answer; later answers say 20-25% is quite possible on top line.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR25,000 crore, against about INR19,000 crore secured in FY26 (including L1 and April wins).
Sustainable EBITDA margin excluding other income guided at about 10-10.5%; management says it will try for more than 10%.
FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore, against INR260 crore in FY26.
PAT margin: management aims to maintain the same momentum and margin.
Dividend was supposed to be declared but is delayed; management said it will be declared within a few weeks.
Revenue growth of 20-25% a year for up to about 3 years was stated as the aspiration; no fundraising planned.

Chennai Metro TBMs have completed breakthrough; about 40% of value left, completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028 (stations included in scope).
New TBMs being bought for Pune Metro and Delhi Metro; large-diameter TBM would be needed for large diameter tunnel work.
No idle TBMs at present; a TBM is typically engaged for 3-4 years on a job.

Pipeline of about INR70,000 crore, of which group is about 35-40%; roads and highways and tunnelling are the main segments, each about INR1 lakh crore market.
