509675|2026-03.headline: BirlaNu Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore; standalone EBITDA margin up ~380 bps, but Parador impairment of Rs 74 crore hit standalone books.
509675|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year, with subdued demand, pricing pressure and Middle East-driven volatility. Q4 improved: consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore and standalone EBITDA margin expanded about 380 bps, helped by a Rs 5 crore Clean Coats dividend and resin price spikes in March. Full-year consolidated revenue was Rs 3,730 crore (+3%), while standalone EBITDA rose 39% to Rs 146 crore, aided by Rs 22 crore Clean Coats dividend and Rs 7 crore asset-sale profit. A Rs 74 crore diminution provision on the BirlaNu International GmbH (Parador) investment was booked as an exceptional item in standalone accounts, and Parador posted a Rs 35 crore operating loss in Q4 including a Rs 19 crore severance provision. Total debt was Rs 851 crore at year-end, down from Rs 929 crore in December.

segments.name: Construction Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 37 crore (+58% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 117 crore (+45%), crossing Rs 100 crore milestone. Ex-Clean Coats growth was 25% for FY26; Clean Coats contributed Rs 20 crore over 4.5 months since acquisition.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 147 crore (+4% YoY, ~+30% QoQ per CEO); FY26 revenue Rs 495 crore (-8%) with flat volumes. Q4 EBITDA margin up ~1,300 bps YoY on March resin price spike and inventory revaluation; FY26 margin up 280 bps. CPVC ~39-40% of mix, uPVC/SWR/pressure pipes the rest; Q4 volume growth about 2-3%.

segments.commentary: Revenue down 9% YoY in euro terms in Q4 and 7% for FY26; operating loss Rs 35 crore in Q4 including Rs 19 crore severance. Management expects gradual recovery through FY27 from retail reboot and premium Engineered Wood range.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is applying external advisers' recommended actions at Parador, some visible and some not, and acts on data and order books rather than hope; no specific exit decision was disclosed.

509820|2026-03.headline: Huhtamaki India Q1 FY26 EBITDA up 24.8% YoY on mix and efficiency; sales up only ~10 bps, EBIT hit by INR 88 mn prior-period depreciation charge.
509820|2026-03.overview: Management reported sales broadly flat (up about 10 bps YoY) with EBITDA up 24.8% YoY, attributed to higher-value sales mix and operational efficiency. Reported EBIT was about INR 386 mn after a one-off INR 88 mn depreciation charge for prior two years (WDV instead of SLM error), with EBIT margin ex-charge at about 8% (27.8% EBIT margin ex-charge is stated in the call and appears to be an inconsistent figure relative to the 8% quoted). Reported PAT of about INR 256 crore was roughly 2% lower YoY; management said it rose about 23.1% excluding the prior-year charge. Raw material costs rose sharply from end-March on the Middle East conflict; management said most of the increase was passed through to customers, with low-to-medium double-digit RM impact.

financial_highlights.value: ~8% (sequential trend chart, excl. prior-period item); management also cited 27.8% ex-exceptional
financial_highlights.change: ~170 bps higher than Q1 last year on the 8% basis
~2% lower YoY; up ~23.1% excluding prior-year charge

financial_highlights.metric: Interest on income tax refund (other income)
financial_highlights.change: Other income roughly doubled YoY per analyst

financial_highlights.value: INR 106 crore vs INR 95 crore prior quarter
financial_highlights.change: QoQ increase; management said not substantial

segments.name: Flexible packaging (sole reported business)
segments.commentary: Growth focused on selected customers and higher-value categories (innovation, premiumisation, sustainability). Management said it is deliberately not participating in some low-value segments, which limits volume growth.

guidance_outlook: Management said raw-material cost increases are being passed through, so margin impact is expected to be minimal; top-line should rise mechanically from pass-through, barring market changes.
Management said the impact will be more visible in Q2 FY26 results, due end-July 2026.
No numerical guidance on growth or margins was given; management said it cannot disclose exact figures.
Solar captive power project at Khopoli is signed and in execution; expected to go live in the next few months, with benefits from H2.
Demand growth expected in line with industry norms: large FMCG customers 2-5%, smaller regional customers faster; industry growth cited at 6-7% per year by management.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation not disclosed; management said capacity is not a constraint and there is 'a lot of room to grow'.
Solar captive electricity project at Khopoli plant under execution, expected to go live within months.
Solvent consumption reduction: capital spent on solvent cooling and other equipment; all plants reducing solvent use.
Zero liquid discharge status at Khopoli, Rudrapur and Silvassa; plans to extend to other plants.
Property in Daman put up for sale after curtailing operations there.
demand_pricing: Raw material costs (films, paper) rose from end-March 2026 with volatility; management estimated low-to-medium double-digit RM impact on products overall, and said availability is not an issue.
Pricing: India was among the first regions to pass through costs; by end-March almost all future orders were locked at new prices, with contracts allowing pass-through.
Customers came with panic-driven volume requests during the conflict; management said demand has since stabilised with no significant change.
Competition: large multinational customers grow slowly; smaller regional Indian players grow faster. Management said it is not chasing low-value volume.
Analyst cited annual report reference to Indian flexible packaging growing 10-12%; management said the comparison is not like-for-like because the definition includes paper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact post-war and is availability an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose from end-March and are volatile; low-to-medium double-digit RM impact overall. Availability is not an issue given global procurement, though shipments from overseas can be delayed. Most costs passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments are seeing demand post-war and how is cost affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers initially over-ordered in panic, then volumes stabilised. No significant demand change; large FMCG customers grow 2-5%, regional customers faster.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing share given the 10-12% market growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market includes multinationals and smaller regional Indian players growing faster; the company is selective and focused on innovation and premium customers, so growth is in line with its value proposition. Amit Gupta said the market definition includes paper and is not comparable.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the jump in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest on an income tax refund (about INR 6.5 crore), higher FD interest, and FX gains on exports from rupee weakness. Management said several one-offs offset this.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in other expenses from INR 95 crore to INR 106 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is not substantial, expense ratios are declining as a percentage of sales, and the one-offs include provision reversals and the INR 88 mn depreciation charge plus a property charge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 100 crore ECB repayment to the parent extended from Feb 2026 to June 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: The ECB loan from the parent follows RBI tenure guidelines; part has been repaid and the balance is payable by June 2027. Servicing cost is linked to FD returns, so no negative impact, per management.

risks_watch: Q2 FY26 margin impact of raw material pass-through lag and volatility in RM prices, given the Middle East conflict.
Whether the INR 88 mn prior-period depreciation error is contained, and whether any further prior-period adjustments emerge.
Rising other expenses QoQ (INR 106 crore vs INR 95 crore) and reliance on non-operating income (interest and FX gains) in reported profit.
Volume growth weakness versus industry, as the company deprioritises lower-value customers.
Balance sheet: INR 100 crore parent ECB repayment deferred to June 2027; Daman property sale.
509820|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins and pass-through execution, but evasive on quantitative items such as capacity utilisation, RM cost percentages and the other-expense increase, citing competitive sensitivity. New CFO Amit Gupta was more cautious in answering questions on drivers.
key_quotes: We are going after higher-value business, which is also consistent with our strategy and our strength in terms of the innovation leader in the industry.
We did an excellent job where we passed on most of these costs to our customers.
So capacity is not a constraint at the moment.
We have corrected the books of accounts, both from a P&L and the balance sheet standpoint and all the reflections in the P&L are coming correct starting from January 2026.

rows.why: No numerical guidance was given, and management said it cannot disclose exact figures; flat YoY sales and deliberate exits from low-value business give no basis for an upgrade.

rows.why: The Daman property has been put up for sale after operations were curtailed, but no price or timing was disclosed.

509820|2026-06.headline: Huhtamaki India Q2 CY26 net sales rose 23.1% to INR723 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.3%, with PBT up 77%.
509820|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q2 net sales of INR723 crore, up about 23% YoY, with growth split roughly evenly across price, volume and product mix and broad-based across exports and domestic. EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% from 8.3%, and PBT rose 77% to INR559 crore, with EPS up about 77%. H1 sales grew close to 12% and H1 EBIT margin was hit by a one-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge; excluding it, EBIT margin was 7.6%. Management attributed the quarter to pricing pass-through of Middle East-driven raw material inflation, a healthy portfolio mix and productivity, plus some customer inventory build-up that it said would partly reverse.

financial_highlights.value: Growth of ~77.3% YoY (absolute value not stated)

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew at roughly the same rate as domestic in Q2; exports are about 30% of sales volume. Management said duty-related challenges are stabilising.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic growth was almost identical to exports at about 23%; volume growth in liquid and home care categories was highlighted.

segments.name: Blueloop (mono-material sustainable packaging)
segments.commentary: Blueloop share of output is below 30% of material volume, up from the prior quarter; the balance of blueloop asset output (>70%) is used for products previously outsourced.

guidance_outlook: No numeric guidance given; management declined to commit to a quarterly EBITDA margin (said it could be 8%, 10% or 15%).
Management would not commit to INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate; said it depends on pass-through (single-digit), product mix and customer growth.
Volume growth expected to track market growth (about 4-5%); management said 23% growth should not be expected every quarter.
Festive season expected to support demand in coming months; inventory build-up at customers to be clearer by Q3 CY26 call.
Solar captive plant expected to come online in Q3 and supply ~50% of power for Khopoli plant.
capex_capacity: Volume growth was high single-digit (just short of double digit per management); exact capacity utilisation not disclosed on competitive grounds.
Productivity improvement programme over last 3-4 quarters is said to free capacity enough for growth; management sees no capacity constraint for at least a couple of years.
Modernisation and productivity capex funded from cash on balance sheet; no specific capex amount disclosed.
Solar captive power plant at Khopoli to be commissioned in Q3 CY26, supplying ~50% of Khopoli plant power.
Zero liquid discharge maintained; Taloja implemented mechanical vapour recompression water recycling.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q2 described as high single-digit; price, volume and mix each contributed roughly one-third of the 23% sales growth.
Raw material cost pass-through is contract-dependent (quarterly or monthly indexation, or ad hoc); management says most price changes occurred in Q2 and the process is 'never a done story'.
Customers valued supply reliability and contingency during the Middle East crisis; management said this drove share-of-wallet gains with same customer base.
Customer inventory build-up in anticipation of price increases is a tailwind; quantum not known to management.
Home care and liquid categories growing faster than food and beverage in India; late monsoon boosted beverage season.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q2 volume growth and export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was high single-digit, just short of double digit; exports and domestic grew at almost identical rates of about 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing volume growth again after sacrificing volume for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not moved away from profitable growth; product mix and customer base have largely settled and the focus is share-of-wallet and innovation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; INR750 crore includes single-digit price pass-through, and outcome depends on product mix and customer growth. It could be INR650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and receivables trend (inventory and receivables roughly doubled; receivables ~50% of six-month turnover)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute values are higher due to price increases and higher volume; DSO and DIO are stable, and there are no realisation or ageing challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for acquisitions or monetising land such as Daman?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific non-organic plans disclosed; cash is directed to modernisation and capex. Thane land sale was completed a couple of years ago; other land monetisation will be disclosed in annual reports if it happens.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth rate be sustainable into next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to track market growth (around 3-5%) rather than repeat 23% every quarter.

risks_watch: Customer inventory build-up may reverse, reducing volumes in coming quarters; management will update in Q3.
Raw material volatility from the Middle East crisis; pass-through lags and inventory cost effects on margins.
Working capital: inventory and receivables rose in absolute terms; DIO and DSO said to be stable, to watch next quarter.
Export duty and import tariff regulation uncertainty affecting export growth.
One-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge in Q1 affecting reported EBIT; the Q2 and H1 comparison base.

Several answers on inventory build-up, pricing sustainability and acquisitions were deferred to the Q3 call or left undisclosed.

rows.why: No new product or brand launches were discussed; Blueloop share is below 30% of material volume and growing but no launch date was given.

rows.why: Inventory and receivables roughly doubled in absolute terms (receivables about 50% of six-month turnover), with DSO and DIO said to be stable and to be watched next quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 profitable growth and share-of-wallet gains but cautious on forward numbers, declining to quantify margin, the INR750 crore run-rate or volume beyond market growth; analysts pushed on pricing sustainability, inventory build-up and receivables.

509930|2026-03.headline: FY26 volume rose about 12% to 753,907 MT while consolidated PAT fell 1% to Rs 954 crore; FY27 volume guided at 12-13%.
509930|2026-03.overview: Supreme Industries reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 11,218 crore (up 7%) on volume growth of about 12%, with consolidated operating profit up 7% to Rs 1,654 crore and PAT down 1% to Rs 954 crore. Plastic piping volumes grew 14% while industrial products degrew 1% in volume and 3% in value. Management said the industry's plastic piping volume declined 9% in FY26 and guided FY27 piping volume growth of 15-17%, with overall growth of 12-13% and margins of 14-14.5%. PVC resin prices swung sharply in March (up about Rs 32-37/kg) and then fell about Rs 34/kg between 5 and 21 April, which management said was now corrected. Capex of about Rs 1,000 crore is planned, adding about 1.10 lakh MT of capacity to reach about 1.35 million MT per annum.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook for piping and overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Piping volume growth of 15-17% and overall volume growth of 12-13%, with margins of 14-14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in Q4 or Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No inventory gain for full FY26; Q4 net inventory gain around Rs 70-80 crore; no gain expected in Q1 as PVC prices are falling.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 1.10 lakh MT capacity addition is in piping?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1,00,000 MT in piping and 10,000 MT in material handling systems, all to be added by FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses stay flat in Q4 despite higher volume?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there was no one-off; repairs and advertising were controlled from Q3, and FY26 publicity spend was Rs 98 crore versus Rs 125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise sharply in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said assets capitalised from prior-year capital work in progress of more than Rs 400 crore; closing CWIP is Rs 136 crore; total FY26 asset additions Rs 1,400 crore including Wavin.

qa_highlights.question: Is government spending on Nal Se Jal or Jal Jeevan picking up?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; management said central funds depend on state matching contributions, and only about one-third of budgeted spend was achieved in the last two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin and how is it defined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management's stated criterion is return on average capital employed above 25%, which it says has been achieved for 18 years; it sees 14-14.5% margins as delivering that.

509930|2026-06.headline: Supreme Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% to INR2,718 crore on 14% volume decline, with standalone PAT up 17% to INR208 crore; FY27 guidance held.
509930|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volumes fell about 14% to 1,57,536 tons, but revenue grew 4% to INR2,718 crore as value-added products rose 22% to INR1,142 crore. Standalone operating profit rose 25% to INR398 crore and PAT rose 17% to INR208 crore, helped by lower-margin agri pipe volumes falling sharply. Management attributed the weakness to April 2026 polymer price volatility and channel destocking, and said volumes recovered in May-July. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 12-13% overall volume growth, 15-17% piping volume growth and 14-14.5% EBITDA margin, plus about INR1,000 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see growth in the coming years and where will FY27 end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying projections are in the quarterly results. It said growth and profit will be 'very, very good' versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹365 crore order book be executed this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it is expected in FY27, with some orders closing in the following year. New large orders would be announced.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for NSE listing, promoter stake reduction and fundraising?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE listing depends on first meeting minimum public shareholding (MPS) norms, and there is time to do so. No instrument, amount or dilution has been decided and nothing is pending with the board.

qa_highlights.question: What is the green hydrogen product, its patents and when will it generate revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a solid-state hydrogen storage technology, described as a first in India. Management holds both design and technology patents. No revenue timing was confirmed, and commercialisation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kavach work and are there orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Axis is in proof-of-concept with several companies and got approval for Kavach. No Kavach orders were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins low despite about 13 granted patents?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hydrogen revenue and margins are not yet in the financials. It said one industrial engineering and systems patent is in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: MRO, AMC and warranty revenue is about 5-6% of total revenue and is expected to rise over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give utilisation or peak revenue. It said products are customised rather than batch-produced, and the facilities would not constrain the top line.

risks_watch: Revenue mix swung sharply by vertical (industrial engineering 59%, water 26%), so quarterly comparisons are noisy. Management said it is working to neutralise this.
Pre-revenue bets (hydrogen storage, Kavach, EV charging) carry execution and timing risk, and management would not commit to dates.
Receivables ageing was flagged by an analyst; management attributed it to year-end billing. Q2 debtor data should be checked.
MPS compliance (minimum public shareholding) could lead to promoter dilution or a fundraise. Holds 85.64% promoter stake, 12.62% public and 1.74% DIIs.
Tax was nil in Q1 FY26 and ₹37 lakh in Q1 FY27, so PAT growth (77%) lagged PBT growth (about 98%). Watch the effective tax rate.
Disclosure is limited: management declined to give revenue, capacity, subsidiary-level or order-level detail. The call was also marred by audio problems and unanswered questions.
511144|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, but evasive on guidance, order detail, hydrogen and Kavach commercial timing, and capacity. Management repeatedly deferred to the quarterly results or one-on-one meetings.
key_quotes: Ninad Vora: Dipenji, about the projection for the year, whatever the projection may be, you will find it in the quarterly results, because it is a compliance issue if we disclose this here.
Ninad Vora: We cannot right now declare anything confirmed right now, because we are trying for the commercialise this. Once we can confirm anything, you will receive the orders.
Ninad Vora: Till now, we have not got any order, nor have we sold any of the items in hydrogen. So, the hydrogen margins have not been added to any financials as of now.
Ninad Vora: Sir, you are going again and again to the revenue part, which we cannot disclose.
Ninad Vora: Right now, whether we have to go for NSE or not will be decided by the management, but first of all we need to comply with MPS, the minimum public shareholding requirement.

511147|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 26% to about INR111 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR6.14 crore, while Q4 growth slowed on macro and war-related travel weakness.
511147|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with revenue crossing about INR111 crore for the first time, PBT of INR8.03 crore and PAT of INR6.14 crore, and the company stated it remains debt-free. Q4 was hit by macro volatility, especially in March, from the US-Israel-Iran conflict and lower US student travel, though management said Q4 revenue still grew 22% and GTO grew 16%. Management highlighted the FEMA 401/2026 RBI circular, which expands AD-II scope to trade remittances and family maintenance and allows Forex Correspondent (FXC) appointments, and said it has recommended a 15% dividend. Management also acknowledged that rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup have taken share from forex cards in leisure travel, and that leisure market volumes contracted about 25% from March.

segments.name: Student
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver per management; overall market contracted about 20% in the year while the company gained share. Loan-funded students growing while own-funds students contracted after TCS was cut to 2%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Over 900 corporates served; management cited a 95.62% CAGR. Named clients include Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra and, recently, Adani.

segments.name: Retail / leisure
segments.commentary: Card business declined in FY26 on lower US student traffic and competition from rupee credit cards; leisure market down about 25% since March. Management described this as a calibrated, value-led push with a minimum margin per transaction.

segments.name: Prepaid cards
segments.commentary: Four products (three plastics and one digital-only, Uni-Z launched last month). Switch Card supports 30 currencies; Xplorer Metal card is by invitation. Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 to be a challenging, linear quarter with leisure travel down roughly 25% from March, and expects the next one to two months to remain tough.
Trade remittances expected to become a material business in 12 to 18 months; family maintenance (about $3 billion market) to be a growth area.
FXC network expected to expand through the model over the next 12 to 15 months, with Spice Money group network and NBFC/retail partners as possible distribution.
Trade remittance margins expected 20-30 bps, below current blended levels, as competition rises.
Target to raise digital/automated share of transactions from about 60% to 80% this year.
Management did not give numerical FY27 targets for cards or revenue; it said Q2 to Q4 are peak months and FY27 mix will change materially.
capex_capacity: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35 when the CEO took over, 16 in COVID); expansion planned mainly through FXC appointments rather than owned branches.
Company is evaluating whether to apply for a PA-CB licence.
Working on multiple payment rails for faster, holiday-enabled remittances and a student fee-remittance platform.
Smart Agent Platform, FPaaS, Smart Corporate Platform and consumer app run on a unified payments stack.
demand_pricing: Q4 traffic hit in March by the US-Israel-Iran conflict; leisure market contracted about 25% from March to May 2026 per management.
Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup and lounge perks have taken a large share of international spend (management estimate about 60%), with credit card spend outside LRS and TCS.
Management says it will not price at a loss; pricing uses interbank rates with a small card fulfilment fee on the Switch card.
B2B and corporate make up about 80-85% of business; partner commissions and referral fees are a larger share of costs.
Retail customer lifetime value is quoted at about INR1,000 of annual income per traveller versus high digital CAC.
Management expects more competition after the RBI circular, with margin pressure; trade remittances may run at 20-30 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new RBI circular affect volumes, revenue and margins over the next one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scope has expanded to trade and non-trade current account transactions, with no negative impact from the circular itself, but competition will pressure margins. Trade remittance margins are expected at 20-30 bps; current net margin is 0.6-0.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will be most affected by the new regulations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split out the impact by segment. It said the new trade and family maintenance categories open new growth areas, and that retail/leisure faces the most pressure from credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with low-priced small players on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay competitive but will not work at a loss per transaction, citing a minimum margin policy and a digital platform for each segment. It acknowledged its retail pricing may not be the lowest.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise FY26 revenue, volume, customer and new-product breakdown; agent commissions versus branch revenue; CAC; card KPIs and FY27 targets
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only broad-based answers: B2B and corporate are 80-85% of business, partner commissions are higher as a B2B company, and digital CAC is high. It declined to give specific numbers and said detailed data would be shared through the company's written channel.

qa_highlights.question: How does Scapia (bank-sponsored card) compare, and how are rupee credit cards affecting forex cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cards hold a regulatory arbitrage (no LRS or TCS), that around 60% of international spend has moved to credit cards, and that the association has represented to RBI for parity. Forex cards are positioned on rate certainty for multi-currency travel; corporate and student segments do not use credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCS cut to 2% for education remittances doing to the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2% TCS mainly hit own-fund students, while loan-funded students are growing; it called the change a relief and said zero TCS would be better for the priority-sector segment.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and payables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Pooja Mishra said the rise in current assets and liabilities reflects card-program customer wallet balances on both sides of the balance sheet. Capital turnover improved to 4.4x from 3.8x, and short-term borrowings are fixed-deposit-backed working capital lines, not structural debt.

risks_watch: Leisure and card volumes down about 25% since March; Q1 FY27 expected to be linear and challenging.
Rupee credit cards eroding forex card share in leisure; RBI parity representation is pending with no timeline.
Margin pressure from new AD-II entrants and FFMC-licensed competitors; trade remittance margins guided at 20-30 bps.
Execution risk on FXC network rollout and trade/family maintenance scope, which management said still has open clarifications.
Management was evasive on FY27 numerical targets, segment-wise volumes, card KPIs and PA-CB licence decision.
Customer service complaint raised on a Delhi branch; management promised corrective action.
511147|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the regulatory opportunity and long-term structure, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: Q1 FY27 was flagged as challenging and specific FY27 targets and segment KPIs were withheld. Management was defensive when discussing credit card competition and pricing.
key_quotes: Revenue crossed around INR111 crores for the first time. Revenue grew 26% significantly ahead of GTO growth, good business profitable mix.
We are happy to say we are increasing our market share year-on-year while the business has -- overall market has contracted by 20%.
So, from our perspective, we are clearly focused on forex cards, how to bring out the merits of the forex card and it's up to the customer's choice to take a forex card or credit card.

511196|2026-03.headline: Can Fin Homes FY26 disbursements hit INR10,531 crore, just above guidance, with Q4 a record INR3,245 crore; FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore.
511196|2026-03.overview: FY26 disbursements of INR10,531 crore marginally beat the INR10,500 crore guidance, with each quarter setting a new peak and Q4 at INR3,245 crore. AUM growth was about 10.44% as rundown ran about INR600 crore above the INR6,000 crore assumption. Karnataka grew 7% in disbursements after e-khata issues, and Telangana ended roughly flat at INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore. Q4 included two one-offs: INR46 crore additional DTA provision on standard assets and INR13.5 crore tax refund gain; management says underlying FY26 profit was INR1,027 crore, up 20% from INR857 crore. Around 85% of the book has moved to quarterly reset, with the 50 bps pass-through and a 15 bps cut in January leaving an opening yield near 9.8% and spread of about 2.8%.

financial_highlights.change: all-time quarterly high; new peak in each quarter of FY26
after 50 bps quarterly-reset pass-through and 15 bps January cut

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursement growth of 7% after e-khata delays; Q4 averaged about INR290 crore per month; FY27 target is 15% growth. Delinquency is lowest among six zones.

segments.name: Telangana
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursements INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore in FY25, roughly flat; now running INR100 crore-plus per month and expected to be positive from day one of FY27.

segments.name: North and West zones
segments.commentary: Each running about INR150-160 crore per month; North and West together grew about 40%-plus in FY26 per management.

segments.name: Tamil Nadu
segments.commentary: Running INR180-200 crore per month; growing around 30%.

segments.name: East zone (mainly Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Running close to INR100 crore per month; grew about 40%-plus in FY26 per management.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: Share rose by about 2 percentage points in FY26 as a deliberate push, mainly in Karnataka.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore, about 25% growth, applied roughly uniformly across zones.
FY27 rundown (prepayments, BT outs, closures) assumed at about INR7,000 crore, giving net book addition of about INR6,000 crore and AUM growth of about 14%.
FY27 spread guidance 2.75% and NIM guidance 3.75%, kept conservative versus opening spread of about 2.8%.
FY27 credit cost guidance 15 bps, though management expects it to be well below that.
IT programme: about INR40 crore net incremental cost in FY27 (about INR60 crore of depreciation and opex against about INR20 crore current IT cost); cost-to-income ratio to rise slightly.
FY27 ROA target about 2.4%; ROE expected at 18%-plus, slightly diluted by IT costs.
28 new branches planned for the first half of FY27 (3 in Karnataka, 2 in Telangana); sales team to grow from about 80-90 to about 150.
Employee cost expected to rise about 10%-12% in FY27; other opex from INR134 crore to INR175-180 crore.
capex_capacity: IT transformation totals INR300 crore: INR100 crore capex and INR200 crore opex spread over 5 years; depreciation begins mainly in FY27.
Infrastructure and security modules are complete; deposit applications and HRMS are live; LOS and LMS go live in Q1 FY27 and are expected to drive the next stage of efficiency gains.
Branch network grew by 54 branches over FY23-FY25; 15 branches opened in the first half of FY26 contributed INR863 crore of disbursements versus INR128 crore from earlier branches in FY25.
Sales team of about 80-90 people contributed about INR868 crore in FY26 versus INR183 crore from a team of 30-35 in FY25.
demand_pricing: Demand inquiries remain good across branches; affordable segment has slowed to mid-single-digit growth, while mid and prime segments hold up better.
About 85% of the book is now on quarterly reset (from about 48% annual-reset-to-quarterly shift in Q4); about 15% remains on annual reset and would lag if rates rise.
About 62% of liabilities are bank loans linked to repo; NCDs carry a blended cost of about 7.66%-7.67%; CP rates fell to about 6.45% in April from above 7% in Q4.

Q4 BT outs were about INR400 crore, roughly 25% of the INR1,730 crore total rundown; main competitors for BT outs are LIC Housing and Bajaj Finance, with Bajaj winning mainly on takeover-plus-top-up offers.
Incremental yield is about 9.8% or higher; salaried share of new business fell from about 89% to about 83-84% (self-employed mix rising).
PMAY/CLSS traction is limited: about INR1 lakh crore of PMAY claims across all HFCs and NBFCs in six months, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BT-out and rundown rate peaking after the April quarterly-reset shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q4 to be the peak; BT outs were about INR380-400 crore in Q3 and Q4, nearly flat, and FY27 rundown is modelled at INR7,000 crore versus about INR6,600 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will disbursements reach INR13,000 crore given branch growth of about 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are 28 new branches in H1 FY27, expanding the sales team from 80-90 to about 150, and recovery in Karnataka and Telangana; the company is also planning for elevated prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 state-wise disbursement run rates and opex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current monthly run rates: Karnataka about INR275-290 crore, Tamil Nadu INR180-200 crore, North and West INR150-160 crore each, Telangana INR110-120 crore, East about INR100 crore. Employee cost is INR177 crore and other cost INR134 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Are the West Asia situation or LAP delinquencies showing stress, and is any management overlay planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No stress seen in bounce rates or delinquencies through March and April; no additional management overlay planned, but PCR rose from 49% to 56%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and margins after the reset and NHB repricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is expected at about 2.8%, with guidance kept at 2.75%; the only risk is a rate rise, which would affect the roughly 15% of the book still on annual reset.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company losing prepayments to LIC Housing and Bajaj?
qa_highlights.answer: LIC wins on price, offering rates such as 7.15% on new business; Bajaj wins on takeover-plus-top-up, where Can Fin is more conservative on LTV.

risks_watch: Rate-up cycle: about 15% of the book on annual reset would lag repricing, while about 62% of liabilities reprice quickly.
Prepayment pressure from LIC Housing and Bajaj; rundown assumed at INR7,000 crore, and a higher rundown would cut the 14% AUM growth outlook.
Affordable segment demand slowdown, which management acknowledged.
LOS and LMS go-live in Q1 FY27 and the IT cost ramp (about INR40 crore net) could weigh on cost-to-income ratio.
Karnataka e-khata rollout in gram panchayat rural areas is still delayed; Telangana needs to sustain INR100 crore-plus monthly run rate.
Borrowing cost trajectory: NCD refinancing at lower rates and NHB tranche repricing are expected benefits but not yet visible.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,650 crores, up 28% YoY; accounted for about 63% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Non-housing / LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 958 crores, up 32% YoY; about 37% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Self-employed (SENP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 44% YoY; current NPA around 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% in salaried, per management.

segments.name: Karnataka / Telangana
segments.commentary: All six zones grew; Karnataka grew 18% YoY (lowest zone), Telangana slightly higher. IT-sector exposure about 6% of customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crores with 14% AUM growth; management may push to INR 13,200-13,400 crores if needed to offset higher rundown.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target INR 3,000 crores; quarterly path then steps up to INR 3,500 crores and INR 4,000 crores in Q3 and Q4 per prior plan.
NIM to be maintained at 3.81% plus; Q2 incremental bank borrowing at 7.25-7.5% expected to add only marginal cost, on new loans only.
Credit cost guided at 10 bps for FY27; management sees no challenge to this.
Cost-to-income ratio around 19.5% for FY27, trending back toward 18% over about three years.
Remaining 245 branches to move to new IT platform by end of Q2, in tranches at month-end (July, August, September); update expected around September.
Opex: about INR 40 crores of further IT-related costs yet to come; no other major surprises expected.
capex_capacity: New LOS/LMS/report-generation platform live in 5 pilot branches from 8 July 2026, with sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS collections and closures processed.
Rollout to remaining 245 branches (250 total) planned within Q2 FY27, migrating month-end data in tranches.
Management expects about six months for new branches to stabilise on the new system; staffing benefits expected this year with sales additions from existing headcount.
APF (apartment finance) approvals up to 331 projects; per-project exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.
demand_pricing: No demand slowdown seen across geographies; partner banks willing to sanction, including a couple of large sanctions.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and blended yield by segment; are there trade-offs by ticket size?

qa_highlights.question: Housing vs non-housing and salaried vs self-employed growth; number of loans; run-rate going forward?

qa_highlights.question: Is the IT-sector hiring slowdown in Bangalore affecting home loan offtake or policy?

qa_highlights.question: Any opex surprises in FY27 and how far is APF exposure per project capped?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the book rundown elevated for four quarters, and is the 4% level the new normal? Also, how does the best-rate gap to banks affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crore (vs INR 976 crore) drove the rundown, as borrowers under change-in-tenure kept EMIs constant and paid down principal. BT-outs were INR 408 crore (vs INR 400 crore), and other closures INR 377 crore (vs INR 360 crore). Best rate gap widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps; management is exploring deposit conversion and bureau alerts for retention.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROA of about 2.4% and ROE of about 18% be achieved in FY27 given higher opex and the soft Q1?

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Does a rising rate cycle affect home loan demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 25-50 bps move is a non-event for demand because EMI impact is limited on 15-year tenors. Rates of 7.15-8% are among the lowest seen, so customer behaviour is not expected to change much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk to FY27 disbursement target from the South monsoon or drought, and to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early to assess; drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, but the company lends mainly in Tier 1-2 areas. If industry slows, it could hit disbursement, and it may use LAP or construction top-ups as short-term levers.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational efficiency from Project Tejas play out in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited manual processes now automated, native AI features, auto form filling, and a digital sourcing channel expected to reach about 10% of business. Sales headcount to rise from about 90 to 150 this year without adding branch staff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate pass-through and prepayment outlook after the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing rates rose 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 against a 25 bps repo hike, which translates to about 12-13 bps on the book. Management said a 100 bps rise could cut the rate gap by about 60 bps and reduce prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How reset timing works for bank borrowings and the loan book, and whether spread is at risk in a rising cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo-linked bank borrowings reprice from 1 November; T-bill-linked ones reset quarterly. About 87% of the floating book is on quarterly reset and 12-13% on annual, with roughly one-third repricing each on 1 November, 1 December and 1 January. Management said it will pass on hikes to protect spread and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in the H2 disbursement ramp (about INR3,500 crore per quarter) and the FY28 AUM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was INR2,600 crore against a planned INR2,500 crore, so the INR100 crore buffer was used; Q3 target is INR3,500 crore with about INR400 crore shortfall recovered in Q4. FY28 disbursement target of INR16,000 crore implies AUM growth of about 15-15.5%, with 15% described as a resultant figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity ramp for new branches and the pipeline status?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches take about 18 months (range 18-24) to reach 5 cases per staff per month. Management said sanctioned-but-not-disbursed rose about INR118 crore quarter on quarter, and that some pipeline was lost during the migration.

We will be looking at a 20% plus growth in terms of the disbursement, which consequently should become a 13%- 14% AUM growth this year and a 15% plus AUM growth in the next year.
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected.

511218|2026-09.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 59.37% YoY to INR3,677.03 crores, with NIM at 9.52% and gross Stage 3 at 4.65%.
511218|2026-09.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q2 FY27 earnings, with disbursements up 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crores and AUM up 16.96% YoY to INR3,29,021.72 crores. segments.commentary: Liability mix is public deposits 31%, NCDs 15.71%, ECB and bonds 16.5%, bank and institutional borrowing 21%, and securitisation 14%, out of total liabilities of INR2,36,271 crores. Gold loan target is unchanged: double the gold book in three years, from about 2.5% to about 5% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM and cost of funds evolve?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AUM growth guidance lower, and are credit filters being tightened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided to 15-17% because of the West Asia war and weak monsoon, and said credit filters are unchanged unless the economy slows. qa_highlights.question: Are gold loan stress levels a sign of industry-level problems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is mainly from the new EMI and interest-servicing gold products, where customers used to bullet repayment are paying late, and it sees no industry-level challenge. The gold growth plan is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong April CV and PV data from OEMs reflected on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said April sales, credit and collections were very strong versus April 2025, and it has seen no change in customer behaviour.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CSEL growth, opex and ROA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CSEL pre-tax ROA is expected to exceed 3% this year from Q4 ROA of 2.3%. Q4 opex included a one-time CGTMSE cost (about 6% of the segment's opex), and the opex ratio should normalise to about 4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business loan book is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of unsecured assets are covered and this may rise to 80-82%. Only the business loan book is in CGTMSE, at about INR3,000-3,500 crore (about 80% of a roughly INR5,000 crore BL book); Q4 CGTMSE cost was about INR38 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Did the overlay change PD-LGD assumptions, and why is NIM up 50 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: No PD-LGD change was made; the overlay was set using COVID and diesel-price experience. The NIM jump relates to ARC receipts recognised as income, offset by higher credit losses, leaving ROTA largely unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital-raising policy and gearing guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raising would be evaluated if Tier 1 approaches 13%. Growth below 23-25% is expected to be funded from internal accruals. Gearing fell from 7.17x to 6.94x.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and fuel-price pressure on HCV long-haul operators; management says HCVs are only 5-7% of Vehicle Finance AUM.
Gold loan build-out (about 360 branches) adds cost and needs experienced staff; operating leverage deferred about a year.
Home loan disbursements stuck around INR1,800-2,000 crore a quarter; the southern-state election delays may persist.
Fintech run-down book of INR300-400 crore has a long tail through the year.
Cost of funds may rise marginally in FY27, offsetting newer-business yield gains.
Rating upgrade from AA+ is under discussion with agencies; ICRA has a positive outlook.

511243|2026-06.headline: Chola Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR29,612 crore and AUM 23% to INR2,54,392 crore, with net credit cost down to 1.5% from 1.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and vehicle finance Stage 3 rise YoY?

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook and rate hike assumption?

qa_highlights.question: Can PBT-ROTA exceed 3.5% by Q4 FY27?

511742|2026-03.headline: UGRO Capital says Q4 FY26 net total income rose 51% YoY to a figure not stated in the call, with GNPA at 2.5%, cost of borrowings at 10.16%, and FY27 opex guided to INR 490-500 crores.
511742|2026-03.overview: UGRO Capital's first full quarter of its February 2026 structural realignment saw AUM broadly flat QoQ as the non-focus intermediated (DSA-led Prime) book runs down and focus verticals (EM-LAP and embedded finance) grow; focus share rose from 33% to 38% of AUM. Net total income grew 51% YoY and 34% QoQ, and PAT grew 26% YoY, after a one-time restructuring cost of about INR 25 crores. Management reiterated five FY29 commitments (85% focus-vertical AUM, INR 220 crore cost takeout, 15-20% annual Prime run-down, no new equity, ROA of 3-3.5%), and said FY27 is a transition year with only marginal ROA improvement. Q&A focused on growth outlook, co-lending exit, embedded-finance credit quality and the Profectus acquisition economics. Note: the call's Q4 net total income level and total PAT were not stated in the transcript.

segments.commentary: Secured portfolio including machinery loans about 67% of total AUM with GNPA ~1.5%; unsecured (embedded plus business loans) capped at 30-35% of portfolio per management.

Credit cost expected in the zone of just under 2%, not more.

Full-year impairment was INR76 crore versus INR18-18.5 crore in FY25, and cost-to-income is about 85% for now, with management guiding 70-75% for the full year. Management confirmed a DA transaction of about INR100 crore with Hinduja, and cost of funds fell to 9.48% in Q4 from 10.09% in Q3. Questions focused on the lack of profitability and dividends, the NPA trajectory, and the lack of disbursement growth; management pointed to a 2-wheeler-funded cost base, and a shift away from co-lending.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said AUM grew from about INR2,000 crore to INR3,500 crore and cited higher opex from new verticals and digital spend; CFO said FY26 impairment was INR76 crore versus INR18-18.5 crore in FY25, and gave no FY27 profit number, only a pre-tax ROA target of 2.0-2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked if the board would consider new leadership given five to six quarters of weak performance and net NPA above 4% with about 50% PCR.

511766|2026-06.headline: Muthoot Capital Q1 FY27: GNPA fell to 3.94% (down ~182 bps YoY) after a ₹203 crore ARC sale; PAT near ₹8 crore.
511766|2026-06.overview: Management highlighted a CRISIL upgrade to AA minus stable, public deposits crossing ₹100 crore, and a sharp GNPA decline driven by a third ARC sale of ₹203 crore at about 45.6% valuation. Co-lending was wound down to ₹499 crore from roughly ₹1,000 crore a year earlier, with retail AUM rising to ₹2,851 crore. Q1 disbursements were ₹564 crore consolidated (₹535 crore standalone), with PAT near ₹8 crore and PBT near ₹11 crore. Management kept the ₹4,000-4,200 crore FY27 AUM target and ₹10,000 crore FY28-29 ambition, while acknowledging a 2.5% pre-tax ROA target is still far from the current ~1%.

segments.commentary: Still the largest book, with a stated blended yield of 22% and GNPA around 3.5%; the portfolio is shrinking after excluding DA and ARC sales, down ~1% YoY on a stable basis. 2-wheeler industry grew 14% in Q1, against MCSL's 6%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target of ₹4,000-4,200 crore reiterated; Q3 (festive season) expected to be the biggest quarter, with disbursements scaled up from end-Q2.
Long-term target of ₹10,000 crore AUM for FY28-29 reiterated; FY28 AUM growth implied at about 150% if FY27 reaches ₹4,000-4,500 crore (analyst's framing, not confirmed by management).
Pre-tax ROA target of about 2.5% for FY27; current pre-tax ROA around 1%; management says impairment cost is not expected to rise much further this year.
Retail GNPA guided below 4% and NNPA below 2% through FY27, with no change to ECL policy or 50% PCR.
Further ₹0.40-0.50 reduction in borrowing cost expected after the CRISIL upgrade; ECL model revision due in about four weeks, with a possible LGD cut from ~50% to 40-42% held back as buffer.
capex_capacity: Approval rate deliberately held at 35-40% of logged cases vs industry 75-80%; management plans to scale disbursements from end-Q2 once an in-house scorecard is live.
Average productivity in car and CV rose to ₹20 lakh+ from ₹13-14 lakh last year, with a target of ₹30-35 lakh.

Branch activation: 25-30% of Muthoot FinCorp's 4,000+ branches generate at least one vehicle loan a month; target 50-60% by year-end. Group entities contribute 15-20% of incremental sourcing, targeted at 40%.
Tech: AI bots handle the entire X-bucket collection, with 55% resolution in the month; QR-code on-spot approvals at dealerships.
Equity raise: 2-3 investors in talks, with meetings expected in Q2; the company is comfortable with leverage up to 6x debt-to-equity.
demand_pricing: Q1 disbursement growth was held back by deliberately low approvals and the wind-down of co-lending, which fell from ~₹120 crore in Q1 FY26 to ₹20 crore in April 2026.
Pricing is moving to risk-based, reviewed weekly with an in-house scorecard in place of quarterly vendor reviews.
Management says competitors in its Tier 2-3 markets price in a similar range, so NII pressure is not expected near term.
ARC pricing: ARC-3 valued at a blended 45.61% (SR investment ~₹81 crore), versus 50-55% in the earlier two ARC deals.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 2-wheeler and retail book be repositioned in FY27-28 to defend margins amid rising funding costs and fintech competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is diversifying into CV, CE and car, which carry lower GNPA (sub-0.5% on existing book), is cutting funding costs through the rating upgrade, and is moving to risk-based pricing with an in-house scorecard. Liability franchise is said to cost about 150 bps less than the average borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARC transaction details and how do they compare with prior ARC deals?
qa_highlights.answer: The third ARC covered ₹203 crore (₹83 crore write-off pool plus a 600+ DPD GNPA pool of ~₹120 crore) at a blended 46.51% valuation. The first ARC (Sept 2023, ₹235 crore pool) has recovered 75% of its SR; the second (Sept 2024, ~₹100 crore) has recovered 46.71%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the accounting impact of the ARC sale on profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹83 crore write-off pool was fully impaired in prior years. Recoveries of ₹14 crore so far are recognised in this year's P&L with no gain on the sale; 85% of the ₹14 crore is held as SR investment, and the ~₹120 crore pool sold for ₹78 crore against a ₹59 crore provision and ₹60.34 crore book value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 AUM targets, and how is the ₹10,000 crore goal progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 AUM target of ₹4,000-4,200 crore is intact; ₹10,000 crore is still the goal for FY28-29. Two-wheeler is to fall to about 30% of the book over three to four years, with car, CV, CE and tractors making up 70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA outlook for the used car book, given its 18.6% yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Used car is expected to reach about 1-1.5% ROA, with breakeven targeted in FY27. Impairment cost is about 0.5% against 2-2.5% for two-wheeler, and opex is to fall from 6-6.5% to about 4% of AUM as productivity rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the group-channel ROA and how is group sourcing performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Group entities contribute 15-20% of incremental sourcing, targeted at 40%. Management says group-sourced business carries lower acquisition costs and somewhat higher ROA than the dealer channel but did not share numbers on this call.

risks_watch: Fresh equity raise is still pending, with meetings expected in Q2 and leverage at 4.88x.
The ECL model revision is due in about four weeks; a possible LGD cut could release provisions but is being held in reserve.
Two-wheeler borrowing mix and rising cost of funds could pressure margins if the rating-driven cost reduction slows.
Retail GNPA of 3.49% excludes one corporate loan; the 3.94% total GNPA depends on that account's recovery through a property sale in 6-8 months.
Management flagged macroeconomic risks (including war) to the FY28-29 AUM target, and the company has not disclosed an ROA plan beyond FY27.
Credit acceptance rates of 35-40% limit growth until the new scorecard is in use.
